jobs.ashbyhq.com/duffel/4eac1fa4-85ca-40.description_excerpt:
Software Engineer London | Full-time | Hybrid | Shoreditch/Liverpool Street
Create the Future of Travel With Us
Whether it's visiting the people closest to us, starting an exciting adventure, or a career-defining business trip, travel is essential.
Yet we've all experienced the aches and pains of getting to our destination.
More than 4 billion airline passengers rely on technology that hasn't kept up with modern expectations. That's why we're rebuilding the infrastructure that underpins the travel industry - simplifying systems and building tools that will make the future of travel effortless.
We were part of Y Combinator S18's cohort and we're backed by Benchmark, Blossom, Index Ventures, and Kima Ventures - a fantastic set of investors that has helped build some of the world's largest companies.
Our London team is growing, and we're looking for talented people to join us on our journey.
Engineering at Duffel
We're building tools to simplify travel distribution, search, and booking through one seamless API. The technical challenge? Design a beautiful API, then integrate it with hundreds of travel providers - each with different systems and requirements - whilst delivering a fantastic developer experience.
We work with Elixir, Phoenix, Kubernetes, and Google Cloud Platform, but we value strong engineering fundamentals over specific tech experience.
You'll Thrive Here If:
✅ You're passionate about designing beautiful APIs and creating great developer experiences
✅ You have a high bar for code quality and API design
✅ You have opinions on good engineering standards and processes as we define ours at Duffel
✅ You think big picture - making tradeoffs between technical work and business impact
✅ You communicate clearly, articulating what you're working on and why in a structured way
✅ You thrive collaboratively - you believe in your methods but stay open to feedback and suggestions
Bonus: Experience in travel, flights, hotels, or cars
What You'll Get:
💰 Competitive salary + equity (you'll own part of Duffel)
🏝️ Work from anywhere policy
🛩️ Duffel travel allowance (use what we build)
🍼 Matched parental leave
🧘‍♂️ Sabbatical programme (3 months full pay)
🪩 Office in Shoreditch + regular team socials
Why Now Matters
You'll work on the core API powering millions of travel bookings. Early-stage role = outsized impact on how we build and scale.

Our Payments team looks after the infrastructure that powers our travel operations: payment acceptance, supplier settlement, reconciliation, commission tracking and payouts, billing, and more. These are some of the hardest and most interesting challenges Duffel is facing as we operate as a global travel platform.
About the role
As the Product Manager for Payments, you'll own the roadmap for the operational backbone of our Payments product. The role is largely internal. You'll work closely with Finance, Engineering, and Operations to optimise settlement, billing, commissions and reconciliation, and to build the platform services that other Duffel teams, and eventually external partners, rely on. There's a customer-facing dimension too, but the bulk of the work is making the inside of the product as well-engineered as the outside.
You'll spend most of your time with engineering, define the weekly goals and milestones for the product squad, work closely with internal stakeholders (Finance especially), and bring real depth to a team that values getting the detail right. You'll own the overall Payments roadmap, to shape where your areas go next, including parts of the product we've barely touched yet.
What we're looking for
- You're fluent in payments without being wedded to the rails. You understand how money moves (settlement, reconciliation, commissions, FX, chargebacks) but you're more energised by building great internal product on top of that than by optimising payment rails for their own sake.
- You're a builder. Most of what this team needs, we build rather than buy. You like designing the systems, automated commission flows, supplier reconciliation, billing, that Finance, Operations and eventually external partners rely on.
- You translate between worlds. A big part of this job is sitting between Finance and Engineering: turning finance narratives into technical requirements, technical realities into language Finance and Ops can act on, and getting both sides to genuinely understand each other.
- You prioritise ruthlessly. This is a small, in-demand team (three engineers) constantly trading internal needs against customer-facing work. You're good at deciding what matters now and saying no to the rest.
- You sweat the detail. Reconciliation logic, commission edge cases, audit trails: this is the kind of work that energises you rather than drains you.
- You shape product direction. You can take a roadmap area, work out where it should go and why, and drive it.
- You've got commercial instinct. You can spot when something we've built for ourselves (like reconciliation) could become a product customers would pay for.
- You're API-literate. You don't need to write code, but you can have a meaningful conversation with engineering about how systems actually work.
- You handle ambiguity, breaking complex, undefined problems into a clear way forward, and use both quantitative and qualitative analysis to back your calls.
- You think being challenged on your assumptions makes you better, and that challenging others helps them grow.
- Nice to have: exposure to travel-specific payments (BSP, IATA, virtual cards, agency settlement). Useful, not essential.
Some reasons why you’ll love working here:
🏡 Work From Anywhere - work abroad for part of the year
🛩️ Duffel Travel Allowance - because building in travel should come with travel perks
🍼 Enhanced parental leave
🧘 Sabbatical options - proper time to recharge
🪩 A Shoreditch office near Liverpool Street + regular team socials
💰 Competitive salary + potential equity

This role sits at the intersection of AI, product, and full-stack engineering: you will take ideas from prototype all the way to stable, observable features in production.

- Build and maintain the surrounding infrastructure: data pipelines, evaluation harnesses, prompt and model management, observability, and safety/guardrails.
- Work across the stack—from backend integrations and APIs to simple UI hooks—to deliver complete AI features, not just model endpoints.
- Partner with product and customers to identify high-value workflows, run experiments, and iterate quickly based on usage.
ABOUT YOU
- 3+ years developing production software, including designing, testing, and operating services at scale in a cloud environment.
- Hands-on experience with modern LLM providers and tooling (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic, Hugging Face, vector stores, RAG patterns).
- Familiarity with prompt design, retrieval-augmented systems, evaluation methods, and safety/guardrail approaches.
- Ability to reason about tradeoffs between different models, architectures, and deployment patterns and make pragmatic decisions.
- Comfortable working in a high-ownership, fast-paced environment where experiments and iteration are the norm.
OUR STACK (AI-LEANING)
- TypeScript/Node.js and Python for AI and backend services.
- Modern LLM APIs and orchestration libraries for building agentic workflows.
- Postgres and other managed cloud services for data and state.
HOW WE WORK & VALUES
- Speed over everything: prototype AI workflows quickly, then harden what works.
- Own, downscope, ship, iterate: one clear owner per feature, from prototype to production.
- Fundamentals done well: evaluation, observability, and safety are part of the first version, not an afterthought.
- Competitive salary and meaningful equity.
- Health, dental, and vision coverage.
- Flexible time off and support for experimentation, learning, and staying current with the AI ecosystem.

jobs.ashbyhq.com/firstwork/27eba85a-56da.description_excerpt:
FirstWork is a forward-deployed applied-AI company for frontline hiring, the largest and most heavily regulated labour market in the world. One platform carries a worker from application through onboarding, compliance verification, training and payroll, for enterprise customers across 40+ countries and a dozen-plus languages. Our AI agents run that work rather than assisting someone who still does it: document agents validate credentials against policy, browsing agents operate government portals that have no API, and voice agents screen and follow up with candidates.
The scale is live, at roughly 50,000 new applicants a week and 2.5 million API requests a day. We bill on usage, per document validated and per agent action executed, so throughput and cost show up directly in revenue.
We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to own a product line, the platform primitives beneath it, and the AI capabilities that run on top.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
- Own the strategy, roadmap and commercial shape for a product line or platform portfolio.
- Integrate LLMs and agentic AI deeper into the product architecture.
- Innovate and enhance product capabilities, from new feature development to improving the maturity, accuracy and performance of existing features.
- Build new product lines from zero, taking a validated use case to a general, multi-tenant product.
- Decide which capabilities are assistive and which are autonomous, and set the evidence standard each must meet before acting without human review.
- Draw the boundary between deterministic, auditable rules and model-based judgement.
- Decide what becomes a shared platform primitive, what stays customer configuration, and what we decline to build.
- Own accuracy and evaluation infrastructure across the portfolio, including regression detection during scale-up.
- Own packaging, pricing and unit economics, including model cost and margin.
- Own the audit, evidence and explainability layer that operators and auditors depend on.
- Hire and coach product managers, and set the standard for specifications, decision records and design review.
- Represent the product in enterprise procurement, security review and AI governance discussions.
WHAT WE LOOK FOR
- 8+ years of product management experience, including senior ownership of a platform or multi-product portfolio in B2B or enterprise software.
- Experience platformising a complex workflow product: extracting primitives, exposing them as configuration, and moving a second segment or vertical onto them without forking.
- Production experience with LLM or agentic systems, including ownership of accuracy, cost, latency, fallback design and autonomy decisions.
- A track record of both zero-to-one launches and scaling an established line past its first plateau.
- Strong technical judgement across data models, decision logic, throughput and agent architecture. This is not a functional product role.
- Commercial fluency across pricing, packaging, margin and cost to serve.
- Experience in a regulated domain, with judgement on when to be conservative and when to escalate to legal.
- Experience developing product managers, as a manager or as a senior individual contributor.
- Influence through writing and demonstrated results rather than authority.
BONUS
- Agentic systems where an agent takes real action in an external system.
- HR tech, workforce management, staffing, identity, payroll or financial infrastructure.
- Multi-region product work with regulatory variation as a design problem.
- Usage-based pricing design, including migration away from seat-based models.
- Experience at a forward-deployed or implementation-led company that became a product company.
- First product leader at a company, building the function from scratch.
- Experience working in AI-first or fast-moving product teams.

ABOUT FIRSTWORK
Labour markets are broken. Millions of people are ready to work and can't start. Screening, right-to-work checks, contracts, onboarding and scheduling still run across disconnected systems, with hundreds of manual decisions in between. Firstwork builds AI agents that run frontline workforce operations end to end. We activate hundreds of thousands of workers a month globally for some of the world's largest employers and staffing firms, working forward-deployed inside the customer's operation. Backed by Y Combinator and Gradient (Google’s AI fund), with offices in New York, with London and Dubai opening later this year.
WHY THIS ROLE
European customers are not evaluating us out of curiosity. Workforce compliance has turned into a board-level risk and there are deadlines attached to it. The demand is already here. What we don't have is coverage, or an enterprise motion that repeats.
You are the first commercial hire in Europe and you build the team around you. It is a player-coach role and it stays that way, because we are not going to put someone in charge of coaching a European motion; they have never run against European buyers themselves. You carry a quota while you hire. A Solutions Consultant joins alongside you, SDRs come after that, and how the pod fits together is your call.
None of this starts from zero. The North American playbook holds up on qualification, pricing, security review and technical validation. Your job is to work out which parts of it survive European procurement, works councils and regulators, rebuild the rest, and turn the result into the thing every rep in the region runs.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
- Own enterprise revenue across EMEA, and carry your own deals from first meeting through to signature
- Build and qualify pipeline in staffing, healthcare, logistics, manufacturing and retail
- Turn the North American motion into a European playbook other people can run
- Hire the pod. SDRs, account executives, and with the CEO, the first five people on the team
- Forecast well enough that the exec team can plan the company against it
- Get what you hear in the field back to product while it still matters
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
- Seven or more years selling complex enterprise software, with six and seven figure closes you can talk us through in detail
- Time selling into staffing, healthcare, logistics, manufacturing and/or retail
- Deals across more than one European market, so you know how procurement, works councils and regulators change the shape of a cycle
- Experience hiring and managing reps while still carrying your own number
- The ability to hold a room with a Head of Compliance and a CTO in it at the same time
- A territory run on tooling rather than headcount. AI for account mapping, call prep, proposals and pipeline hygiene, and we will ask to see the stack
- No difficulty being wrong in front of the CEO

THE ROLE
We're looking for a Churn Specialist for our craft subscription box brands to help us get closer to our customers - understand what they actually need, spot where we're falling short, and find ways to retain them.
You'll work across multiple Foxelli Group brands, investigate the full customer lifecycle, and turn data into initiatives that actually move the needle on retention.
You won't just track churn numbers. You'll own the thinking behind what is happening with the brand and drive the ideas to help retain our customers.
If you love:
- getting into customer data and finding the story behind the numbers
- mapping out a customer journey and spotting where things go wrong
- testing ideas - onboarding tweaks, lifecycle flows, CRO experiments, win-back sequences, etc
- using AI and automations to move faster and do more with less
- understanding what makes customers stay (or leave) on a psychological level
- working across multiple products and brands without losing focus
- working with crafts like knitting, crochet, and quilting
And if you're someone who can take a messy churn problem, break it down into clear hypotheses, and see them through to results…
…you might be our person 👀
🚀 WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING
Churn Analysis & Research
- Analyse churn patterns across multiple Foxelli brands - when customers drop, which segments are most at risk, and what's driving it
- Research competitors and benchmark what best-in-class retention looks like in our space
- Use AI tools to accelerate research, surface insights, and identify patterns
- Build a clear picture of our customers - their motivations, frustrations, and what "good enough to stay" actually means to them
Customer Journey & Onboarding
- Audit the full customer lifecycle with a churn lens - from first-touch onboarding to long-term engagement
- Identify drop-off moments and experience gaps that are costing us customers
- Own initiatives to improve onboarding flows and early-stage activation
Retention Initiatives & Experimentation
- Develop hypotheses and run experiments - lifecycle communications, CRO tests, loyalty mechanics, win-back campaigns, cancellation flows
- Build and maintain automations that support retention at scale - triggered flows, at-risk alerts, personalised sequences
- Use AI to generate ideas, draft copy, simulate scenarios, and iterate faster
- Track the impact of every initiative and iterate based on results
- Document what worked, what didn't, and why
AI & Automations
- Build and maintain automations that support retention initiatives at scale
- Proactively explore how AI can improve the way we understand and respond to churn
- Stay current with new tools and bring ideas to the table before anyone asks
WHAT YOU BRING
- At least 2 years of experience of direct experience fixing actual churn for a physical product
- Proven experience diagnosing churn, not just reporting on it, but getting to the root of it

- Experience building automations: triggered flows, lifecycle sequences, or similar

Being in sales is a rewarding career. Doing so within Life Sciences where your technology can help improve the lives of millions is even better. Our Business Development Associates at ONI have just that opportunity. And more. We’re working with some of the brightest researchers in UK, Norway, Sweden, Finland and Denmark to bring our breakthrough Nanoimager technology to their work; work that’ll lead to their own breakthrough discoveries too.  Sales roles aren’t much more rewarding than that.
As an established target-hitting life sciences salesperson where the technology you sell is exceptional but still requires a deep understanding of how it will be deployed, and how it fits the wider research being undertaken. You’re used to being ‘out in the field’ but remaining connected to the business. Others know they can rely on your CRM records (in our case Salesforce) to have clear visibility of exactly where customers are in the pipeline.  And, of course, your forecasting is renowned for its accuracy regardless of how many opportunities you’re handling.
Reporting to our new Global Director of Sales your focus will be on the UK, Norway, Sweden, Finland and Denmark territory and your responsibilities are going to include:
Identifying customers in academia,  pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries using tender portals, CRM tools, customer references and other resources
Owning the sales cycles including lead generation, demonstrations and close of opportunities  to meet and exceed the territories
Working with leadership on development of annual sales strategy, providing input on ways to maximise revenue, efficiency and product opportunities
Keeping CRM updated with prospective and lost sales opportunities, customer interactions, demonstration outcomes, and market feedback
Representing voice of customer internally to Marketing and Customer Success teams, providing market feedback to influence strategy and product development
To be successful you’re going to need that strong track record of achieving your sales targets within the Life Science market, with a degree in that subject area.  What really sets you apart is your own scientific curiosity and credibility to listen, question and engage with researchers to understand their work and goals. Product pricing means our Nanoimagers are most often classified as ‘capex’ and you’re used to unit sales in the $150,000+ range. The thought of talking with scientists about how they’ll use our technology inspires you – as does their mission – but you’re equally as comfortable talking pricing and commercials with procurement teams.
So if you’re ready to help our breakthrough technology and make a breakthrough move in your career we should be talking….

jobs.ashbyhq.com/harmonic-security-inc/a.description_excerpt:
AI is being run everywhere, by humans and agents. Harmonic Security governs all of it. The AI Governance and Control (AIGC) platform understands user / agent intent and data context in real time, giving security teams visibility and control across every tool and workflow so companies can move faster with AI while minimizing risk.
We operate in one of the fastest-moving spaces in tech: the emerging intersection of AI and cybersecurity. It's a market still being defined, and we're among the first to build natively for it - protecting sensitive data in real time, at the endpoint, with minimal friction for the teams using it. Enterprises get full visibility and control. Their people get to innovate without guardrails slowing them down.
Named to the Rising in Cyber 2026 list, Harmonic is gaining serious recognition and serious traction. We're led by deep cybersecurity expertise and backed by investors who know the space: N47, Ten Eleven Ventures, and In-Q-Tel.
As AI adoption inside the enterprise accelerates, the ability to safely observe, control, and enforce policy in real time isn't a nice-to-have. It's mission-critical infrastructure. That's what we build.
HOW WE WORK: AI-FIRST BY DESIGN
Harmonic exists to help enterprises adopt AI safely and at scale. We hold ourselves to that same standard. Everyone here actively leverages AI tools to perform their best work — from deep research and writing to building robust processes and automating complex workflows. We expect every new hire to bring a genuine curiosity for AI and a commitment to using it to work smarter, faster, and with greater creativity.
For some, this involves tinkering and remaining open to emerging tools; for others, it means architecting entirely new systems with AI at the core. We will be transparent about expectations for every role and provide the tools and support needed for you to thrive.
ABOUT THE TEAM
Our Product Delivery team is the engine that turns vision into impact. We ship early and often, getting valuable features into the hands of customers quickly and iterating from there. We work in the open by default, sharing progress and ideas, and we trust each other to own outcomes. We’re a small but mighty crew where every person plays a critical role and we’re committed to using AI to work smarter and faster.
ABOUT THE ROLE
We’re looking for a Backend Engineer who has an appreciation for all things security and system interconnectivity. This is a very hands-on technical role where you will be responsible for designing, building and maintaining scalable integrations between our core applications, identity providers and data security platforms.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
- Own deliveries and features from start to finish
- Design, build, and own backend services in a microservices-based, event-driven architecture
- Implement core domain logic that drives key product workflows and system behavior
- Ingest and process high-volume usage and event data from customer-facing endpoints
- Build backend services that support operational, analytics, and reporting use cases
- Model, persist, and manage domain data, enabling querying, filtering, and lifecycle management
- Expose well-designed APIs and webhooks consumed by customers, UIs, and external systems
- Power customer-facing UI experiences by providing backend APIs for visibility, analytics, and configuration
WHAT YOU BRING
- 3–5+ years of professional software engineering experience building backend services and distributed systems in the Java ecosystem (Java, Spring Boot, Maven/Gradle)
- Strong understanding of event-driven architectures, asynchronous processing patterns, messaging systems, and distributed system design
- Proven experience designing and maintaining RESTful APIs, web hooks, and service-to-service integrations
- Comfortable operating in AWS, GCP, or Azure environments and working with modern observability tooling, logging, and monitoring platforms
- A track record of delivering performant, reliable and scalable applications
- Excellent collaboration and communication skills in cross-functional teams
YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF YOU
- Have experience building products in cybersecurity, identity, governance, compliance, data protection, or enterprise SaaS environments
- You understand not just how to build systems, but why architectural decisions matter
- You can balance scalability, reliability, maintainability, and speed of execution
- You think critically about security, observability, and operational excellence from day one
- Love the idea of blending software development, distributed systems and data-intensive applications
- Strong familiarity with authentication and identity technologies such as OAuth, OpenID Connect (OIDC), SAML, SCIM, Entra ID (Azure AD), Okta, or other enterprise identity providers
- Thrive in fast-paced startup environments where ambiguity is the norm
- Enjoy shaping culture and engineering practices, not just writing code
- Leverage AI tools as an engineer to help you build smarter, faster and better
WHY JOIN US
This isn't just a job - it's a chance to help define a category. Harmonic Security was named to the Rising in Cyber 2026 list, and we're just getting started. We're building at the intersection of AI and security, carving out an emerging market where the rules haven't been written yet, and the people who join now will write them.
We believe today's talent is tomorrow's success, and we're committed to creating an environment where you can do the best work of your life.
- Recognized momentum - We made the Rising in Cyber 2026 list, a signal that the market is taking notice
- Rare market opportunity - Join early in a category-defining company at the convergence of AI and security, where your work directly shapes how enterprises tackle one of the biggest unsolved problems in tech
- Competitive pay and meaningful equity - A real stake in Harmonic's success, not a token gesture
- Comprehensive benefits - 401K, pension plan, generous PTO, and flexible hybrid work
- A small, high-trust team that values transparency, creativity, and continuous learning - no politics, no bureaucracy
- Thoughtful leadership - that cares deeply about your growth, not just your output
- Annual global off-sites - past trips include Lisbon, Portugal and Nashville, TN
- Real ownership - you'll shape the product, the culture, and the direction of the company from day one
HARMONIC'S CORE VALUES
🌱 Flourish in the Unknown
We embrace new, unfamiliar situations that require initiative and rapid decision-making. We orient ourselves quickly and deliver results with minimal guidance.
🔥 Never Full
We raise our hands, take on challenges, and assist others whenever possible. We hunger for opportunities to learn and do more.
🤝 Perfect Harmony
We support one another to create cohesion and unity. We collaborate openly, share feedback honestly, and help everyone produce their best work

jobs.ashbyhq.com/gigaton/85907722-9baa-4.description_excerpt:
At Gigaton, we’re on a mission to cut gigatonnes of carbon emissions from the world’s biggest emitting industries (like cement, steel and glass), by building autonomous AI control and optimisation systems that learn and leverage the physics of manufacturing. Our products run heavy industrial plants more efficiently, more stably, and with lower emissions in real time - laying the foundation for the next industrial revolution.
We are a team of scientists, engineers, builders, and operators who love hard problems, have high standards, and want to make change happen in the physical world. We care about deep tech, but we care even more about whether it delivers cost and carbon impact in a live plant, with real people, under real constraints.
With Gigaton, you’ll solve really tough problems in places few people ever get close to, and build something that actually helps the planet. Are you up for the challenge?
ABOUT THE ROLE
We’re seeking a Solutions Engineer to join our Solutions Engineering team and sit on the frontline of industrial decarbonisation.
This role blends industrial process expertise, control engineering, and deployment leadership. You’ll work directly with plant management, process engineers and operators to understand complex chemical processes, design optimal AI control strategies, and integrate Gigaton’s AI into live production environments. Your mission is to ensure that we delight our customers by using our AI solutions to solve critical operational problems and deliver real, measurable cost and carbon impact.
YOUR MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES
- Build trust and engagement with plant managers, process engineers and operators by clearly explaining technical decisions and demonstrating measurable benefits aligned to operational needs.
- Analyse plant data to assess and identify opportunities, and evaluate the performance of Gigaton’s software.
- Develop and refine control strategies, leveraging APC, MPC, and PID principles.
- Deploy and integrate Gigaton AI into live plants, ensuring stable, safe, and effective operation.
- Collaborate with plant and process teams to identify optimisation opportunities, tune control loops, and validate performance improvements.
- Collaborate with machine learning engineers to refine algorithms and recommendations based on real-world outcomes.
- Create and refine deployment playbooks and templates, ensuring repeatable, scalable, and high-quality rollouts across plants.
- Act as a feedback loop into Gigaton’s product and machine learning teams, providing field insights that shape our product roadmap.
- Travel to sites (~1 week/month) to work hands-on with teams during commissioning, testing, and optimisation phases.
WHAT A GREAT FIT LOOKS LIKE
- Strong process or control engineering background, ideally in cement, chemicals, energy or heavy manufacturing.
- Comfortable collaborating with operators, plant managers, engineers, and data scientists, bridging industrial know-how with data-driven insights.

About Us
Hawk is the leading provider of AI-supported anti-money laundering and fraud detection technology. Banks and payment providers globally are using Hawk’s powerful combination of traditional rules and explainable AI to improve the effectiveness of their AML compliance and fraud prevention by identifying more crime while maximizing efficiency by reducing false positives. With our solution, we are playing a vital role in the global fight against Money Laundering, Fraud, or the financing of terrorism. We offer a culture of mutual trust, support and passion – while providing individuals with opportunities to grow professionally and make a difference in the world.
YOUR MISSION
As an Implementation Specialist at Hawk, your responsibility is to transform customer requirements into a functioning solution that helps them achieve their business objectives around transaction monitoring, customer screening and fraud detection, alongside cutting-edge AI technologies. You start with a signed contract and support the customer until go-live. This includes translating policies, regulatory obligations and risk factors into Hawk's setup, data mapping, workflow configuration, UAT support and ensuring that key project timelines and milestones are met. You support our customers in realising true value by detecting more financial crime, allowing investigators to focus on what matters instead of drowning in false positives, and adopting state-of-the-art AI technologies.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
- Requirements and needs assessment: gather and analyse the customer's AML, fraud and screening requirements and advise on best-practice configuration.
- Configuration: translate policies, screening algorithms, regulatory requirements and risk factors into Hawk's setup, covering rules, screening, customer risk rating and workflows.
- Data mapping and integration: lead the technical deployment and integration with the customer's systems, via API or batch mechanisms.
- Testing and go-live: support the customer through testing, UAT and sign-off, troubleshoot issues, and support a successful transition to a production environment.
- Training and enablement: deliver training to the customer's teams from a functional as well as technical standpoint.
- Project management: plan and run the implementation from signature to go-live on time and within scope, with documentation and regular stakeholder updates, combining hands-on work with project leadership.
- Primary contact: be the first point of contact for implementation questions and issues.
- Collaboration and feedback: work closely with Customer Value Partners for a smooth implementation, and bring actionable customer feedback and gaps to Product, Development and Hawk's GTM organisation.
- Document every configuration decision and the reasoning behind it, so the setup holds up when the customer's auditor or regulator asks why a rule was set the way it was.
- Manage each implementation task and the implementation success as an outcome you own, as directed by our Customer Value Partner, resulting in activity completion and a go-live on the dates you committed to.
YOUR PROFILE
- 6+ years in implementation consulting or solution consulting, with at least 3 of those years hands-on implementing AML, fraud or screening solutions.
- Subject matter expertise in AML and compliance. You are familiar with key typologies and patterns, the regulatory expectations behind them, and how monitoring programmes as well as AI get examined.
- You can confidently stand in front of an MLRO and discuss and defend a rule set. This is a must-have, not a nice-to-have.
- Hands-on data skills: SQL, APIs, CSV and JSON, and data modelling. You're familiar with standardised payment message formats, including SWIFT MT and ISO 20022, SEPA and card data.
- Integration literacy. You don't write production code, but you're at home with APIs, JSON payloads, SFTP configurations as well as SSO.
- Proven track record of taking complex implementations to go-live on time, ideally several in parallel, with banking customers or other financial institutions.
- Stakeholder alignment. You ensure that internal and external parties both have the information they need, keep them aligned and manage expectations.
- Able to explain complexity simply. Imagine data models for compliance leads, fraud typologies for data engineers. You do it clearly in writing and in the room, in fluent English.
- A degree in computer science, information systems, engineering, finance or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
BONUS
- Business-fluent German, for working with our DACH customers.
- CAMS (or equivalent) certification, or time spent in a second-line compliance or MLRO team.
- Builds constructive relationships with customers and stays calm and under pressure Builder mentality: works independently and brings structure to ambiguity where no established process exists, taking the initiative to define one.
- Is a resourceful problem-solver who investigates unknowns and tests system behaviour. Knows when and whom to escalate.
- Manages expectations proactively. Flags timeline and scope risks early, quantifies them, offers phased options and aligns Sales and Customer Success.
- Handles product gaps transparently. Clarifies the underlying (regulatory) requirement, offers workarounds with their trade-offs, feeds back to Product and doesn't commit to unconfirmed dates .
- You use AI tools such as Claude in your daily workflow to speed up mapping, documentation and analysis, and you have opinions about where they help and where they don't.

About Us
Hawk is the leading provider of AI-supported anti-money laundering and fraud detection technology. Banks and payment providers globally are using Hawk’s powerful combination of traditional rules and explainable AI to improve the effectiveness of their AML compliance and fraud prevention by identifying more crime while maximizing efficiency by reducing false positives. With our solution, we are playing a vital role in the global fight against Money Laundering, Fraud, or the financing of terrorism. We offer a culture of mutual trust, support and passion – while providing individuals with opportunities to grow professionally and make a difference in the world.
YOUR MISSION
As a Customer Data Scientist at Hawk, you're the person our customers trust to make their AML and fraud detection models actually work for them: tuned to their transaction patterns, defensible to their regulators, and provably effective in their own numbers. You sit inside the regional customer team, working directly alongside Customer Value Partners on live accounts, not behind a wall of tickets from a central data science function. Your work spans model and threshold tuning, deep analytical investigation into detection performance, and building the customer-facing narrative that shows exactly what's improved and why. You've done this in front of customers before, and you know the difference between a model that scores well in a notebook and one that survives contact with a real investigator's workload.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
- Tune and optimize detection models and thresholds against each customer's live transaction data, balancing detection effectiveness against false positive load, not just against a benchmark dataset.
- Investigate detection performance deeply: dig into missed cases, alert quality, and pattern drift, and turn what you find into concrete tuning or configuration changes.
- Translate technical findings into customer-facing insight: build the analysis that shows investigator productivity gains, false positive cost reduction, and detection effectiveness improvements in language a customer's compliance and risk leadership actually uses.
- Sit in the room with customers directly. Present findings, defend your methodology to a customer's own data science or compliance team, and answer the hard “why did the model do this” questions live.
- Partner closely with your regional Customer Value Partners on account strategy, informing where the model needs to change to unlock the next stage of value realization or a renewal conversation.
- Feed patterns and findings back into Hawk's broader model and product functions, distinguishing between “this customer needs local tuning” and “this is a systemic gap worth fixing centrally.”
- Own the regulatory defensibility of the tuning decisions you make. Document your reasoning so a customer's audit or regulator review holds up.
- Bring rigor to how you validate model changes before they go live: backtesting, sample review, and sign-off discipline that protects the customer's compliance posture.
YOUR PROFILE
- 5-7 years as a data scientist in a customer-facing role, presenting analysis and defending model decisions directly to clients. This is not an internal-facing engineering or product data science background; you've sat across the table from a customer before.
- Real experience in AML, fraud detection, or financial crime analytics is required. You understand transaction monitoring, typologies, and what a false positive actually costs an investigator, not just what one costs on a confusion matrix.
- Strong hands-on skills in the standard data science stack (Python, SQL, and whatever ML tooling you've used in production), but your edge is judgment under ambiguity: knowing when a model change is safe to make and when it needs a human in the loop.
- Comfortable being the technical voice in a room with a customer's risk, compliance, or data science stakeholders, and holding your own when questioned.
- A track record of translating model performance into business value a non-technical stakeholder can act on: not just accuracy metrics, but investigator hours saved, false positive cost avoided, and cases caught.
- Genuine comfort with ambiguity and live production systems. You're not looking for a clean offline research problem, you're looking for the “why did this alert fire on a real customer's data at 2pm today” problem.
- An ownership mentality. You don't wait for a ticket; you notice when an account's detection performance is drifting and you go find out why.
BONUS
- Experience specifically in transaction monitoring or payments fraud detection at a bank, payment provider, or a vendor serving them.
- Familiarity with explainable AI and rules-based hybrid detection approaches, since that's core to how Hawk's models work.

Responsibilities
• Lead the implementation and delivery of real-time embedded firmware for AEC retimer silicon across 224G/lane, 448G/lane and forward-looking 896G/lane configurations; remain a hands-on C/C++ contributor.
• Implement and maintain boot, configuration, calibration, link-training, fault-recovery and run-time supervision state machines on resource-constrained RISC-V or ARM platforms.
• Translate approved firmware architecture into module designs, APIs, task and interrupt models, memory budgets and hardware/software contracts; surface implementation tradeoffs early.
• Code, debug and optimize firmware for SerDes equalization and adaptation, FEC-aware monitoring and re-adaptation, telemetry capture, thermal behavior and power management.
• Own low-level drivers and management interfaces including SPI, I2C/SMBus, I3C, MCTP and JTAG, and integrate firmware services with the CMIS management layer.
• Drive pre-silicon development and first-silicon bring-up; isolate issues across firmware, RTL, boards and lab setups using JTAG, register traces and targeted instrumentation.
• Set coding and review standards; build unit, integration and hardware-in-loop tests; enforce CI, static analysis and release evidence; improve Python-based build, debug and test tools.
• Break the roadmap into deliverable work packages, estimate and track execution, mentor firmware engineers and coordinate with architecture, ASIC, DV, validation, SI and applications teams.
Essential Experience
• 8+ years developing and debugging production real-time firmware in C/C++, including 2+ years leading firmware modules, projects or a small team.
• Expert hands-on C/C++ in resource-constrained systems, with recent evidence of personal code delivery, code review and complex defect resolution.
• Firmware experience on a retimer, gearbox, PHY, AEC, AOC, optical module, networking ASIC or comparable high-speed mixed hardware/software product.
• RISC-V and/or ARM bare-metal or RTOS firmware, including interrupts, traps, CSR or register access, concurrency and tight RAM/flash budgets.
• RTOS development with Zephyr, FreeRTOS or equivalent; ownership of scheduling, synchronization, timing and failure recovery.
• At least one silicon or board bring-up cycle using JTAG and related debug mechanisms, with root-cause analysis across firmware, drivers, RTL and hardware.
• Python, Git/GitLab, Make/CMake, CI, unit and integration testing, and static analysis, with disciplined reproducible development workflows.
BS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or Computer Science, or equivalent experience; strong communication, planning, mentoring and cross-functional leadership.
Useful experience
• IEEE 802.3ck or 802.3dj link training and equalization, SerDes adaptation algorithms, channel-quality monitoring and register-level PHY tuning.
• FEC exposure including KP4 or RS-544, pre-FEC and post-FEC telemetry, symbol-error analysis and FEC-aware recovery behavior.
• CMIS 5.x firmware integration, module or datapath state machines, VDM telemetry, and sideband protocols including SMBus, I3C and MCTP.
• Bootloaders, secure boot, root of trust, authenticated A/B firmware updates, rollback protection and field-recovery mechanisms.
• Pre-silicon firmware development using QEMU, SystemC, FPGA, simulation or emulation; heterogeneous multicore or vector-processing systems.
PCIe or CXL, hyperscaler qualification, interoperability debugging, and production support for field or manufacturing issues.

About Legal 500
Legal 500 is a global legal market research, data and intelligence business. Our research helps corporate clients make informed decisions about legal representation and gives law firms insight into their market position, performance, and clients.
Beyond research, we’re building a growing data, benchmarking, market-intelligence and subscription service offering. We bring the legal market together through a global programme of events - awards ceremonies, conferences and roundtables that convene leading law firms, in-house teams and their advisers. And through Legal Business, our journalistic title, we deliver independent news, analysis and commentary on the business of law and the strategy, performance and leadership of the world’s leading law firms.
We are a growing, multi-site organisation, with colleagues working across research, data, technology, product, journalism, commercial and events in London, Leeds and Bristol.
About the Role
This is a new role at Legal 500, created as a result of a period of growth due to acquisitons, new products and creating new research capability. We are, therefore, looking to hire two driven and commercially minded Business Development Managers to generate new subscription revenue across our product portfolio. by identifying, engaging, and converting prospective customers.
This role is ideal for a proactive sales professional with experience selling subscription-based products, information services, memberships, or recurring revenue products.
What you'll be doing:
New Business Development
- Identify and target prospective customers across legal market in the US
- Build and maintain a robust pipeline of qualified opportunities.
- Conduct outbound prospecting through calls and email
- Be unfazed by contacting C-suite decision makers across multiple international jurisdictions and confidently presenting and selling the product to marketing and legal professionals across the world’s leading law firms, as well as partners and senior lawyers.
Sales & Revenue Growth
- Manage the full sales cycle from lead generation to contract signature.
- Deliver compelling product demonstrations and presentations.
- Understand client needs and align subscription solutions to business challenges.
- Negotiate commercial terms and close deals to achieve and exceed revenue targets.
Market Intelligence
- Stay informed on industry trends, customer challenges, and competitor activity.
- Provide feedback to marketing, product, and leadership teams on market opportunities.
- Identify emerging sectors and growth areas for subscription sales.
Collaboration
- Work closely with marketing to maximise lead generation campaigns.
- Partner with customer success and account management teams to ensure smooth onboarding and handover.
- Contribute to sales strategy, pricing discussions, and go-to-market initiatives.
What we're looking for:
- Solid experience in business development, new business sales, or subscription sales
- Proven track record of achieving or exceeding revenue targets
- Experience selling subscription information, media, research, or membership products
- Strong consultative selling and negotiation skills
- Excellent communication and presentation skills
- Ability to manage multiple opportunities simultaneously
Even better if you have...
- Experience selling to professional services firms, legal, financial, or corporate clients
- Knowledge of recurring revenue business models
- Experience using CRM platforms (Salesforce, HubSpot, Dynamics, etc.)
- Experience with social selling and LinkedIn prospecting
- Understanding of customer success and retention principles
Role information
- This role can be based in either our London or Bristol offices
- This is a US-focused role - our working hours are 9.30am - 5.30pm but you will have flexibiliy to make your day work
- We operate a hybrid working policy - 3 days per week in the office and 2 days remote

About the Role
Our new Enterprise AI Product Owner will own the adoption and value of AI in how Legal 500 works. You'll use our enterprise AI tools, with Microsoft Copilot and the wider Microsoft 365 AI capability as the main platform. You'll recommend what should be built or adopted and why, put governance in place where none yet exists, and make sure people across the business use the tools well.
This is a business-facing product role that starts from how the business works, not a technical build role. Copilot is the primary tool of choice, but you'll also oversee the other AI tools the business adopts.
What you'll do
You'll sit centrally within our People & Business Operations function, reporting to the Director of People & Business Operations. Your remit covers the whole of Legal 500, not a single department. You'll:
- Own the roadmap and prioritised backlog for our enterprise AI opportunities, recommending what to build or adopt, what not to, and why. You'll write clear user stories and acceptance criteria and hold a consistent line with senior stakeholders when demand exceeds capacity.

ABOUT NEURAL CONCEPT
Neural Concept is the engineering intelligence platform used by leading manufacturers in automotive, aerospace, and energy. We combine geometric and physics AI with LLM-based agents so engineering teams can move from customer requirements to validated designs in a fraction of the usual time.
ABOUT THE ROLE
Design decisions depend on information that lives outside the CAD model: customer requirements, design rules, manufacturing and assembly constraints, and cost targets. This information is spread across specification documents, handbooks, ERP systems, requirements management tools, and system models. Engineers gather it by hand, often late in the process, and conflicts surface at design reviews or on the production line.
We call the capability that closes this gap Design Engineering Knowledge. It connects the design to the information ecosystem around it, so requirements, constraints, and trade-offs are available to engineers and AI agents while they work on the design itself.
As a Product Engineer, you will build this capability. Requirements are the first focus area: extracting them from customer specifications and requirements management systems, structuring them, and keeping them traceable. You will then extend the same foundation to design rule checks, Design for Manufacturing (DfM), Design for Assembly (DfA), and Design for Cost, and connect it to the enterprise systems where this knowledge already lives.
You will work with the Product Manager, solution engineers, and customer engineering teams, as the primary developer from the first customer conversation to the version running in production.

- Extend this foundation to design rules, DfM, DfA, and Design for Cost, turning standards, handbooks, and company know-how into constraints that software and agents can use.
- Bring requirements, constraints, and trade-offs into the design workflow, so engineers can check a design against them at any stage and see which ones apply to the part they are working on.
- Build integrations with the systems around the design: requirements management systems, ERP (cost, materials, and supplier data), and system design and MBSE tools for architecture and system-level requirements.
- Design the data model that links requirements, rules, and constraints to parts, design parameters, and simulation results.
- Create evaluation sets and quality metrics with customers, so extraction and checking accuracy is measured and improves with every release.
- Design human-in-the-loop review flows where engineers validate and edit AI output, with versioning and a full audit trail.
- Spot recurring patterns across customers and turn them into reusable components of the Neural Concept platform.

- Experience integrating with enterprise systems through APIs and data models, for example ERP, PLM, or requirements management tools.
- Experience with document processing, such as PDF parsing, OCR, or information extraction.

Of course, you cannot do this alone.
As a Growth Strategist at Maneuver, you will lead a product marketing team comprising a copywriter, creative strategist, designer, and media buyer to grow 2 flagship products. You’ll meet with fellow Growth Strategists to exchange ideas and best practices regularly. The product marketing team is supported by cross-functional teams: (a) Influencer & Partnerships, (b) Videos, (c) Marketplaces, (d) Measurement, (e) Retention, (f) Other Channels (e.g. AppLovin, Google), and (g) Tech - all of which are essential to grow a product to $100M+ a year profitably.
As such, the best candidates have a track record of building something from scratch and demonstrate strong resourcefulness to overcome challenges and explore uncharted territory.
WHAT YOU’LL DO
STRATEGIC GROWTH PLANNING & OPPORTUNITY DISCOVERY
You’ll own the development and iteration of Meta-led growth strategies grounded in first principles, real-world data, and deep DTC competitive intelligence.
- Identify bottlenecks and opportunities through structured root-cause analysis across creative, media, offer, funnel, and product positioning.
- Systematically uncover under-tapped or untapped opportunities by reverse-engineering winning DTC products and offers across Google Search, Amazon, Shopify, Meta, YouTube, and adjacent channels.
- Analyze why products sell well (positioning, mechanism, claims, pricing, bundles, merchandising, distribution) and map those learnings to Maneuver’s products to unlock new markets, angles, and growth paths.
- Prioritize high-leverage initiatives that balance short-term profitability with long-term strategic breakthroughs (new positioning, new audiences, new use cases).
- Act with urgency to gather new signals, test hypotheses, and adapt strategy in-market.
- Ruthlessly focus team energy on the highest-ROI initiatives that move core business metrics.
DEEP MARKET & CUSTOMER RESEARCH
You’ll lead a continuous discovery process that directly informs positioning, creative direction, funnel strategy, and media execution.
- Conduct social listening across Facebook Groups, Reddit, TikTok, Pinterest, reviews, and UGC ecosystems to surface pains, unmet needs, objections, and language patterns.
- Dive into product‑level inputs (clinical studies, ingredient claims, AOV/LTV trends, customer reviews, refunds, CX tickets) to sharpen value propositions and positioning.
- Run deep competitive audits using tools such as Meta Ad Library, Atria, Transparency Center, VidTao, Google Search, and Amazon to identify messaging gaps, offer structures, and creative patterns.
- Triangulate qualitative and quantitative insights into clear strategic actions that unlock growth.
MEDIA STRATEGY
Design and manage high-performance Meta ad systems that balance testing discipline with scalable performance.
- Architect account structures, naming conventions, and testing frameworks for clean data capture and fast learning.
- Execute and evolve bid strategies (Cost Cap, minROAS, Bid Cap, Highest Volume, Accelerated Bid Cap) based on signal quality, scale phase, and business context.
- Build creative testing matrices and scale frameworks (ABO/CBO/ASC setups, budget ramps, funnel staging, whitelisting).
- Ensure delivery systems and media execution align tightly with strategic hypotheses and growth objectives.
CREATIVE STRATEGY & MESSAGING ARCHITECTURE
You’ll provide a bird’s eye view of the creative and messaging ecosystem, ensuring alignment across teams and funnel stages.
- Co-own the high‑level creative roadmap across TOF / MOF / BOF / Buyer stages with the copywriter and creative strategist
- Map current messaging by awareness level and sophistication, identifying gaps, redundancies, and misalignment.
- Assess whether ads, offers, and funnels are congruent with the intended messaging strategy at each stage.
- Co‑own messaging architecture with the copywriter and creative strategist, helping segment and prioritize messaging buckets such as, but not limited to:
- Authority / expert‑led
- Founder / brand story
- Mechanism‑led education
- Objection handling
- Social proof & validation
- Use in‑market performance signals to continuously refine angles and creative direction.
FUNNEL STRATEGY, CRO & PROJECT OWNERSHIP
You’ll own funnel strategy, CRO direction, and end‑to‑end project execution.
- Identify funnel bottlenecks and CRO opportunities in partnership with media buyers, creative strategists, and copywriters.
- Define what should change and why (structure, messaging emphasis, flow, offer presentation), and translate that into clear briefs for copywriters and designers.
- Collaborate with tech team members to implement changes once copy and mock‑ups are finalized.
- Own projects end‑to‑end: scoping, prioritization, implementation, QA, launch, and post‑launch monitoring.
- Ensure tight feedback loops post‑launch, with media buyers monitoring test performance and providing analysis to inform next iterations.
COLLABORATION
You’ll act as the connective tissue between strategy, media, creative, CRO, and cross‑functional partners.
- Provide high‑signal strategic and CRO briefs aligned on performance goals and compliance considerations.
- Partner closely with creative strategists, copywriters, and designers to ensure creative execution reinforces strategy.
- Collaborate tightly with media buyers on test design, optimization feedback, and learning agendas.
- Bring awareness to upstream partners (tech, supply chain, CX, retention)…

You’ll partner with all departments in a matrix environment (Creative, Growth, Tech & Ops) and have direct contact with senior managers and leaders to turn business goals into people outcomes. Expect real ownership: run performance cadences, level pay decisions, uplevel managers, and automate HR ops with modern tooling. You’ll refine playbooks, policies, programs and strategies and prove impact with eNPS, cycle time, and retention metrics.
If you are looking for a challenge, eager to learn, love translating data into decisions, coaching managers, and building scalable, hybrid set-up, this role will stretch your craft and accelerate your career growth!
This is a fully remote role that involves close collaboration with Singapore-based stakeholders. Candidates should be able to provide at least 3–4 hours of working overlap each day within Singapore business hours (9:00 AM–6:00 PM SGT).
WHAT YOU’LL DO
COMPETENCY FRAMEWORKS, PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT & COMPENSATION

- Support and strengthen job levelling and role clarity across functions
- Orchestrate SMART KPIs linked to company OKRs, mid-cycle checkpoints, calibrations, and high-quality review narratives
- Coach and train managers on feedback, bias checks, and PDPs/PIPs with clear success criteria
- Convert review outcomes into 30/60/90-day development plans tied to skills, courses, and mentoring support
- Help prepare compensation approval packs with compa-ratio, budget gates, parity checks, and transparent total-rewards rationale
- Perform pre-offer checks and parity spot audits to support fair, consistent compensation decisions
- Ensure performance and compensation processes are documented clearly and applied consistently across teams
EMPLOYEE ENGAGEMENT, CULTURE & COMMUNICATIONS
- Run quarterly pulses, segment insights, and publish action plans with clear owners and timelines
- Translate engagement data into practical recommendations for leaders and managers
- Support employee experience initiatives across both in-person and remote/distributed teams
- Enable managers with comms packs, town hall content, and recognition rituals tied to company values
- Help strengthen culture, connection, inclusion, and follow-through through clear communication and manager enablement

ONBOARDING, OFFBOARDING & TRANSITIONS

Report time-to-proficiency, mobility, certification, and ROI narratives each quarter

Mimica automatically analyzes your team’s work, then generates the AI agents to execute it. Our software turns everyday work into data-backed decisions, helping companies remove process bottlenecks, automate the right tasks, and upskill teams with precision and confidence.
We’ve raised $26 million in Series B financing and are scaling fast. Backed by investors including Khosla Ventures and Paladin Capital, our proprietary AI technology is trusted by Fortune 500 companies to accelerate transformation. Mimica is recognized as a Top 100 AI Start-up by Accel and an industry Leader by the Everest Group.
Our team
Behind our platform is a team of exceptionally talented people, remote-first and globally distributed across 16+ countries. We're looking for curious, collaborative people excited to solve complex problems. You'll join a fast-paced environment built on high ownership, bottom-up thinking, and transparent, open communication – helping some of the world's leading organizations transform the way work gets done with AI.
Where we are in our scale-up journey
We’ve achieved strong product-market fit and are now scaling with intention. You’ll join a 60-person team of Senior+ engineers and Product leaders who prioritise product impact over mere headcount. We have 8 cross-functional teams, including a dedicated Platform team focused on infra & developer experience. We started building proprietary ML before the LLM boom, so we don't just consume models - we train them from the ground up.
Our approach to engineering
- We prioritize customer needs first
- We work in small, cross-functional, feature-oriented teams
- We have flexibility in terms of the problems we work on
- We own the full lifecycle of our projects
- We avoid silos and encourage taking up tasks in new areas
- We balance quality and velocity
- We have a shared responsibility for our production code
- We each set our own routine to maximize our productivity
YOUR MISSION
You will join our Mapper Team, whose goal is to produce and service the Process Maps that are at the core of Mimica's product.
We found good product-market fit, which means two things: building new features and making architectural decisions that will enable exponential growth in usage.
You will take ownership of projects end-to-end, build new features, release improvements to existing components, and take operational responsibility for what you build.
We have a bottom-up culture where Engineers identify pain points, experiment with and iterate on their solutions, and leverage tight feedback loops.
As such, you‘ll have the opportunity to shape the technical direction, processes and culture of the Engineering org, Chapter and Team.
PART OF YOUR DAY-TO-DAY
- Developing data-visualisation applications and new features around displaying significant large data properties (e.g., insights regarding processes, workflows and metrics) in effective ways, with scalability & reliability in mind.
- Building interfaces and real-time frontend services that enable multiple users to edit graph data and re-train AI models through their input.
- Owning projects end-to-end as part of small teams, collaborating with our TLs and Product Managers.
- Participating in architectural decisions, collaborating across teams to identify and implement product improvements and producing documentation for your implementations.
- Participate in and improve the Team's and Chapter's internal processes and rituals so that we're more effective.
- Providing feedback to peers through RFCs, code reviews and helping those around you to level up.
- Participating in hiring and onboarding new team members.
WHO YOU ARE
- You have at least 8+ years of experience as a Software Engineer and high engineering standards.
- Strong experience and understanding of React, state management, front-end architecture & concepts.
- Knowledge of advanced system design principles, data structures, algorithms, and the core concepts underlying data-intensive applications.
- Deep understanding of advanced performance optimisation techniques.
- Previous experience working in the backend.
- Committed to upholding high engineering standards, delivering clean, testable, reusable, modular, and well-documented code.
- Experience owning projects from start to finish, including speccing, design, development, testing, deployment, release and observability.
- Drive to develop your skills, improve team processes and reduce debt.
- Fluency in English, with effective communication skills – articulating complex ideas, concepts and trade-offs clearly.
BONUS
- Background working in fast-paced, successful scale-up environments or as a founding engineer, with a track record of delivering value quickly and iteratively alongside building processes.
- Graph or Canvas-based Rendering, or graph/geometry editing. (FE-focused).
Location
This is a fully remote position. To ensure effective collaboration with our team, we are only considering candidates in the following regions:
- Europe & Africa: Locations within European timezones (typically UTC-1 to UTC+3).
- The Americas: Locations in the Eastern Time Zone (e.g., US East Coast, Toronto) or UTC-3 (e.g., Brazil, Argentina)
RECRUITMENT STAGES
- Stage 1 | Recruiter Screen with Technical Recruiter
- Stage 2 | Take-home Challenge (async) + Follow-up (Live) - with colleagues in an equivalent role
- Stage 3 | System Design (Live) - with the Chapter Leader + colleagues
- Stage 4 | Founders/Behavioural Interview - with Chapter Leader + Co-founder/CTO
WHAT WE OFFER
💰 Generous compensation + stock options - aligned with our internal framework, market data, and individual skills.
🏢 Distributed work: Work from anywhere - fully remote, in our hubs, or a mix.
💻 Company-issued laptop, remote setup stipend, and co-working budget
📍 Flexible schedules and location
☀️ Ample paid time off, in addition to local public holidays
🍼 Enhanced parental leave
🧘‍♀️ Health & retirement benefits
📖 Annual learning & development budget
🌴 Annual workaways and regular virtual & in-person socials
🌍 Opportunity to contribute to groundbreaking projects that shape the future of work
Note: Some benefits may vary depending on location and role

Location: While this position is posted in a specific location, all of Oyster's positions are fully remote, you can work from home, forever. To create the best experience for our new hire, this role requires you to be based within +3 / -5 UTC.
We’re hiring a Lead Product Manager to own the vision, strategy, and outcomes for a critical area of Oyster’s Employer of Record product. You will shape customer-facing experiences, internal tools, and operational workflows that help companies employ talent globally with confidence, compliance, and simplicity.
You will work across the full EOR system, not only individual features, to understand how customer needs, country requirements, policies, data, operational processes, and technology interact. You will start with the customer problem and desired business outcome, use direct discovery and first-principles reasoning to identify root causes, and decide whether the best intervention belongs in product, process, policy, Operations, or a combination.
You’ll operate independently, making and communicating difficult trade-offs amid ambiguity. You will constructively challenge requested solutions, align senior stakeholders, and connect product decisions to measurable customer, operational, and commercial impact. You will also identify where AI and automation create real value, and where risk or customer needs call for a human in the loop.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
- Own the product vision, strategy, prioritization, and measurable outcomes for an EOR sub-domain.
- Build a systems-level view of customer journeys, internal workflows, policy constraints, data flows, and exceptions across the EOR lifecycle.
- Lead direct customer and operational discovery. Separate symptoms and feature requests from underlying problems, and evaluate product, process, policy, and operational interventions before choosing a solution.
- Translate strategy into outcome-based roadmaps with clear decisions, learning plans, and success measures.
- Work deeply with Operations and AI Engineers to improve scalability, exception handling, service quality, and cost-to-serve, not simply digitize existing processes.
- Partner with Engineering and Design from discovery through delivery, using prototypes and technical insight to reduce risk early.
- Constructively challenge and align senior stakeholders across Legal, Compliance, Finance, Operations, and Go-to-Market, and communicate strategy, trade-offs, and impact clearly in senior forums.
- Contribute repeatable product practices that strengthen discovery, decision quality, and outcome ownership across the Product organization.
CORE REQUIREMENTS
- 5+ years in Product Management, including demonstrable experience owning a complex product area end-to-end.
- 3+ years in HR tech, payroll, benefits, hiring, compliance, or another regulated or operationally complex B2B domain.
- Strong systems thinking, with the ability to explain how policy, operations, data, and technology interact, including exceptions and edge cases.
- Proven first-principles thinking: the ability to separate the requested feature from the desired outcome and explain why one intervention (product, process, policy, or Operations) was chosen over the alternatives.
- Strategic judgment and independence: proven ability to make significant decisions under ambiguity, with explicit trade-offs and a clear view of what was deprioritized.
- Deep direct-customer discovery, with examples where conversations with customers and operational teams materially changed the problem definition or planned solution.
- Proven ability to constructively challenge, persuade, and align senior stakeholders with competing priorities, and to partner strongly with Operations, Engineering, and Design.
- Clear executive communication, with evidence of measurable customer, operational, or commercial impact (e.g. cost-to-serve, cycle time, retention), including the baseline, the change, and how the result was attributed to the decision.
Bonus / Nice-to-Have Experience
- EOR, payroll, HR technology, benefits, compliance, fintech, healthcare, logistics, or another regulated and operationally complex domain. Transferable experience counts where the complexity is comparable (multi-country rules, compliance exposure, human-in-the-loop workflows).
- Scaling products or workflows across countries, customers, teams, or markets.
- Hands-on experience prototyping with AI tools or shipping responsible AI- or automation-enabled product experiences.
- Fully distributed and multicultural working experience.
YOU'LL ALSO NEED
- A reliable home internet connection and fluency in both written and spoken English.
- High standards for quality, ethics, privacy, and compliance in products that affect people and employment.
HOW WE WORK TOGETHER AT OYSTER
Our values guide the work we do, the decisions we make, and the culture that makes Oyster what it is. We make it happen—progress is our default setting. We drive change, we build and give trust, and we move as one united team.

We are hiring a content marketing lead to set the company-wide direction for Oyster’s editorial narrative: the category story we tell about the future of work, the arguments our executives make in public, and the original research that HR, Finance, and Legal leaders cite when making decisions.

- Act as the final quality bar for voice, accuracy, evidence, and taste across human- and AI-produced content.
Build company-wide AI content mechanisms
- Architect and govern reusable systems for research, brand voice, fact-checking, source verification, repurposing, evaluation, and reporting.
- Define risk-based rules for where AI leads, where humans lead, and where specialist or executive approval is mandatory.
- Establish mechanisms and standards adopted across Marketing and relevant partner teams, not only within the content workflow.
- Measure leverage through throughput, cycle time, cost, adoption, quality, and business impact; evolve the system each quarter.

- Set the operating model for executive publishing and advise leaders on the arguments Oyster should make publicly.

- Build reporting that enables executives and teams to make better portfolio and investment decisions.
- Identify emerging market shifts early and recommend company responses before they become obvious.

- Set direction for senior stakeholders, freelancers, agencies, specialists, and subject-matter experts without relying on formal authority.
- Create decision rights, operating rhythms, and shared standards that enable multiple teams to execute consistently.

This role is based out of our Amsterdam office 🇳🇱 or London office 🇬🇧
We are an office-first company & believe great products are made when we are together.
About Stacks
Stacks is building an AI-native platform that reinvents how modern finance teams run the monthly close. The opportunity is massive: every growing company depends on accurate, timely financial data, yet most are still operating with tools and workflows built for a different era.
In just two years, we’ve grown from a team of 2 to 30+ and are on a rapid trajectory. We’ve raised a $23m Series A led by Lightspeed Venture Partners https://stacks.ai/resources/stacks-raises-23-million-to-reinvent-finance-operations-with-agentic-ai, and we were recently recognised as one of Harmonic’s Hottest Startups of 2026 https://harmonic.ai/hot-25-companies/q2-2026.
We’re already trusted by leading European scale-ups including Pleo, Freetrade, and Motorway.
Our team is a blend of finance, product, and technical experts from top-tier companies like Uber, Plaid, Miro, Mollie, and Bunq, united by the drive to create a game-changing solution.
We’re a team that is deeply customer-obsessed, plays to win, and isn’t afraid to take big, bold bets. We move fast, hold a high bar, and are committed to growing together as we scale.
ABOUT THE ROLE
Stacks is looking for a fiercely ambitious, entrepreneurial, and commercially driven Accounting Engineer / Solutions Consultant to join our GTM team!
In this high-impact role, you’ll contribute to create and execute our GTM strategy at Stacks. If you’re excited by the idea of limitless growth and fast-paced challenges, this is a unique opportunity to accelerate your career as you help shape the future of Stacks.
🧱 WHAT YOU'LL DO
- Drive Solutions Engineering: Own the technical and accounting aspects of the sales and post-sales journey, from discovery and demos to implementation and optimization. You’ll regularly interact with Controllers, VPs of Finance, and CFOs.
- Accounting Expertise Meets Customer Focus: Leverage your deep accounting knowledge to advise prospective and existing customers on best practices & help them translate complex accounting workflows into solutions using Stacks.
- Sales Engineering Excellence: Partner with Sales, Customer Success & Engineering to lead technical discovery, deliver demos, and drive successful POCs that win deals.
- Seamless Implementation: Lead implementation for new customers, ensuring they are fully onboarded and confident in using the product to transform their monthly close process.
- Cross-functional Collaboration: Work directly with product and engineering to translate real-world accounting needs into product features and enhancements
- Strategic Growth: As an early team member, you’ll help define Solutions Engineering at Stacks, building playbooks, processes, and eventually future teammates.
🧩 WHAT YOU NEED
- 3–7 Years in Solutions Consulting: You've led technical sales cycles in a SaaS environment, and bring hands-on experience from an accounting or controller background.
- Accounting Domain Knowledge: You’ve worked in or closely with accounting teams, ideally as a Controller, CPA, or someone deeply familiar with the month-end close process, reconciliations, and reporting.
- Customer-Facing Confidence: Comfortable engaging with senior finance leaders and technical stakeholders alike. You know how to listen, challenge assumptions, and earn trust.
- Product Mastery: Quick to understand and explain complex systems. You’re able to turn accounting pain points into clear product solutions.
🚀 WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU
- Foundational role: Help shape a category-defining company from an early stage, working directly with founders and a small, high-agency team.
- Meaningful ownership: Competitive equity in a company scaling rapidly towards $10m ARR, where your impact will directly shape the outcome.
- Cutting-edge product and tech: Work at the intersection of AI and finance, building systems that fundamentally change how companies run their financial close.
- High-calibre team: Collaborate with people from companies like Uber, Plaid, Miro, and Mollie.
- Exceptional workspace: Our London HQ is based in Fora — a modern, design-led space in the heart of the city with access to a gym, classes, and an environment built for focused, in-person building
- Strong team culture: We run regular socials and off-sites that bring the team together properly, we recently have our 2-year anniversary party https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7452732855543259136/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAACQ1TQUB9bCcNVJHhIuwqSi-01DyuyrCVXE in Amsterdam, with board games, a tarot card reader and live music 🎶
🤝 THE HIRING PROCESS
- Step 1: 30-minute screening call with Farid (COO) to discuss your background, motivation, and experience
- Step 2: 30-minute conversation with Mickael (our Solutions Engineer) to dive deeper into your commercial and accounting background
- Step 3: Take-home and 1-hour on-site panel interview with our team at Stacks with Farid (COO) and Naman (Founding Product)
- Step 4: 30-minutes with Albert (our Founder)
- Step 5: Offer!

This role is based out of our Amsterdam office 🇳🇱 or London office 🇬🇧
We are an office-first company & believe great products are made when we are together.
Stacks is building an AI-native platform that reinvents how modern finance teams run the monthly close. The opportunity is massive: every growing company depends on accurate, timely financial data, yet most are still operating with tools and workflows built for a different era.
In just over two years, we've grown from a team of 2 to 50+ and are on a rapid trajectory.
