Join us in shaping the future of the Built World and exponentially accelerate your career in the process. We welcome you to do your life's work here.
ABOUT THE ROLE
Build sells outcomes, not seats. We find and validate the sites and answers our clients need - powered land with confirmed capacity, energisation dates, zoning and title - and deliver them under a single master services agreement. Once that first outcome lands, platform, workflows and services follow under the same agreement, without another procurement round.
We're hiring Account Executives to own that motion end-to-end with data center developers, hyperscalers, energy and institutional real estate investors. You'll open the door with a concrete outcome, close the first deal, and set every customer up to expand within their first 30 days.
This is an IC closer role, not a player-coach seat. Head of Sales owns the number and the team; you own your pipeline and your closes. You'll bring Build's domain experts into the room for technical credibility and delivery, and work with founders on accounts when it helps you win.
WHAT YOU WILL OWN
- New business from first contact to signed contract: outbound, qualification, discovery, proposal, procurement and close
- A pipeline of developers, operators, hyperscalers and institutional investors across digital infrastructure, energy and industrial real estate
- Leading with outcomes: scoping the first validated sites or deliverables and getting the MSA signed
- Expansion: working with customer success on a 30-day plan for every first deal, then landing platform, workflow and services order forms under that MSA
- Forecasting and CRM discipline: every deal, next step and stage kept accurate
- Feeding what buyers ask for, push back on and compare us to into product and GTM
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
- 2–4 years of quota-carrying sales closing multi-stakeholder deals (tech, services, or real estate / infrastructure)
- A track record of hitting or beating quota, not just activity metrics
- Real estate, data center, energy or infrastructure exposure is a strong plus - for example a brokerage, Big 4 real estate advisory, or data center sales
- Comfort selling to senior buyers: heads of acquisitions, development directors, procurement
- An outcome-first, consultative style: you sell the result, not the feature list
- Automation-first mindset and genuine curiosity about AI
- Based in New York or London, and willing to travel to close
WHAT THIS IS NOT
- A volume SDR motion. We don't win deals by sending 500 cold emails.
- A demo-and-hand-off role. There is no handoff at Build: you stay with the customer through the first outcome and the expansion.
HOW TO WIN AT BUILD
Growing Build requires a radically different approach to company building. As a company we're focused on one outcome: winning. That means we move fast, work with intensity, and demand excellence from ourselves. We operate with intensity but create an environment that allows for a lot of fun together. The result is that we're one of the fastest shipping teams in vertical AI, partnering with the best to automate the world around us.
Performance and teamwork are the core of Build's operation. We look for those who are able to do both, who often exhibit a particular ability for;
Velocity: You are relentless in asking the right questions to set direction. Once you find the right direction you go all-in.
Excellence: You obsess with being the best. For you, excellence is a non-negotiable standard rather than an aspiration.
Long time horizons: You choose to be in something for the long run, because that's where most of the returns are realized.
Ownership: You take full ownership of the outcomes. You're meticulous in your pursuits and believe you can actively shape your environment rather than adapt to it.
Customers: You have a passion for the built world and those who shape it. You probably have a quirky hobby or story that relates to your love for building.
Integrity: You chose to do the right thing even when it isn't easy.
Trust: You only work with people you can trust because it's the only way to do truly extraordinary things.
Yield: You have a burning need to see a result on every action you take and you're always looking for routes to do more with less.
WHAT WE OFFER
Radical autonomy, real ownership: High standards. Minimal bureaucracy. You own problems end-to-end, choose how the work gets done, and are accountable for exceptional outcomes. Ownership is matched with meaningful, generous equity.
An accelerated founder's track: Build is for builders. If you want to learn what it actually takes to create a generational company - Product judgment, execution speed, and accountability - there is no faster path than building from zero when everything is for grabs.
Elite teammates, uncompromising bar: You work with people who think clearly, execute relentlessly, and take full ownership. The team you build becomes the company you build. Growth here is not just professional; it reshapes how you operate and in return how Build operates.
Perpetual adventure: We attract the strongest of the strange. Extraordinary experiences are part of the culture - from the food we eat together to the space we occupy. Intensity is intentional.
Shape the built world: We are rebuilding how the physical world gets made. Our software doesn't live in the abstract - it turns into real projects breaking ground because we exist. We work with the largest institutions, push the frontier of AI, and watch our decisions translate directly into the world around us.

ABOUT US
Hawk-Eye Innovations is at the forefront of sports technology, delivering officiating, tracking, broadcast and performance solutions across some of the world's biggest sports. As part of Sony Sports, we continue to push the boundaries of innovation, helping athletes, coaches, teams, broadcasters and governing bodies make better decisions through technology.
BUILD TECHNOLOGY THAT CHANGES HOW SPORT IS EXPERIENCED
What if athletes, coaches and teams could access the kind of tracking technology that has traditionally been out of reach?
We’re building a new generation of tracking services for elite and semi-professional sport, creating products that bring powerful technology to the people who need it most.
We’re looking for a Senior Android Engineer to take ownership of the mobile application at the heart of this experience.
You’ll join a small, cross-functional engineering team building something new, with the opportunity to shape the architecture, influence technical decisions and see your work make a tangible difference. We work with a high degree of autonomy and embrace AI-augmented development to help us build and iterate at pace.
THE ROLE
You’ll own the Android application from architecture and implementation through to release and ongoing reliability. It’s the part of the product that athletes, coaches and teams interact with directly - the application that captures data, coordinates devices, manages sessions and transfers information back to the wider system.
The challenge is making all of this work reliably in the real world.
Our products are often set up and operated by users who have never used them before. They may be working on unreliable internet connections, managing multiple devices and operating in environments we cannot control. That means intuitive setup, clear feedback, resilient data transfer and graceful recovery from failures are fundamental to the product, not features to add later.
You’ll work across the full Android stack, from camera capture and local storage to device-to-device communication, background processing and release management. You’ll also integrate native C++ components developed by our computer vision engineers, helping bring advanced tracking capabilities into a dependable mobile experience.
This is a role for an engineer who enjoys owning complex problems end to end, making thoughtful architectural decisions and building software that works beyond the ideal conditions of a development environment.
WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING
- Own the Android application: Lead the design, architecture and implementation of a production-ready mobile application, taking responsibility for quality, maintainability and performance.
- Build the capture experience: Develop and maintain the camera and media capture layer, including camera configuration, session management, recording and local storage.
- Coordinate connected devices: Build the mechanisms that allow multiple devices and on-site edge units to operate as a single system, including communication, setup, synchronisation, shared state and recovery when connections fail.
- Make unreliable networks manageable: Design robust data and media transfer, with prioritisation, queuing, retries and partial-failure handling built into the application.
- Integrate native components: Connect C++ computer vision components through the Android NDK and JNI, owning the Android application functionality and integration around them.
- Own the release lifecycle: Manage releases across environments, including Google Play submissions, internal testing tracks, remote configuration and release signing.
- Build for reliability in the field: Implement crash reporting, diagnostics and observability so that issues can be understood and resolved without someone needing to be physically present.
- Design for real devices: Account for battery consumption, thermal behaviour, background execution restrictions, permissions and differences across Android versions and device types.
- Collaborate across disciplines: Work closely with backend, design and computer vision engineers, managing dependencies and ensuring the application integrates effectively with the wider system.
- Maintain high engineering standards: Write testable, maintainable code that other engineers can understand, extend and confidently build upon.
- Help the team deliver: Contribute to planning, estimation and task breakdown, identifying risks and dependencies early.
- Build with AI: Use AI-assisted and delegated development tools as a standard part of your workflow, within our security and intellectual property guidelines.
As the team grows, there may also be opportunities to mentor other engineers, take technical leadership of mobile development and establish the standards and practices that shape the discipline.
WHAT YOU’LL BRING
You’re an experienced Android engineer who enjoys taking ownership of an application from the first architectural decisions through to production release.
You understand that great mobile engineering is about more than functionality. It’s about building an experience that remains reliable when devices behave differently, networks drop out and users encounter situations you couldn’t have anticipated.
You’re comfortable working independently, making sound technical decisions and collaborating with engineers outside your specialism. You take pride in delivering production-quality software and are motivated by solving practical problems that have a direct impact on users.
You’ll ideally bring:
- At least 4 years of mobile application development experience, including substantial delivery of native Android applications using Kotlin.
- A portfolio of applications shipped and available on Google Play.
- Experience taking applications through the full development lifecycle, from project creation and architecture to release signing and store approval.
- A degree in a software-related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
- A willingness to learn new technologies, tools and platforms.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
You’ll have expert-level knowledge of:
- Native Android development using Kotlin.
- Device-to-device communication and data serialisation, including technologies such as Wi-Fi Direct and Protocol Buffers.
- Mobile camera and media systems, including capture pipelines, codecs and local storage management.
- Building resilient applications for unreliable networks, including background transfers, queuing, retries and partial-failure handling.
You’ll also be comfortable with:
- Mobile CI/CD and automated release pipelines.
- Writing unit and integration tests.
- Git, code management and code review practices.
- Task and ticket management tools such as Jira.
- Mobile application architecture and design.
- Android device lifecycle constraints, including thermal behaviour, battery usage, background execution limits, permissions…

THE ROLE
You’ll own computer vision on the device, taking detection and tracking models and making them work reliably on consumer Android phones and tablets.
That means much more than getting a model to run. You’ll optimise and profile inference for real-world hardware, balancing performance with accuracy across different devices, lighting conditions and environments. You’ll work close to the camera capture pipeline, where frame timing, exposure and device behaviour can all affect the quality of the output.
Your challenge is to ensure that the data produced on a mobile device is accurate, reliable and trusted by the wider tracking system.

- Solve real-world camera challenges: Work close to the capture pipeline, understanding how frame timing, exposure and camera behaviour influence model performance.
- Make accuracy measurable: Build validation tools and measurement processes that demonstrate performance against ground truth in real-world conditions.
- Engineer for real devices: Account for thermal constraints, battery consumption, hardware differences and the unpredictable conditions encountered in the field.
- Collaborate on model improvements: Work with our computer vision and machine learning specialists to identify, prototype and evaluate improvements to model performance.
- Shape technical decisions: Help determine what should run on-device and what should run elsewhere, bringing clear reasoning and an understanding of technical trade-offs.
- Build production-quality software: Write maintainable, testable and reliable code that meets the team's engineering standards.
- Work across disciplines: Communicate clearly with mobile application, backend and machine learning engineers who depend on your work.
- Build with AI: Use AI-assisted and delegated development tools as a standard part of your workflow, working within our security and intellectual property guidelines.
As the team grows, there may also be opportunities to mentor other engineers, take technical leadership of on-device vision and establish the standards and practices that shape our approach to edge AI.
WHAT YOU’LL BRING
You’re an experienced computer vision or machine learning engineer who enjoys taking algorithms beyond the lab and making them work reliably in production.
You’re comfortable working close to the hardware, investigating problems that don’t show up in controlled environments and making informed trade-offs between accuracy, performance and resource consumption. You can work independently, communicate your thinking clearly and collaborate with engineers across different disciplines.
You’ll ideally bring:
- At least 4 years of applied computer vision or machine learning engineering experience, including solutions deployed into production.
- Demonstrable experience running inference on Android or embedded devices, rather than working exclusively with desktop or server hardware.
- A degree in computer science, engineering, mathematics or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
- A strong interest in learning new technologies, tools and platforms.
Experience in automotive, embedded systems or other resource-constrained environments could be particularly relevant.
TECHNICAL SKILLS

- Mobile or embedded inference runtimes, including model conversion and quantisation toolchains.
- Model optimisation and performance profiling for resource-constrained hardware.
- C++, particularly the Android NDK and JNI.
- Measuring and validating model accuracy against ground truth.
You’ll also be comfortable with:
- Kotlin, with enough experience to work effectively across the JNI boundary.
- Python for prototyping, tooling and data analysis.
- Mobile camera capture pipelines, including frame timing and exposure control.
- Machine learning fundamentals, allowing you to contribute meaningfully to discussions about model improvements.

It would be beneficial to understand:

Our stack includes C++, Android NDK, JNI, Kotlin, Python and AWS, supported by Git, GitHub Actions, Jira and Android mobile inference and profiling tools.

At Inherent, we are on a mission to build AI that recursively self-improves to discover new knowledge. Scientific advances are the backbone of our economic, technological and societal prosperity, but ideas are getting harder to find and breakthroughs are becoming more expensive. We are building a new frontier lab dedicated to developing AI that explores “unknown unknowns” to uncover paradigm-shifting research contributions. Science is a social endeavour, and so our mission is inextricably a human-machine teaming problem. We’re starting by reinventing the AI research factory so that our own agents accelerate their own creation.
Inherent is a well-funded, fast-growing neo-lab backed by Tier 1 VCs who believe in our ethical stance. We are a team of operators with backgrounds at frontier labs who have done foundational work in recursive self-improvement, AI Scientists, world modelling, meta-RL and human-machine cooperation. Working in-person every day at our high-intensity London headquarters, we believe that Europe will lead the way in the coming paradigm of AI-enabled science, unlocking human potential across the globe.
ABOUT THE ROLE
We’re looking for Members of Technical Staff to lead work on post-training state-of-the-art foundation models for open-ended agentic capabilities in scientific research. You’ll be involved at every level of the post-training pipeline: sourcing and creating data, building autocurricula, devising and implementing SFT and RL algorithms, constructing tools and harnesses for foundation model self-improvement, analysing research results, and using information gained to devise future hypotheses. You will work closely with an experienced technical team of humans, and increasingly alongside the AI scientist collaborators we dogfood.
WHAT YOU'D DO
- Design, implement, and tune SFT and RL algorithms to post-train models that autonomously perform state-of-the-art research.
- Build the autocurricula, judges, harnesses and eval pipelines that turn open-ended research tasks into reliable reward signal.
- Run large-scale experiments on state-of-the-art hardware and analyse experiments to determine the next hypotheses to test, in collaboration with our AI agents.
- Close recursive loops so that AI agents drive their own post-training research.
- Work closely with colleagues in the Infrastructure and AI for Science teams to optimise hardware and deliver remarkable performance in real scientific domains.
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
- 3+ years of deep learning research experience.
- Experience post-training large language, vision, video or multi-modal models.
- Demonstrated track record of success in deep learning research, whether papers, model releases, open-source contributions, or other artifacts.
- 5+ years of software engineering experience, including deep familiarity with Python and at least one deep learning framework (e.g., PyTorch, JAX).
- Experience using the latest coding agents, and opinions about optimal workflow.
- Enthusiasm for experimental organizational design.
- AI-pilled: adopting agents, keen to build a company where agents are front and centre.
STRONG CANDIDATES MAY ALSO HAVE
- PhD in mathematics, computer science or hard science discipline.
- Hands-on experience training LLMs with RL at scale (GRPO/PPO, DPO, distillation, and variants).
- Familiarity with distributed and long-context training infrastructure.
- A background in autocurricula, open-endedness, meta-learning, or recursive self-improvement.
- Experience post-training frontier models at an industry lab (scale, infra, and iteration speed).
WHY THIS IS INTERESTING
- You'll shape the core research of a frontier AI lab from the beginning.
- You'll work on genuine recursive self-improvement — training AI scientists that improve the very pipeline that trains them — not incremental benchmark-chasing.
- You'll dogfood your own work: the agents you post-train accelerate the research that creates them.
- Small team, high trust, no bureaucracy, and a genuinely technical culture.
CULTURE
If you believe in our mission and culture, and are qualified and motivated, we encourage you to apply, even if you don’t meet every one of the criteria above. We know that many of the most creative and talented people have had unusual career paths and backgrounds. Building a team with a diversity of thought is mission-critical, for plurality spurs curiosity, invention and collective experimentation.

King’s Cross, London, with international travel · £110,000–£130,000 (flex for the right candidate)
Almost every leap in how we live, from medicine to energy to computing, began with a scientific breakthrough. But breakthroughs are getting harder to find and more expensive to make. We think AI can change that.
As our Talent Architect, you’ll assemble the team that builds Inherent: focusing on high impact researchers and engineers. You’ll do it with total access to our founding team, and you’ll help invent an AI-native way of doing it.
What we’re building
Today’s AI is brilliant at giving good answers. It’s far worse at working out which questions are worth asking, and it still can’t learn on the fly. Yet many of the discoveries that changed the world, like penicillin, X-rays and the microwave oven, came from stumbling into unknown unknowns.
Inherent exists to build AI that can do that: AI that recursively improves itself to discover new knowledge, working alongside human scientists on the hardest problems we face.
Our core bet is that bolting AI onto old ways of working only brings small gains. Electricity didn’t transform industry until factories were redesigned around it, and we think the research lab is no different. So we’re rebuilding ours from scratch. Faraday, our AI scientist, works as a full member of the team. It reads papers, joins meetings, runs experiments, manages compute and even helps with hiring. As Faraday improves, the whole company speeds up, and how humans and agents work together is itself part of our research.
We’re doing this with care. Inherent is a public benefit corporation, and we think hard about the second- and third-order consequences of what we build.
Current state of play
Our founders have been at the frontier of this work for a decade. We’ve brought together a small team of elite researchers, and applications are growing every week.
This year we raised a $50m seed round led by Tier 1 VCs, and we’re growing fast. The next people through the door will decide what this lab becomes, and you’ll be the one who finds them.
What you’ll do
Fundamentally your job is to become one of the most well connected people in frontier AI and scientific R&D, with the freedom and responsibility to build a truly new kind of organization.
- Find people before the market does. Map talent across post-training, AI for science and infrastructure, looking hardest for people others have overlooked.
- Build an elite network. Find and win over exceptional researchers and engineers from top academic and industry labs, the people who rarely look at job ads.
- Represent Inherent around the world. Travel to conferences such as NeurIPS, ICML and ICLR, meet researchers in person, and help run our own dinners, seminars and hackathons.
- Make everyone a talent architect. Build and track referrals across the team, compounding our unique culture of technical excellence, deep commitment to societal benefit, and creative weirdness.
- Keep us fast. Run a pipeline and interview experience that’s quick, thoughtful and that candidates remember for the right reasons.
- Centre the machine. Work with Faraday, our internal agent, and in close collaboration with the “Reinventing the Factory” team to turn hiring into a system that improves itself, so every search, screen and conversation makes the next one better.
Why you’ll want this
Few people early in their careers get to build an AI-native talent function from scratch, working side by side with founders. Here, that’s the job. Every system you build makes you faster, so your reach compounds month on month, much like the agents we’re building. You’ll learn from the people at the frontier of the field, with a path to wider operational leadership as we scale.
What you’ll bring
- A genuine fascination with the future of scientific discovery and why AI could change it.
- Curiosity about AI research: you read papers, follow the labs and want to understand the work.
- New ideas about how to build a world-leading team and its associated brand: we want you to build architecture for talent differently, not to follow a generic playbook.
- Good judgement about people, and a willingness to learn to spot exceptional researchers from a CV, a GitHub profile or a paper trail.
- A passion for uncovering fascinating people: you enjoy finding the person whom few others might have noticed.
- Clear, warm, distinctive writing. Outreach that gets replies because it’s specific, credible and unusual.
- Organisation to keep many conversations moving without dropping a thread.
- Ability to coordinate distinctive, tasteful events that reflect Inherent’s intellectual ethos.
- Discretion with sensitive information about candidates, pay and company plans.
- You already use AI to multiply your time, and want to push that much further.
- A desire to participate in and build a culture that values weirdness, creativity, artistic excellence, scientific precision, hard work and kindness.
It helps if you’ve done some recruiting or sourcing, studied or worked in a scientific or technical field, or built a community around something you care about. But none of this is essential. We’d rather hire someone sharp and mission-driven early than someone experienced and indifferent.
Worth knowing
We’re in person every day in King’s Cross, the pace is high, and there’s no playbook for hiring. You’ll travel regularly for conferences and events. If you want a well-oiled process to run, this isn’t it. If you want to build one, it is.
Apply
If that sounds like you, apply, even if you don’t tick every box. Some of the best people we know took strange routes to get here.

ABOUT THE ROLE

- Partner with our strategy and creative production teams so paid and creator work are planned together, not bolted on
- Track platform and channel changes and tell us what to do differently because of them
WHAT YOU'LL BRING
- 5+ years in digital paid media, in-house or agency-side, with deep hands-on ownership of TikTok and Meta
- AI Savvy, experience using AI in your workflow (Claude preferred).
- A track record of improving campaign performance through analysis you did yourself — you can walk us through a specific example
- Experience managing paid budgets of $1M+ and being accountable for the outcome
- High proficiency in Excel and strong numeracy — you're comfortable being the person who checks the maths
- The judgement to make a call that affects client performance and defend it clearly
- Real attention to detail on the administrative side: reporting accuracy, budget tracking, and campaign hygiene
- Comfort working with clients and teams across multiple countries and time zones
NICE TO HAVE
- Experience mentoring or line-managing a junior paid media hire
- Background working directly with creators or on creator-led paid social

We’re on a mission to protect society from fraud and money laundering. We’ve already protected over 3 million people through life’s big transactions.
Fraud and regulation are rising, costing the UK economy over £100bn every year; this makes it more difficult for businesses to protect themselves and their clients - individuals like you and me - from fraud and money laundering.
Our co-founders Olly and Jack were led to this area when a friend was defrauded of £25K when buying their first property. At the time, anti-fraud technology didn’t exist, which meant that completing the anti-fraud checks required in these processes was largely manual. These big life moments should be exciting, but instead are often confusing and scary due to the painful process of completing these paper-based checks and the risk of fraud.
Thirdfort helps businesses to facilitate these anti fraud checks so that individuals know they can transact safely and seamlessly with professionals during these big transactions. Our anti-fraud platform provides a secure way for professionals in regulated sectors like Lawyers, Estate Agents and Accountants to transfer funds and verify sensitive information through app based document checks, facial recognition and open banking.
Over 1,500 businesses now trust Thirdfort to verify their clients. We are FCA regulated and have raised over $33m in capital from leading Fintech investors Breega and Element Ventures, as well as the founders of Zoopla, Funding Circle, Comply Advantage, Tessian, Fenergo and Fidel.
About the role:
This AI Operations role sits within TechOps. TechOps at Thirdfort enables teams to do their best work by building reliable, secure internal systems and processes, and increasingly, by using AI and automation to remove manual effort at scale.
We're looking for someone who has already built and run automations in a real business and can own meaningful work end-to-end. You'll scope problems with the teams who have them, ship working solutions yourself, and keep them running. We're looking for a creative, adaptable teammate to help shape how we operate and build a secure, scalable tech foundation for the future.

As Marqeta’s Senior Account Executive based in London, you will lead the expansion and scaling of our most impactful partnerships across larger Fintech, Financial Institution, banking, and embedded finance businesses. This highly strategic role requires a critical, pre-existing understanding of the entire payments ecosystem, particularly the issuing side, to successfully navigate complex business and technical engagements.
The European Sales team at Marqeta is looking to expand our sales footprint in Europe to focus on some of the largest and most impactful commercial opportunities in Marqeta’s evolving business.
The customers in focus include all traditional and digital banking organisations, as well as large scale fintechs, fintech innovators and companies who are looking to take control of and expand their card programme offerings to their customer base - essentially those looking for solutions to launch, scale and continuously evolve their banking products and services.
This exciting role is ideal for individuals seeking to go deep in all aspects of complex business and technical engagements and will span multiple areas of development:
- Cultivating and managing relationships with executives and entrepreneurs seeking to innovate and disrupt B2B & consumer payments;
- Working closely with internal stakeholders in Product, Legal, Compliance and Delivery to define solutions that will empower our customers;
- Originating new customer opportunities, responding to inbound opportunities, and shepherding deals from opening through to contract and closing stage.
Key to this role is an ability to deeply understand and articulate Marqeta's technology and how it brings value to the market, expertly communicate its benefits, and win the trust of the key stakeholders across revenue growth, product and technology teams of our potential partners.
PLEASE NOTE: This is a hybrid role and requires employees to be based within 35 miles of our London office. You will be expected to work on-site two days a week, on Tuesday and Thursday, with the flexibility to work remotely on the other days.

You will also be responsible for partnering with your team to grow existing accounts and managing opportunities across various stages in Salesforce.

- Experience in launching and scaling products or services in new markets, ideally within the UK

ABOUT US
Pliant is a modular B2B payments platform combining commercial card issuing, payment accounts, FX and spend management for businesses and AI agents.
Businesses across travel, e-commerce, insurance and AI-native technology use Pliant to manage complex payment workflows, while fintechs, software platforms and banks use its infrastructure to build and operate their own commercial payment offerings.
Pliant's API-first platform also enables AI agents and applications to access regulated payment infrastructure with permissions, controls and auditability built in.
Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Berlin, Pliant serves businesses and partners across Europe and North America. A principal member of Visa and Mastercard, Pliant issues commercial cards in 13 currencies across 32 countries under its European e-money license and through regulated partners in the UK and US.
Learn more at www.getpliant.com http://www.getpliant.com.
ABOUT THE ROLE
As Senior Manager Operational Risk (m/f/d), you own the design and operation of the operational risk framework for the UK entity and make sure it meets Pliant’s risk appetite and FCA expectations for a card-issuing e-money business.
This role is based in the UK remote but if you are based in London, our office is open for you to work in.
WHAT YOU’LL DO
Operational Risk Framework & Governance
• Maintain and improve the operational risk framework (risk appetite, risk taxonomy, policies,
RCSA, KRIs, loss event and near-miss data, scenario analysis).
• Make sure governance and controls meet Pliant’s minimum standards, FCA requirements on
systems and controls (SYSC) and the e-money and payment services conduct and prudential
requirements.
• Provide regular, decision-oriented risk reporting to UK management, the UK Board and the
Group Risk Committee.
• Advise on operational risk implications of new products, partners, markets and material
changes (change risk assessments, new-product approval).
Safeguarding & Core E-Money / Payments Processes
• Oversee operational risk in the safeguarding of customer funds: reconciliations, account
structure, third-party safeguarding providers, breaks and escalation, in line with the FCA’s
safeguarding requirements.
• Assess end-to-end risks across the card programme (issuing, authorisation, clearing and
settlement, chargebacks, fraud, scheme rule compliance with Visa and processors).
• Challenge the First Line on process, control and capacity risks as the business scales.
Incident Management & Regulatory Reporting
• Own the incident management framework for operational and ICT/security incidents:
classification, escalation, root cause analysis, remediation tracking.
• Make sure major operational and security incidents are assessed and reported to the FCA
within the required timelines (PSRs 2017 incident reporting).
• Run post-incident reviews and feed the lessons learned back into the control framework.
Operational Resilience
• Lead the operational resilience programme under SYSC 15A: identify Important Business
Services, set and test impact tolerances, run scenario testing, map dependencies and
maintain the self-assessment.
• Oversee business continuity, disaster recovery and exit/wind-down planning, including
alignment of RTO/RPO with impact tolerances.
Outsourcing & Third-Party Risk
• Own the third-party and outsourcing risk framework in line with the FCA’s outsourcing
requirements (SYSC 8 and the FCA’s guidance for payment services and e-money firms),
including intra-group outsourcing to Pliant GmbH.
• Run due diligence and ongoing monitoring of critical vendors (processors, cloud and banking
partners), including exit plans and contractual requirements.
• Prepare and maintain material outsourcing notifications to the FCA.
Regulatory Engagement & Assurance
• Act as the day-to-day contact for the FCA on operational risk topics, in coordination with the
senior management and the Compliance/MLRO function.
• Support regulatory reviews, audits and certification audits; track findings through to closure.
• Support the annual review of the risk framework and the regulatory returns that depend on
operational risk data.
Culture & Training
• Embed a strong risk culture; deliver training on incident reporting, operational resilience and
risk ownership.
WHAT YOU’LL BRING
• Degree in Risk Management, Finance, Information Systems or a related field (or equivalent
experience).
• 5+ years in operational risk in payments, e-money, banking or fintech, ideally in an FCA-
regulated EMI or PI.
• Solid knowledge of the UK regulatory framework for e-money and payments: EMRs, PSRs
2017, SYSC, operational resilience, safeguarding and outsourcing requirements.
• Hands-on experience with RCSA, KRIs, incident management and resilience testing.
• Ability to challenge the First Line constructively and to report clearly to senior management
and regulators.
• Experience working with distributed teams across the UK and Germany
NICE TO HAVE
• CRISC, CISM, ISO 22301 or ISO 27001 Lead Implementer/Auditor.
• Experience with card scheme (Visa/Mastercard) rules and PCI DSS.
• Familiarity with DORA (relevant for the EU group entities).
• German or another European language

🏢 Who We Are
SINGU was founded on the belief that true success in real estate comes from continuous innovation. Our vision is to lead Europe in delivering cutting-edge software for facility management, maintenance, and ESG compliance.
SINGU is one of the fastest-growing PropTech companies in Europe. Today, our platform manages over 250 million square metres of real estate for 2500+ clients across 40 countries, helping property managers digitalise and automate their operations, from maintenance to portfolio management.
SINGU Group now brings together several European businesses (Micad by SINGU, Singu Germany, QRMaint, and Synbiotix), with teams in Poland, Cyprus, the UK, and the DACH region, and more acquisitions on the way.
We are a dynamic, forward-thinking organisation where adaptability, collaboration, trust and ambition drive how we work. We put our clients at the heart of everything we do, and we make sure to have fun along the way.
🎯 About the Role
This is the first in-house legal role in SINGU’s history. You will build the legal function from the ground up and become the day-to-day owner of legal risk across the Group, working closely with the Group CFO.
Today, legal work is handled by a mix of external firms across several jurisdictions. That model served us well at an earlier stage, but it does not scale for a multi-country group that is moving upmarket into enterprise deals and acquiring companies continuously.
We are looking for a commercially minded Legal Counsel who likes getting deals done. Someone who knows our commercial position well enough to negotiate hard and fast, who can bring order to our contract suite and governance, and who sees M&A, compliance and people law as part of one connected job.
The role goes well beyond working through a queue of document requests. Together with the Group CFO, you will shape the legal strategy, design how the business works with legal, and personally lead the most important matters.
📍 Location: London, Warsaw, or Kraków, hybrid (regular office presence), with occasional travel to other locations.
🧭 Reporting line: Group CFO. You will work closely with the Executive Leadership Team and support the Board.
👥 Team: Initially a team of one, managing a panel of external counsel across jurisdictions, with scope to build a small legal team as the Group grows.
💼 What You’ll Do
You will own your work and be accountable for results. In practice, this means:
1. Commercial contracts & deal support
- Own the customer contract suite – take full ownership of our customer-facing legal documents (MSA, Order Form, DPA, EULA, EU Data Act Addendum, Security Policy, SOW and Supplemental T&Cs) and make them complete, consistent and easy for Sales to use.
- Negotiate enterprise deals – lead redlines and negotiations on larger and more complex deals, protecting our commercial position (e.g. billing and implementation triggers, liability, service scope, payment terms) while shortening sales cycles.
- Build a contract governance model – define document ownership, approval rights, negotiation limits and fallback positions, version control, and a review cadence, and decide clearly what is Group-standard and what is country-specific.
- Localise for our markets – deliver compliant local versions where required, starting with Germany (German MSA, EULA, DPA addendum, Order Form, SOW and Security Policy).
- Support bids and procurement – provide legal input on tenders, public and enterprise procurement requirements, and customer security and compliance questionnaires.
- Handle day-to-day agreements – NDAs, partner, supplier and vendor contracts (including HR and technology vendors), and third-party liaison, mostly through templates and playbooks that the business can use on its own.
2. M&A and integration
- Support legal for our buy-and-build M&A model – lead legal due diligence, deal structuring, transaction documents and negotiations on acquisitions, working with our investors, Finance and external advisers.
- Own post-close legal integration – align contracts, entities, software licensing agreements and policies of acquired businesses with Group standards.
- Secure the people side of deals – together with People & Culture, make sure employees of acquired companies land on the right contracts, pay and benefits, and that any restructuring or redundancy process is legally sound in every jurisdiction.
- Build a repeatable playbook – so every transaction is faster, cheaper and more consistent than the last.
3. Compliance, data protection & regulatory
- Own a coherent compliance framework – across UK and EU GDPR, the EU Data Act, sector-specific data handling for enterprise clients, and other obligations, resolving overlaps and conflicts between regimes.
- Be the single legal owner of data protection – including employee data, working with the Data Protection / IT Security lead and People & Culture; oversee DSARs, data processing terms and security commitments made to customers.
- Horizon-scan and keep leadership informed – track changes in Polish, EU, UK and German law that affect the business, flag them early, and give the ELT and Board regular, clear legal updates.
- Manage disputes and exposure – handle pre-litigation, litigation and regulatory matters proactively, with the right external support.
4. Employment & people law
- Be the legal partner to People & Culture – across Poland, the UK and DACH, covering employment contracts, settlement agreements, formal complaints and grievances, ACAS and other employment disputes, and threatened legal action.

About SINGU
At SINGU, we’re redefining how the world’s most ambitious real estate companies run their operations. Our mission is to become Europe’s leading platform for managing warehouse, logistics, retail, and multi-site commercial real estate portfolios — empowering our Clients to protect revenue, boost efficiency, and unlock new value across every aspect of their business.
Our unified CAFM platform already powers the daily operations of over 250 million m² of real estate worldwide, supporting more than 500,000 professionals. Following our union with the UK’s Micad and Germany’s net-haus, we now help manage 100,000+ buildings across 35+ countries — and we’re just getting started.
Backed by a leading growth equity investor, we’re scaling rapidly and partnering with global leaders such as Prologis, ECE, CTP, Hillwood, Logicor, GLP, and Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield. As we continue to grow through strategic acquisitions and bold innovation, we stay true to our core values: adaptability, collaboration, and client focus.
If you’re ready to help build Europe’s leading platform for property operations — and make a tangible impact on how the real estate industry works — join SINGU and be part of this transformation.
THE OPPORTUNITY
This is a new-logo role. You'll win large warehousing, logistics and industrial property owners, operators and FM organisations across the UK that don't work with us yet. You'll run the full sales cycle, from the first cold conversation to signature. Once an account goes live, Customer Success takes it from there.
You'll work a defined UK territory of named target accounts. You'll have reference customers that carry real weight in the supply chain sector, and direct access to the CRO and CEO, who will join your deals when it matters.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
Build your own pipeline
- Build and work a named list of target accounts across UK warehousing, logistics and industrial real estate, with a clear view of why each one should change and what it would take.
- Generate most of your own pipeline. Business development and marketing will help, but you're the hunter.
- Reach C-suite and operational leaders through outbound, industry networks, events, partners and existing customer relationships.
Win complex enterprise deals
- Run the full cycle: discovery, business case, evaluation, negotiation and signature.
- Replace incumbent CAFM/IWMS platforms, in-house systems and spreadsheet-based processes.
- Navigate buying groups, procurement, IT security and legal without losing momentum.
- Qualify rigorously with MEDDICC and use mutual action plans on every live deal.
- Shape the commercial structure of each deal: pricing, multi-year terms, phased rollouts and land-and-expand entry points.
Lead with the business case
- Earn access to CFOs, COOs, CIOs, Heads of Real Estate and operations leaders.
- Sell on operating cost, compliance exposure, portfolio performance and risk, not on a feature demo.
- Bring in Presales, Product and executive sponsors on the deals that justify it.
Forecast with discipline
- Keep a forecast you can defend line by line and a CRM that reflects reality.
- Disqualify early and visibly. Time spent on a real deal is worth more than a pipeline that only looks full.
- Share competitive and market insight with product, marketing and pricing.
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
- A true hunter. You've built a career winning new logos, not managing existing accounts.
- 5+ years in B2B software sales, at an established, credible software business.
- Enterprise deal experience. You've closed complex six-figure deals with multiple stakeholders, procurement and IT security reviews. This isn't high-volume transactional sales.
- Sector knowledge in warehousing, logistics, industrial or supply chain, or in facilities management software. If your background is in commercial real estate, we'd want to see a very strong sales track record.
- A track record you can walk us through. What you sold, to whom, how you got in, and what you said. We value an honest career story over polished numbers. If you've had a quarter or a year that didn't go to plan, we want to hear what you did about it.
- C-level credibility. You can build a business case and defend it in front of a finance audience.
- MEDDICC or a similar qualification framework, used in practice.
- Understanding of the UK market, and the energy to build something as the new-business team grows.
WHAT WE OFFER
- Base salary, uncapped commission and accelerators.
- Dedicated Solution Consulting, BD support and marketing programmes aimed at your segment.
- A real path into enterprise sales leadership as the team scales.
- Remote working, with roughly monthly time together in London or Birmingham.
LOGISTICS
- Location: UK, remote (England or Wales preferred)
- Travel: roughly monthly to London or Birmingham
- Employment type: Full-time
If this role sounds like a good fit, we’d love to hear from you. Apply and help us build technology that supports critical operations every day.

SENIOR C++ SOFTWARE ENGINEER
Remote (UK-based) | Full-Time
ABOUT US
Reactive Markets is the 2026 OTC Trading Platform of the Year (Risk.net http://Risk.net). Our network handles over $75 billion in daily trading volumes across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency, connecting 60+ of the world's leading liquidity providers.
We build trading systems that operate at the edge of what's technically possible — where nanoseconds matter and a dropped message costs real money. Our engineering team is small, senior, and deeply invested in the craft of building cutting edge, reliable, high-performance systems.
THE ROLE
We're looking for a Senior C++ Software Engineer who can shape the technical direction of our Switchboard trading platform while continuing to write excellent code. You'll work on the most performance-critical components — pricing engines, connectivity gateways, market-data systems, and the messaging layer that ties them together — and you'll have a direct influence on architectural decisions that affect the entire platform.
This is not a role where you write code and throw it over a wall. You build it, you test it, you deploy it, you support it in production, and you improve it. Our engineers own the full lifecycle — from design through to operational excellence. When something breaks at 4pm on a Friday, you're part of the team that investigates and fixes it.
Beyond your own delivery, you'll provide technical oversight across the team — reviewing designs, challenging assumptions, and mentoring engineers who are earlier in their careers. You'll help us maintain the quality bar that our clients depend on, and you'll contribute to the architectural decisions that determine how well our platform scales.
Occasional hours outside the normal working day are required for production releases, scheduled maintenance windows, and Level 3 support during critical incidents. We keep this to a minimum and recognise the commitment — but owning a production trading platform means being there when it matters.
WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON
- Modern C++20 and Go on Linux — a modern software stack based on open source
- Cloud-native infrastructure on AWS with colocation in key data centres
- Microsecond-level latency optimisation and high-throughput messaging
- Market-data and reference-data pipelines across multiple asset classes
- FIX protocol integrations with global banks and liquidity providers
- Observability and monitoring — dashboards, alerting, and metrics that make system behaviour visible
- Production systems that handle real money — reliability is not optional
- Architectural oversight — solution design, peer reviews, and technical direction for platform components
- Mentorship — helping junior and mid-level engineers develop their skills, improve their code, and grow into stronger contributors
WHAT WE NEED
Technical:
- Strong C++ with Linux systems programming (5+ years)
- Comfortable working close to the metal — you understand what's underneath your code
- Proven track record of optimising complex, latency-sensitive systems — you can profile, diagnose, and fix performance problems methodically
- Deep understanding of distributed systems architecture and network protocols (TCP/UDP, socket programming, FIX)
- Experience with system design and architectural trade-offs — you've made decisions that stuck and lived with the consequences
- Go experience is a strong bonus — we use Go extensively for microservices and command-line tooling, and you'll be expected to work with it internally. If you don't know it yet, strong C++ engineers pick it up quickly
- Python for scripting, automation, testing, and data analysis — used across the platform for tooling and operational workflows
- Git and shell scripting
- Experience in financial services or trading technology is a plus but not essential
How you work:
- You ship. You're delivery-focused — you iterate, you improve, you get things into production
- You own it. When you build something, you take responsibility for its behaviour in production. You respond to incidents (15-minute acknowledgement SLA during working hours), investigate issues, and close the loop
- You raise the bar. You conduct thoughtful peer reviews, challenge designs constructively, and hold the team to high standards without slowing it down
- You mentor. You invest in the engineers around you — sharing knowledge, pairing on hard problems, and helping people grow. You make the team better, not just the code
- You write things down. Documentation is not an afterthought — it's how we scale knowledge across a distributed team. If it's not written down, it doesn't exist
- You communicate. We're a distributed team across multiple time zones. Clear, proactive communication — especially when things go wrong — is essential
- You care about quality. You write clean, testable code. You review your peers' work thoughtfully. You push for continuous improvement without gold-plating
- You embrace AI tooling. We use AI tools (Claude, Gemini) to amplify our engineering capability — from code review and debugging to incident investigation and documentation. You don't need to be an expert, but you should be curious and willing to learn
WHAT YOU GET
- Real problems — trading systems where performance is measured in microseconds, not user clicks
- Technical influence — direct input into architectural decisions, solution design, and the technical direction of the platform
- An excellent team — senior engineers who care about craft, collaborate openly, and hold each other to high standards
- Ownership — small teams, clear accountability, direct impact on the platform and our clients
- Competitive package — up to 30 days leave + bank holidays, private health insurance, pension, life insurance, dental/optical cashback, cycle to work, socials and offsites
- Remote-friendly — work from home with flexibility. We trust our people to deliver
- Sustainable pace — we work hard, but we don't burn people out. Balance is how we stay sharp
- Growth — career progression to lead roles, performance specialisation, or technical leadership. We invest in people who invest in us
We believe in transparency, honest feedback, and writing things down. We celebrate delivery, not activity. We frame AI as empowering people — removing toil, amplifying capability, enabling higher-value work.
We aim to build systems that don't depend on the heroics of individuals to maintain and support — systems and processes that are resilient, documented, and sustainable.

Format: Video call, ~30-45 minutes
Stage 2: Hiring Manager Conversation with the relevant team lead or hiring manager
Format: Video call, ~60 minutes
Stage 3: Technical Interview with two members of the relevant engineering team
Format: Video call, interactive session, ~60 minutes

We're building genuinely AI-enabled tooling to support this function — so this role is less about arriving with a decade of FIX expertise already committed to memory, and much more about someone sharp, adaptable, and genuinely curious who can use that tooling to go further, faster, and think proactively about how the process itself should keep improving.

FIX Onboarding & Integrations:
- Lead and manage FIX client onboarding projects — from initial requirements gathering through certification and production go-live.
- Configure, test, and validate FIX sessions, including order routing, execution reporting, and market data flows.
- Coordinate conformance testing and certification with clients to ensure compliance with platform standards.
- Document onboarding procedures, client configurations, and integration best practices.
- Leverage internal AI and automation tools to streamline client onboarding and troubleshooting — including tooling built specifically for this function, giving you a genuine head start on deep process knowledge.
- Collaborate with engineering and product teams to support new FIX workflows, APIs, and client integration initiatives.
Client Services:
- Serve as frontline technical support for clients in EMEA across FX and equities business lines.
- Build and maintain strong client relationships, ensuring timely and transparent communication addressing their needs and queries with professionalism and efficiency.

- Manage client inquiries, troubleshoot workflow or configuration issues, and coordinate resolutions across internal teams.

- 2-5 years of experience in a client onboarding, integration, or technical support role within financial technology, trading, or brokerage.

- Familiarity with FX and Equities trading environments, order lifecycle management, and market data connectivity — genuine interest in working across multiple asset classes rather than staying within one.
- A genuinely proactive, tech-first mindset — someone who treats our AI and automation tooling as a way to go further and faster, not a replacement for good judgement, and who naturally looks for ways to improve a process rather than simply following it.
- Excellent communication and organisational skills, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple onboarding/client projects in parallel.
Nice-to-have:
- Experience with OMS/EMS platforms, liquidity aggregators, or trading system integrations.
- Exposure to other API protocols and architectures (REST, WebSocket) — relevant given the depth of our own API.
- Scripting or automation experience (e.g. Python) and familiarity with monitoring tools (Splunk, Grafana, or similar).
- Understanding of financial market structure and post-trade workflows.
WHAT YOU GET
- A genuinely rich API to work with — not a thin FIX wrapper bolted onto a legacy system. You'll onboard clients onto an API with real depth across order routing, execution reporting, and market data — the kind of platform where understanding the protocol properly actually matters.
- Breadth across FX, Equities, and digital assets — most FIX/onboarding roles sit inside a single asset class. Here you'll build knowledge across all three, at a network connecting 40+ liquidity providers — exposure that compounds faster than a single-product environment.
- Real ownership of the tech-to-business bridge — you're not just configuring sessions, you're the person translating FIX/API detail into client outcomes clients actually care about. That combination — technical credibility plus commercial judgement, is the actual shape of this role.
- A genuinely tech-first operation — we've built dedicated AI tooling for this function specifically, so your ramp-up is faster and your day-to-day is spent on the client and integration problems that need real judgement, not repetitive configuration work.
- A small, senior team — you'll work directly alongside Client Services, TechOps, and engineering, with real visibility into how the platform works end to end, not a large layer of process between you and the people who built it.
- Growth across the business — the skills this role builds (protocol depth, client-facing technical credibility, cross-asset exposure) are the same ones that open doors internally.
- Competitive package — up to 30 days leave + bank holidays, private health insurance, pension, life insurance, dental/optical cashback, cycle to work, socials and offsites

Remote (UK-based), with occasional on-site work at our data centres | Full-Time
ABOUT US
Reactive Markets is the 2026 OTC Trading Platform of the Year (Risk.net http://Risk.net). Our network handles over $75 billion in daily trading volumes across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency, connecting 60+ of the world’s leading liquidity providers.
We build trading systems that operate at the edge of what’s technically possible — where nanoseconds matter and a dropped message costs real money. Our engineering team is small, senior, and deeply invested in the craft of building cutting edge, reliable, high-performance systems.
THE ROLE
We’re looking for a Senior Infrastructure Engineer to help run and grow the network and cloud estate behind our trading platform. Networking in our colocation data centres is the core of the role. The estate spans London, New York and Singapore, and from Q1 2027 a new Tokyo data centre.
This is a hands-on role in a small, expert infrastructure team. You’ll work closely with our Head of Infrastructure, following problems from the cross-connect through hosts, containers and AWS. You’ll also help keep infrastructure delivery on track, from timelines and reporting to working closely with our TechOps team.
WHAT YOU’LL WORK ON
- Low-latency networking across our colocation sites: switching and routing, cross-connects, BGP peering with liquidity providers and clients, and the fabric that carries our trading traffic
- Bringing new sites to application-ready, starting with Tokyo
- Our hybrid connectivity into multi-region AWS, including Direct Connect, routing and failover
- Linux hosts and containers on the critical path, with every change made through code (Ansible, Git, Terraform), never by hand
- Monitoring and alerting that catches problems before clients do, plus runbooks and post-incident reviews that someone else can follow
- Planning and capacity: forecasting growth, setting timelines and reporting progress to TechOps and engineering
WHAT WE NEED
- 4+ years running production infrastructure in a latency-sensitive environment, such as HFT, an exchange, market data or bank trading infrastructure
- Strong networking: hands-on routing and switching (MLAG, LACP, VLANs), BGP in production, and a solid grasp of low-latency behaviour such as buffers, microbursts and congestion handling
- Colocation experience: cabinets, cross-connects, remote hands and vendor management
- Solid Linux (RHEL) and TCP/IP, and the ability to trace a problem from the wire to the application
- Infrastructure as code and containers as your default way of working
- Working knowledge of AWS networking, and the confidence to pick up the rest of our stack. Networking depth matters more to us than any particular cloud or platform tooling
- Methodical, evidence-led troubleshooting and clear documentation
A strong plus:
- Project management experience: owning timelines, reporting progress, and working with ops teams to hit deadlines
- Kernel bypass (Onload/ef_vi), PTP and time synchronisation
- Experience bringing up a new colo site
- FIX protocol or OTC FX market knowledge
- Python for tooling
Working pattern: Infrastructure changes are often scheduled outside trading hours, including weekends, and the team shares an on-call rota. We’re a team with flexible hours, so time worked out of hours is taken back during the week. Day-to-day work is remote, with occasional visits to our data centres, most often in London (Slough).

- Real ownership of a live global trading network, hands-on, with few layers of process

- A senior seat in a small, expert team where your changes ship and are measured

At SiteMinder, we believe our success comes from our people. We build diverse, inclusive teams where different voices, backgrounds and perspectives are valued. Our differences drive innovation for our customers, and our people bring the ideas, expertise and energy that help us keep moving forward. We’re better together.
What We Do...
Right now, somewhere in the world, a hotel is taking a booking or increasing their revenue through technology you could help build. SiteMinder is the world’s leading hotel commerce platform. For more than 20 years, we’ve helped hotels attract guests, maximise revenue, forecast demand and perform at their best. Today, our platform supports 56,000+ hotels in 150+ countries, connects to 3,000+ partners and powers more than 140m reservations and AU$85 billion+ in hotel revenue each year.
That’s the kind of impact your work can have here. You’ll solve meaningful challenges with AI, simplify complexity and build solutions that help hotels perform. Supported by clear purpose, a strong platform and teams who care about what they’re building, you’ll have the opportunity to shape the future of an industry that never stands still.
Ready to Shake Up the Hotel World?
Forget boring sales jobs. We're on a mission to help hotel owners ditch the admin headaches and get back to doing what they love – being great hosts. That’s where you come in.
As a Sales Executive at SiteMinder, you'll be a hero to small and medium-sized hoteliers. You'll connect with them, understand their challenges, and show them how our game-changing tech can transform their business, boost their revenue, and simplify their lives. You're not just selling software; you're selling a solution you can believe in.
Worried about being thrown in the deep end? Don't be.
We invest in you, big time. You'll kick things off with a month-long training and onboarding program that will make you an expert on our products and the industry. From day one, you'll have a dedicated sales coach, a buddy, and a team leader in your corner, all cheering you on and helping you smash your goals.
Your Mission!
- Become a Deal Hunter: Uncover new opportunities and show our existing customers some love with killer upsells.
- Smash Your Targets: Drive sales from start to finish and celebrate the wins with the team.
- Wow & Win: Craft proposals that impress and negotiate contracts where everyone walks away happy.
- Keep it Clean: Maintain your pipeline in our CRM (a tidy pipeline is a happy pipeline!).
- Be the Voice: Channel client feedback straight to our product gurus to make our tech even better.
What we need from you:
- Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) sales experience would be brilliant but a passion to sell is the key to this role.
- Fluent in English (written and spoken)
- A confident phone presence, fearlessness in leading meetings with prospects, and great listening skills
- Strong verbal skills to communicate professionally with customers, in writing and over the phone
- Self-motivation and resilience to show up each day and give your best
Our Perks & Benefits…
- Equity packages for you to be a part of the SiteMinder journey
- Hybrid working model (3 days per week at our London Hammersmith office)
- Mental health and well-being initiatives
- Generous parental (including secondary) leave policy
- Paid birthday, study and volunteering leave every year
- Sponsored social clubs, team events, and celebrations
- Employee Resource Groups (ERG) to help you connect and get involved
- Investment in your personal growth offering training for your advancement
Think this role sounds like you? If so, we’d love to hear from you. Please send us your resume and our Talent Acquisition team will be in touch.
When you apply, feel free to share your pronouns and let us know if you need any adjustments during the interview process, we’re here to support you. We also warmly encourage applications from people from underrepresented backgrounds.

About the role
Teza is a systematic trading firm developing quantitative strategies across multiple asset classes. We are looking for a Lead Infrastructure Engineer to own the platform that supports our traders, quants, and developers. This includes colocation hardware near the exchanges, research compute and developer services, and the security and release processes that connect these environments.
This is a player-coach role. You will lead the infrastructure team, which includes DevOps Engineers and Infrastructure Engineers, and set its technical direction while remaining hands-on. You will provision and tune bare-metal trading servers, respond to production incidents, and review the designs and solutions your team delivers.
We are not looking for a manager who delegates all technical work or an engineer who avoids leading people. We need someone who can do both and determine where their time and attention are most needed.
Our platform supports active trading and research today, and we are investing in making it more robust, observable, secure, and developer-friendly. You will have significant ownership and decision-making over infrastructure tooling, standards, and priorities across the firm.
Location:
Austin, Texas (On-Site)
What You'll Own:
- Trading Infrastructure and Colocation. Oversee server procurement and lifecycle management across multiple exchange colocations. Select low-latency NICs, such as Solarflare, Exanic, and Mellanox, and kernel-bypass technologies. Develop and maintain Linux tuning standards for trading hosts, including CPU isolation, NUMA-aware pinning, IRQ affinity, and BIOS and kernel settings. Manage hardware failures, spare capacity, and capacity planning.
- Research and Developer Platform. Oversee compute orchestration for researchers and data engineers, including Slurm for HPC, machine learning, and GPU workloads; Hadoop for batch processing; and Airflow for workflow scheduling. Support shared services such as JupyterHub, databases, artifact storage, and large-dataset storage. Determine when Kubernetes is appropriate and when alternative approaches are better suited.
- Security. Establish and maintain access controls for production trading hosts in colocation. Manage network segmentation across colocation, corporate, and research environments. Oversee secrets management for exchange credentials, API keys, and certificates, including rotation, auditing, and deployment integration. Lead vulnerability management, patching for systems that cannot be routinely rebooted, intrusion detection, and incident response.
- Releases and Deployment. Define how trading strategies, data pipelines, and real-time trading systems move from development into production. Establish rollback procedures and release processes for infrastructure changes, including kernels, firmware, and NIC drivers. Oversee infrastructure-as-code pipelines and coordinate releases with the trading calendar.
- Operational Maturity. Establish the on-call model and escalation paths. Improve observability across internal services through metrics, logging, tracing, and alerting. Lead incident response and blameless post-mortems, ensuring action items are tracked and completed.
- Hybrid Infrastructure. Oversee colocation infrastructure for trading, along with on-premises and cloud environments supporting research and corporate workloads. Evaluate the tradeoffs between these environments, manage cloud costs, and establish disaster recovery plans with defined recovery time objectives (RTOs) and recovery point objectives (RPOs).
- The Team. Hire, develop, and retain infrastructure engineers. Set priorities across trading performance and latency, research compute needs, and operational tooling. Represent the infrastructure team and its priorities across the firm.
What We're Building Toward:
These are the shared goals of the infrastructure team. DevOps Engineers and Infrastructure Engineers execute against them, while you set the technical approach, establish priorities, and drive progress.
- Full-stack observability across internal services, including unified metrics, centralized logging, distributed tracing, and actionable alerting.
- Reliable, self-service compute orchestration across Slurm, Hadoop, and Airflow, enabling researchers and data engineers to run workloads at scale without unnecessary infrastructure bottlenecks.
- Mature secrets management for trading credentials, API keys, certificates, and service-to-service authentication, with rotation, auditing, and deployment integration.
- Unified release pipelines that standardize how trading strategies, data pipelines, and real-time trading systems move from development to production.
- A well-maintained platform foundation that includes identity management, GitHub Actions runners, VPN, and observability tooling, with updates delivered safely and without disrupting active trading.
- A strong security posture across production and research environments, with security practices that evolve alongside the platform rather than being added after the fact.
Basic Requirements:
- Experience operating infrastructure for a trading firm or another environment with strict uptime and latency requirements, including hands-on experience with colocation hardware and bare-metal Linux servers.
- Deep, demonstrable expertise in low-latency Linux, including kernel and network tuning, CPU and NUMA isolation, IRQ affinity, and kernel-bypass NICs and technologies such as Solarflare/Onload, Exanic, and Mellanox/DPDK. You must also have the measurement discipline to validate performance improvements.
- Experience leading an infrastructure, DevOps, or SRE team, including hiring, setting priorities, and taking accountability for outcomes while remaining a hands-on technical contributor.
- Experience building and operating internal platform services for development and research teams, including CI/CD, compute, storage, monitoring, and developer tooling. Experience consuming these services alone is not sufficient.
- Strong Linux systems administration skills and experience with container orchestration technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes. You should understand where containers are appropriate in a trading environment and where they are not.
- Familiarity with machine learning and data-intensive workflows, including GPU scheduling, large-dataset access patterns, and reproducible compute environments.
- Experience designing and operating hybrid infrastructure across colocation, on-premises, and at least one major cloud provider, such as AWS, GCP, or Azure. You should understand the tradeoffs between these environments.
- A practical, mature approach to infrastructure security, including access control models such as zero-trust and bastion hosts, network segmentation, secrets management, vulnerability scanning, patch management, audit logging, and incident response.

jobs.ashbyhq.com/teza-technologies/b4043.description_excerpt:
We're looking for an experienced Portfolio Manager to build and scale systematic trading strategies across global agricultural markets.
This role is ideal for someone who combines deep knowledge of agricultural commodity fundamentals with a quantitative mindset. You'll have the opportunity to develop differentiated alpha by integrating supply and demand dynamics, weather, satellite imagery, logistics, positioning, and alternative datasets into systematic trading models.
You'll work alongside experienced quantitative researchers, engineers, and data specialists while having the autonomy to shape research direction, portfolio construction, and execution.
Location
Austin, TX or London, UK (onsite)
Key Responsibilities
- Develop and manage systematic trading strategies across agricultural commodity markets.
- Generate alpha by combining fundamental commodity research with quantitative modeling and statistical analysis.
- Build predictive models using datasets such as weather, crop conditions, satellite imagery, freight flows, inventories, positioning, macroeconomic data, and other alternative data sources.
- Design and evaluate new signals through rigorous research, backtesting, and performance attribution.
- Continuously improve portfolio construction, risk allocation, and execution efficiency.
- Partner closely with quantitative developers to productionize research and build scalable trading systems.
- Work across the full research lifecycle, from idea generation through live deployment and ongoing monitoring.
Basic Requirements
- Deep understanding of agricultural commodity markets, including supply and demand dynamics, seasonal effects, logistics, weather, and global trade flows.
- Several years of experience managing or researching systematic commodity strategies.
- Strong quantitative background with experience applying statistical or machine learning techniques to financial markets.
- Excellent Python programming skills and the ability to work with large datasets.
- Experience building systematic investment strategies rather than discretionary trading alone.
- Strong understanding of portfolio construction, risk management, and systematic execution.
- Intellectual curiosity and a passion for developing new sources of alpha.
Nice to Have
- Experience trading multiple commodity sectors beyond agriculture.
- Familiarity with alternative datasets, remote sensing, satellite imagery, or geospatial analytics.
- Experience with machine learning applied to commodity forecasting.
- Knowledge of real-time research infrastructure and production trading systems.
- Graduate degree in a quantitative discipline.
- Track record of managing external or proprietary capital.
Benefits
- Health, visual and dental insurance
- Flexible sick time policy

- Own the quality and outcomes of engagements from technical discovery and requirements gathering through solution design, implementation, launch, and handover.
