The Role
As an AI Harness Engineer at Valarian, you will own the experimental design, evaluation methodologies, and benchmark infrastructure for our AI models and autonomous agentic workloads. In an emerging domain with no standard playbook, you will serve as the bridge between rigorous data science, statistical validation, and production agent scaffolding.
You will design robust evaluation datasets, architect calibrated LLM-as-a-judge pipelines, and build metrics that accurately capture multi-step agent performance under non-deterministic conditions. Your insights and error analyses will directly drive iterative improvements to our harness scaffolding, tool orchestration, and system safety guardrails.
What you’ll do:
Architect Evaluation Runtimes & Harnesses: Design and maintain scalable Python evaluation harnesses that measure task completion, trajectory quality, tool-use correctness, cost, latency, and variance across multi-step agentic systems.
Design Experiments & Validate Results: Apply rigorous statistical methods—including hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, bootstrapping, and power analysis—to determine whether performance changes are true system improvements or stochastic noise.
Build & Calibrate LLM-as-a-Judge Pipelines: Develop automated judging systems validated against human ground truth. Measure alignment using agreement metrics (Cohen’s kappa, correlation, precision/recall) and systematically detect judge failure modes such as position bias, verbosity bias, self-preference, and prompt sensitivity.
Curate Benchmark Datasets & Rubrics: Define sampling strategies, detailed annotation guidelines, and scoring rubrics. Measure inter-annotator agreement and manage label noise to ensure benchmark integrity over time.
Deep Error & Trajectory Analysis: Conduct hands-on failure analysis on agent runs, cluster root causes into actionable error categories, and clearly communicate findings to both engineering teams and stakeholders.
Drive Harness Scaffolding Iteration: Translate evaluation results directly into architectural improvements across agent scaffolding, prompt design, tool execution loops, context window compaction, retries, and safety guardrails.
What we are looking for:
Grounding in Statistics & Experimental Design: Demonstrated expertise in hypothesis testing, bootstrapping, power analysis, and statistical significance within probabilistic machine learning systems.
LLM-as-a-Judge Validation: Proven experience building, auditing, and validating LLM judge setups against human annotations, including tracking agreement metrics and mitigating judge biases.
Evaluation Dataset Engineering: Strong track record designing evaluation datasets, crafting precise scoring rubrics, managing label noise, and measuring inter-annotator agreement.
Evaluation of Non-Deterministic Multi-Step Systems: Deep comfort evaluating complex agent trajectories, tool execution sequences, latency, cost, and variance across repeated runs rather than relying solely on single-shot benchmarks.
Metric Design & Integrity: Exceptional judgment in defining metrics tied to real-world outcomes, with a keen eye for detecting benchmark gaming, target drift, or shortcut learning.
Rigor in Error Analysis: Ability to dissect complex execution logs, categorize failure modes, and synthesize clear, data-driven recommendations.
Hands-On LLM Integration: Practical proficiency with LLM APIs, prompt engineering, structured outputs, function/tool calling, and retrieval systems in Python.
Agent Architecture Awareness: Clear understanding of planning loops, tool orchestration, memory management, and multi-agent coordination, including their trade-offs and common failure modes.
Harness & Scaffolding Contribution: Ability to write clean, maintainable Python code to iterate on harness components such as guardrails, retry logic, state handling, and context management.
Nice to have:
Experience with agent and evaluation frameworks (e.g., LangChain, LangGraph, AutoGen, lm-evaluation-harness, Promptfoo, or Ragas).
Exposure to running evaluation pipelines or agent workloads within secure, enclave, or Kubernetes environments.

Valarian: A New Era of Sovereign Intelligence
Valarian is a dual use technology company building critical tools to safeguard the future in an era of evolving global security challenges. Backed by a Series A funding round of $50m led by NEA, we are rethinking security beyond traditional military domains to address asymmetric threats that impact our technological advantage, economic strength, and democratic institutions. We provide the control infrastructure that allows government and regulated enterprise to put frontier-class AI to work safely.
We are bringing a frontier AI experience inside secure boundaries for the first time. Our technology supports mission critical workflows across government, healthcare, and enterprise, including:
Scaling open-weight models without external inference endpoints.
Putting frontier class AI to work across organisations through partnerships with other leading AI startups such as Perplexity.
Increasing operational resiliency for air gapped, on prem, and cloud based systems.
Securing intellectual property and maintaining auditability for high stakes enterprise environments.
Facilitating secure information flow during disaster response, M&A due diligence, and privileged legal communications.
We’ve only scratched the surface. Built in Britain by veterans of the Ministry of Defence, British Forces, Darktrace, and elite engineering backgrounds, we are driven by a shared mission to safeguard western democracy . Whether you join our London HQ or our wider global organisation, you’ll be part of a collaborative, high performing team creating the cutting edge software and infrastructure that defines the frontier of enterprise AI.
The Role
You will lead the operational, delivery, and governance execution for Valarian’s platform engineering team, acting as the primary operational partner to the Head of Engineering. This role sits at the intersection of technical execution, Product and platform security for ACRA, our complex security-focused Kubernetes platform.
You will own the operational lifecycle of external engineering dependencies end to end: from scoping, scheduling, and managing third-party penetration testing to overseeing contractor budgets, statement of work (SOW) execution, and project billing. You will keep engineering operations financially sorted, compliant, and friction-free, ensuring that external technical deliverables align seamlessly with internal platform engineering cycles.
You will serve as the crucial interface between engineering leadership and external partners. You will translate complex security, infrastructure, and operational requirements into actionable engineering priorities, triaging pentest findings, managing vulnerability remediation workflows with engineers, and reporting clear status, risk, and spend metrics directly to the Head of Engineering.
This is not a role for someone who only wants to manage spreadsheets or pass messages. We are looking for someone who understands the technical product vision, challenges assumptions,  and turns complex operational challenges into smooth, reliable systems.
As Valarian grows, this role offers a clear path to increasing operational ownership and strategic influence. We are looking for strong operational judgement, curiosity, ownership, technical fluency, and the ability to bring order to complex environments.
What you’ll do:
Own the Platform Security & Trust Roadmap: Define and prioritize the product capabilities, compliance requirements, and technical enhancements needed to maintain ACRA’s zero-trust security architecture and enterprise readiness.
Define Technical Requirements & Specifications: Translate pentest findings, compliance mandates (e.g., ISO 27001, SOC 2), and technical specs into clear user stories, acceptance criteria, and API contracts for engineering.
Lead Backlog Grooming & Vulnerability Prioritization: Drive product discovery and backlog refinement with engineering, prioritizing vulnerability remediations alongside new feature delivery based on risk, severity, and customer SLAs.
Orchestrate External Security Engagements: Scope and run external penetration tests and third-party security audits as structured product validation cycles, tracking findings through to re-testing and delivery.
Manage External Technical Dependencies: Align third-party integrations, vendor deliverables, and partner APIs with core platform release cycles to ensure unblocked delivery.
Balance Feature Velocity against Technical Risk: Partner with engineering, product, and leadership to evaluate trade-offs between delivery speed, engineering effort, financial costs, and platform security boundaries.
Track Security & Product Metrics: Monitor key product health indicators—including time-to-remediation, security posture compliance, vendor SLA performance, and feature delivery predictability.
Drive Product-Led Security Value: Act as a product owner in a fast-paced startup, ensuring platform security, data sovereignty, and auditability serve as key competitive differentiators for Valarian.
Nice to have:
Experience in secure or regulated environments, such as defence, government, fintech, critical infrastructure, or sovereign cloud.
Understanding of zero-trust architecture, identity-aware systems, policy enforcement, or workload isolation concepts.
Experience managing technical delivery in a high-growth startup or scale-up environment.
Again: these are not requirements. They are areas you may get to work with and go deeper into at Valarian.
Benefits:
Our benefits are designed to ensure our employees feel taken care of and are proud to be a part of the Valarian team. We are committed to consistently enhancing our benefit package, taking into account the overall well-being and needs of our teammates. Here are the key benefits accessible to all employees at Valarian Technologies:
Equity – because you have the right to own what you’re building
A competitive salary – because we value your unique skills
Employer pension contributions – because you deserve a secure future
Private health insurance - because your health is important to us
Hybrid work setup – because everyone has different needs
Gym memberships - because staying active fuels productivity
Rewarding company retreats and meetups that respect your work/life balance – because we love getting to know each other
Life at Valarian
Our culture is built on inclusivity, compassion and flexibility – we want everyone to be empowered to achieve their goals at Valarian.
The work we do is vital, but so are the connections that make it happen. We thrive on the shared energy, spontaneous conversations, and mutual trust built when we spend time together. We operate on an office first hybrid model, regularly gathering in our London office to support one another and collaborate.

👫 Department: Found, Commercial. Reporting to the Head of Commercial, Found
💰 Salary: OTE £75,000 - £105,000 (£50,000 - £70,000 base) + equity
🎁 Benefits & Culture: See here https://careers.lottie.org/
📈 Equity: A very generous EMI share offering

💗 https://emojipedia.org/growing-heart Mission: Elevate later life for everybody and build the care sector of the future
💻 Office Policy: Hybrid with a minimum of 2 core office days per week
🌍 Office Location: London Bridge, London, UK
🔍 https://emojipedia.org/magnifying-glass-tilted-left The Opportunity:
Lottie is building the AI operating system for social care. Families find care through our marketplace. Providers use Found to manage enquiries, occupancy and finances, with Eliza, our AI agent, answering family calls and chats on their behalf.
We're opening Found for Specialist Care as a new vertical, alongside Care Home and Home Care, and we need someone to build it. This is a market to create, not a playbook to follow.
You'll own the full sales cycle from prospecting to close, shape the messaging, and become our go-to expert on specialist care. You won't start from zero: 7-8 specialist care providers already use Found, plus a pipeline we previously turned away. Product work over the next two quarters will be shaped by what you hear from the market.
You'll sit alongside our Care Home and Home Care sales leads, with direct access to commercial leadership, product and our founder. If you want to own a vertical and prove what you can do with real autonomy, this is the role for you!
💻 What does this role involve?
- Own the full sales cycle for specialist care and supported living providers, from first conversation to close, then hand over cleanly to Customer Success
- Build the go-to-market for the vertical: test messaging, learn what resonates and iterate on what works
- Re-engage providers we previously talked to and grow from the existing 7–8 specialist care customers
- Build and manage your pipeline through outbound (calls, emails, LinkedIn, events) alongside inbound leads
- Run discovery calls and demos, often with head-office and operational leaders at multi-site providers
- Negotiate and close deals against MRR targets, with uncapped commission on ARR closed
- Feed market insight to Product and Engineering as we build out Found for Specialist Care
💪 What problems will you be solving?
- Opening a market Found hasn't sold into before, so specialist care providers get modern tools that help them support the people they care for
- Winning in a largely local-authority-funded world, where buying decisions and ROI look different to private-pay care
- Selling honestly while the product is still evolving, and turning provider feedback into what we build next
- Building a repeatable sales motion the team can scale as we grow this vertical
- Being the voice of specialist care providers inside Found, so their needs shape the product
👀 We think you’ll be a great fit if…
- You're a self-starter who can take a brief and run with it, without a ready-made playbook or an SDR feeding you leads
- You have at least 12 months of closing experience in a B2B sales role and have consistently hit or exceeded targets
- You're strong on the phone and comfortable building your own pipeline from outbound

ABOUT MAZE
Maze is the user research platform that helps companies build the right products faster by making user insights available at the speed of product development.
In most companies, research demand far exceeds supply. Time, cost, and lack of access to expertise hold teams back. In today’s AI-powered world, anyone can build a product fast. The real challenge? Deeply understanding user needs and building the right product. That’s where Maze comes in.
We believe companies shouldn’t have to choose between building fast and building right. Maze makes research accessible, intuitive, and fast so product teams can put user insights at the center of every decision.
Our platform enables researchers, designers, and product managers to quickly recruit participants, run studies autonomously, and surface insights that actually drive product decisions. Our AI capabilities automate the busywork and add depth and direction to the insights themselves.
That’s why Maze was recently named the #1 user research platform in UX Tools’ Design Tools Survey https://www.uxtools.co/survey/user-research/user-testing-overview—and why we’re scaling fast across industries like B2B SaaS, e-Commerce, Financial Services, Retail, and Automotive, supporting world class customers such as Uber, Amazon, Atlassian, Anthropic & more.
Maze is a Series B company backed by top-tier investors (Felicis, Emergence & Amplify). We operate a global remote workforce driven by our core values https://maze.co/about-us/.
Location: Remote, preference for Netherlands, United Kingdom, Ireland, Spain or Portugal. Key engineering and product teams are based in these locales.
THE ROLE
As a Senior Full Stack Software Engineer on the Product Engineering team, you'll design and deliver high impact features, working closely with product, design, and other engineers to solve complex problems, build scalable solutions, and ensure our systems are maintainable and performant.
You’ll take ownership of projects from concept to production, contribute to architectural decisions, write high quality code, and help raise the technical bar by sharing knowledge and best practices with your teammates.
YOU'LL WORK ON:
- Building elegant features for user researchers to analyze and extract compelling insights from qualitative data, using both classical techniques and large language models
- Expanding audience management to help researchers connect with and reward participants from across the world
- Integrating video and scheduling tools to provide a streamlined experience for managing and booking user interviews
AS A PRODUCT ENGINEER AT MAZE, YOU WILL:
- Partner closely with product managers, designers and other engineers to design, build, and ship new features
- Establish best practices, frameworks, and repeatable processes that enable us to measure the impact of every feature that we ship
- Evaluate and improve the performance, maintainability, and security of applications in production
- Work in a collaborative and open team, which places high value on feedback, continuous learning and trust.
YOU SHOULD APPLY IF:
- You're proficient with modern full-stack JavaScript (Node.js and React) and relational databases (PostgreSQL)
- You're enthusiastic about well-tested code and strive to improve your work environment
- You have excellent written and spoken English skills
- You thrive in a remote environment
BONUS POINTS:
- You have Next.js, NestJS, GraphQL, and/or TypeScript experience
- You have experience with AWS and/or Kubernetes
- You're interested in UX, UI design, and the research field

At Maze, we are dedicated to building an equitable, inclusive, and authentic workspace. Unique and diverse perspectives are welcomed, and continuous growth is encouraged. We believe that people are more than their resumes, so if your past experience looks different than the criteria listed, we'd still love to hear from you. We are informed by data and regularly check our salary ranges (either United States or Rest of World) against other venture backed companies. Additionally, we are proud of our holistic and generous benefits offerings, included in every compensation package.
Your salary is dependent upon many factors, including years of experience, expertise, etc. During your first interview, you can expect to have an open conversation with your recruiter regarding your compensation expectations.
WHY MAZE IS UNIQUE
- Early-stage startup: You will join an early-stage startup with less than 150 team members. This means you'll have the unique opportunity to directly impact success and help shape the future of Maze.
- Market disruption: We believe that the way companies build products is fundamentally broken and the user research market is ripe for disruption. For too long, companies have been forced to choose between rapid development without user insights or investing months into research before bringing products to market. But there's finally a groundswell building around a path forward that eliminates this compromise - and Maze is leading the charge.
- Product-market Fit: Maze is used by 100,000+ brands across 4,000 companies, from SMB to enterprises, and in the last fiscal year, we saw 6.5M questions answered, supporting 25K decisions

- $1,500 remote work setup fund to ensure you can set up a productive work space
- Flexible work schedule where you manage your own working hours

- Virtual social engagements randomly throughout the year

This role is a mix of software engineering and customer-facing problem solving. You’ll work closely with engineering teams at companies like Notion, Dropbox, Wealthsimple, Outtake, and LaunchDarkly to understand how their systems work and help them successfully deploy Meticulous. Some days you’ll be writing and debugging code; other days you’ll be discussing technical decisions, trade-offs, and best practices with customer engineers.
You won’t be expected to know everything on day one. You’ll be supported by experienced engineers on the team, but you’ll also be given real ownership and responsibility early on.
CORE RESPONSIBILITIES
This role spans both engineering and customer success. You’ll take ownership of customer deployments and do what’s needed to make Meticulous successful for them, including:
- Work with customers to deploy Meticulous at scale. Partner with customer engineering teams to understand their architecture, design implementation approaches that fit their systems, and work alongside them to ship reliable solutions.
- Improve the product based on real-world usage. Debug issues that block deployments, investigate problems that reach into core parts of the system, and help ship improvements or features that make the product work better for both the customer you’re focused on and Meticulous overall.
- Build strong customer relationships. Communicate regularly with engineers and engineering leaders, help guide rollouts, and collect feedback to ensure customers are successful and supported.
- Influence product direction. Use what you learn from working with customers to help inform what we build next. For smaller improvements, you’ll often implement them directly; for larger changes, you’ll work closely with the core engineering team to scope and deliver them.
- Help define best practices. As the Forward Deployed Engineering function grows, you’ll contribute to documentation, tooling, and processes that make each new deployment smoother than the last.
WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR
- Strong technical foundation. A degree in computer science, engineering, or a related technical field, with solid fundamentals in programming and systems.
- High ownership and motivation. You’re comfortable taking responsibility, figuring things out, and moving projects forward even when things are ambiguous.
- Entrepreneurial spirit. You’ve spent time building things outside of structured coursework such as working on a startup, founding or contributing to an open-source projects, or shipping personal projects end-to-end.
- Clear communicator. You can explain technical ideas clearly, ask good questions, and enjoy working directly with other engineers.
- Willingness to travel. Around 25% travel to customer sites, primarily in the US.
WHAT YOU’LL GAIN
- Learn by building a new function. You’ll be part of shaping an entirely new role at Meticulous, with clear opportunities to grow in responsibility and influence as the team expands.
- Exceptional growth and mentorship. We intentionally keep the team small and highly experienced. You’ll work closely with engineers who have led large teams and built complex systems at top technology companies. The environment is fast-paced, collaborative, and focused on learning quickly from each other. Beyond core engineering growth, you’ll spend significant time working with engineering leaders at fast-growing startups and established tech companies. This gives you exposure to a wide range of technologies, architectures, workflows, and engineering cultures - experience that normally takes many years and multiple jobs to accumulate.
- Expand your network. Our investors and advisors include leaders from Vercel, GitHub, Segment, YC, Adobe, and Dropbox. Through the role, you’ll also work directly with engineering teams across many top technology companies, building relationships early in your career that can compound for years.
- Solve novel technical problems. You’ll work on challenging problems at the intersection of browser technology, testing infrastructure, and large-scale systems - areas that few engineers encounter early in their careers.
- World-class compensation. Base salary £80k–£140k plus significant equity, competitive with top technology companies and startups.
LIFE AT METICULOUS
We believe autonomous testing will eventually enable the automation of much of software development. You’ll be working at the forefront of this shift, alongside the companies that are adopting these tools first.
This role is on-site at our office in Moorgate. We’ve found that the level of collaboration, learning, and iteration required to succeed works best when the team is together in person.

Our almost 1,000-person team builds tools that make work better for the three billion frontline workers who keep the world moving. We've got big tech scale, without the sign-off layers or corporate theatre. This next chapter is about scaling smart, powered by AI, a clear vision and real ownership.
Big tech impact, without the big tech ick.
Role Purpose
This role exists to unlock technical value for Mitti’s customers, designing and implementing solutions that ensure customers integrate deeply with the platform and realise measurable operational outcomes, while bridging the gap between Go-to-Market (GTM) teams and Product, Design & Engineering (PDE). They own end-to-end delivery of integration offerings within defined scope, timeline, and budget, escalating only where customer requirements exceed standard package boundaries.
Key Responsibilities
Drive customer success and stickiness
- Own technical solution design for select customers: from scoping integrations and data workflows through to working implementations that enable full platform value.
- Deliver the standard Integration/Automation packages end-to-end: scope confirmation, project delivery, build, testing, and handoff within the defined timeline and effort budget.
- Advise customers and partners on integration architecture: how to connect Mitti to their existing systems effectively and sustainably.
- Partner with Customer Success Managers (CSMs) to build implementation plans that accelerate time-to-value for managed accounts.
- Work alongside Account Executives (AEs) during pre-sales to communicate technical platform capabilities (APIs, security architecture, and cloud integrations) and resolve technical blockers in the sales cycle.
- Act as a technical bridge between GTM and PDE, capturing and routing customer integration feedback that shapes the product roadmap.
- Partner with the API and Integrations Engineering team to resolve complex customer requirements and advocate for platform improvements that benefit the broader customer base.
Improve how we deliver
- Identify recurring technical patterns across customer integrations, propose and participate in standardisation efforts: new packaged offerings, reusable automation, or templated solutions that reduce delivery effort across the customer base, not just for one account.
- Build and maintain technical automations (scripts, workflows, tooling) that reduce manual effort in the standard delivery motion, contributing them back to the shared Customer Solution & Implementation toolkit rather than keeping them account-specific.
- Flag when the same "out of scope" request appears repeatedly across customers, as a signal the package boundary itself needs to move, not just that this customer needs an exception.
Required Skills & Experience
Technical Skills
- Proven ability to design and implement data solutions: writing SQL queries, modelling relational databases, and translating raw data into business-relevant insights.
- Comfortable building across scripting or programming languages (e.g. Python, JavaScript, Ruby, Golang) to automate workflows or extend platform capabilities for specific customer use cases.
- Able to navigate a wide variety of enterprise system architectures, data models, and integration patterns.
- Confident reading API documentation and building or troubleshooting API integrations in enterprise environments.
- Background spanning software development and data analytics; comfortable moving between building solutions and communicating data-driven insights to non-technical stakeholders.
Behavioural Skills
- Translates fluently between technical and non-technical audiences: equally credible in an engineering deep-dive and a customer-facing session with business stakeholders.
- Stays organised across a high-volume, concurrent workload; switches context quickly without losing quality or missing detail.
- Customer-first problem solver: listens to understand the real need before proposing a solution, and brings options rather than just problems.
- Self-directed and comfortable with ambiguity; exercises sound judgment on edge cases while operating within a defined delivery methodology.
- Team-first mindset: invests in the success of CSMs, AEs, and engineering partners, not just their own outcomes.
- Distinguishes clearly between solving a customer's immediate problem and identifying a systemic delivery improvement worth productising, and routes each appropriately.
AI Skills
- Uses AI tools to accelerate integration work, drafting technical specs and documentation, analysing customer data to surface insights, and building automations faster.
- Applies AI coding assistants fluently in day-to-day work; evaluates AI-generated code for quality, correctness, and security before deploying.
- Proficient with AI tools: independently identifies where AI adds leverage in their workflows and adopts new capabilities without direction.
Benefits
At Mitti, we care about people and growing the team, through:
- Equity with high growth potential, and a competitive salary,
- Hybrid working arrangements with flexibility,
- Access to professional and personal training and development opportunities; Hackathons, Workshops, Lunch & Learns;
- We encourage involvement in the community, open source work, attending talks and events, and experimenting with new technologies.
You'll also receive other perks such as:
- Remote flexible working arrangements
- Wellbeing initiatives such as subsidised fitness programs, EAP services and generous parental leave policy
- Quarterly celebrations and team events
- Table tennis, board games, gym sessions, book club, and pet-friendly offices.
We’re committed to building inclusive teams and cultivating a sense of belonging so our people can bring their whole authentic selves to work each day. We seek to make reasonable adjustments throughout our recruitment process to create an even playing field for all candidates. Thanks to the tireless efforts of the entire Mitti team we’ve built an incredible culture which has seen us recognised as a Best Place to Work in Australia , the US and the UK .
Even if you don't meet every requirement listed in the ad, please consider applying for this role. We prioritise inclusion and value individuals with potential over a checklist of qualifications. Don't rule yourself out, hit that apply button if this job resonates with you
You can find out more about life at Mitti via Youtube https://www.youtube.com/c/SafetycultureAu , Twitter https://x.com/MittiHQ , Instagram https://www.instagram.com/mittihq and LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/mittihq/.
To all recruitment agencies, we do not accept resumes or partnership opportunities. Please do not forward resumes to Mitti or any of our employees. We are not responsible for any fees associated with unsolicited resumes.

jobs.ashbyhq.com/mollie/304404f1-c1c6-4e.description_excerpt:
Build with us
Since 2004, we've had one clear goal: to make payments and money management effortless for every business in Europe.
Today, more than 250,000 companies use Mollie to get paid, manage money and grow – with products designed to be simple, scalable, and dependable.
With 950+ Mollies across 14+ locations, we care deeply about autonomy and craft. So we work in small teams, with real ownership, and we trust you to make the right decisions.
We're building for the long term, so we provide the tools you need, processes you can rely on, and a balanced work environment to help you do work you're proud of.
Sound like your kind of place? Let's build together.
Your impact
As our Senior Product Marketing Manager, you'll be leading go-to-market for Mollie's online payments product space. This is our core product offering and includes cards, Klarna, pay by bank and other products. You'll translate product capabilities and roadmap into positioning and coordinated marketing activity, connecting product strategy with execution across marketing, sales, and customer success.
A key and evolving focus of this role is Agentic Commerce, an emerging area involving AI facilitated shopping that requires deep technical knowledge and strategic partnerships with entities like Visa and Mastercard. You'll play a central role in building thought leadership and developing tools such as Generative Engine Optimization to support merchants navigating this space.
This role is particularly exciting because it ensures Mollie's core products are successfully brought to market and aligned with what customers actually need. By turning customer insight into strategic marketing initiatives, you'll directly support Mollie's commercial success.
What you'll ship
- Go to market plans built with product teams, covering technical product understanding, value and benefits, positioning, value propositions, USPs, ICPs, use cases, and messaging
- Coordinated launch activity across channel teams, bringing GTM plans to life in the market
- A launch framework covering foundations, pre-launch, launch, early momentum, proof points, and ramp-up
- Briefs, asset lists, and competitor research that support each launch
- Project timelines kept current as product readiness or market events shift
- Coordinated alignment between product and go-to-market teams when roadmap dependencies or external industry timing affect launch dates
What you'll bring
- 5+ years of marketing experience, at least 3 of those in product marketing
- End-to-end go-to-market planning experience, including ICP definition, positioning, and launch timelines
- Experience in the online payments space or related areas, such as working with partners like Shopify. Prior fintech or payments exposure helps you ramp up quickly, but a strong technical product background from another vertical can also work
- Strong messaging and positioning skills, with the ability to craft compelling value propositions and clear differentiation
- Technical fluency, able to translate product specs, roadmaps, and integrations into GTM-ready language, with comfort using data platforms such as Looker, HubSpot, or other BI tools
- Experience researching competitors and industry trends, running customer interviews or surveys, and using analytics tools to measure performance and shape strategy
- Proven cross-functional project management
- Strong presentation skills for internal decks and training
Grow your way
At Mollie, growth is personal. We believe everyone should have the chance to develop their skills, explore new challenges and shape their career on their own terms.
You'll get regular feedback and performance reviews to support your development, with fair and transparent salary reviews along the way. Many Mollies move into new roles or take on new projects to stretch themselves, and we actively hire from within to help you take the next step.
No matter if you're aiming for promotion, exploring a different career path or building new skills, you'll be supported with the tools, trust and opportunities to grow your way.
Unlock your full potential and join us to eliminate financial bureaucracy
If you're excited by the idea of building what's next, for yourself and for thousands of businesses across Europe, we'd love to hear from you. Apply with your CV (in English) using the form below.
Want a peek behind the scenes? Check out what life at Mollie https://jobs.mollie.com/ is really like.
AI at Mollie
We believe in Always Be Shipping, and AI brings https://jobs.mollie.com/ai-manifesto that philosophy to life across every team, every role, every day.
AI is core to how we build. It helps us move faster, simplify work and make smarter decisions, creating real impact for the businesses we serve. We're looking for people who are excited to use AI to shape the future of finance with us.

jobs.ashbyhq.com/mollie/313f21b9-8f1b-48.description_excerpt:
Build with us
Since 2004, we've had one clear goal: to make payments and money management effortless for every business in Europe.
Today, more than 250,000 companies use Mollie to get paid, manage money and grow, with products designed to be simple, scalable, and dependable.
With 950+ Mollies across 14+ locations, we care deeply about autonomy and craft. So we work in small teams, with real ownership, and we trust you to make the right decisions.
We're building for the long term, so we provide the tools you need, processes you can rely on, and a balanced work environment to help you do work you're proud of.
Sound like your kind of place? Let's build together.
Your impact
Treasury is where Mollie's balance sheet takes shape, this team makes sure that our balance sheet is safe, well-funded and resilient. You, as Treasury Manager, will be one of the first people building the Asset & Liability Management (ALM) function for Mollie.
This is a genuine 0-to-1 role. There is no legacy ALM framework to maintain, no existing ILAAP to update, no established models to inherit. You'll help design and build the liquidity risk framework, the interest rate and credit spread risk approach, and the funding and balance sheet strategy. Your work will feed directly into Mollie’s licence application and, once authorised, into how Mollie actually manages its liquidity and funding risks.
You'll work closely with our product teams, Finance, and Risk Domains and your analysis will be seen by senior leadership and, eventually, by our regulator. As Mollie moves from application to operation, your scope will grow from building the framework to running it.
What you'll ship
- Build and own the core building blocks of Mollie liquidity risk framework, including the ILAAP, LCR/NSFR monitoring, and liquidity stress testing.
- Develop Mollie’s approach to interest rate risk and credit spread risk in the banking book (IRRBB/CSRBB), from risk identification through to models, limits and hedging strategy.
- Contribute to the design of Mollie’s funding and balance sheet strategy, including deposit mix, funding diversification and balance sheet construction.
- Build the Contingency Funding Plan and related early-warning indicators, so Mollie knows exactly what to do under stress before it needs to.
- Produce clear, well-documented policies, methodologies and models that will stand up to scrutiny from DNB/ECB, external auditors, and Mollie's own second and third lines of defense.
- Support senior leadership (ALCO or its future equivalent) with the analysis, reporting and recommendations it needs to make sound balance sheet decisions.
- Partner with Risk, Finance and our external advisors, to make sure Treasury's frameworks are consistent with Mollie’s wider risk appetite and governance.
What you'll bring
- Around 5+ years of experience in Treasury, ALM or balance sheet risk management, ideally within a bank, though experience in a fintech, PSP or consultancy building similar frameworks is also relevant.
- Solid working knowledge of liquidity risk (LCR/NSFR, ILAAP) and/or interest rate risk in the banking book (IRRBB/CSRBB). You don't need to be deep in both, but you understand how they connect to the balance sheet as a whole.
- Comfort building models and frameworks from a blank page. You're not looking for a well-worn playbook, you're excited to write the first one.
- Strong quantitative and Excel/financial modelling skills, with the discipline to document your logic clearly enough that someone else, including a regulator, can follow it.
- The ability to explain complex balance sheet risk topics clearly to non-specialists, and the confidence to defend your recommendations to senior stakeholders.
- Genuine curiosity about how AI can speed up the parts of this work that don't need a human, so more of your time goes toward judgment and design.
Grow your way
At Mollie, growth is personal. We believe everyone should have the chance to develop their skills, explore new challenges and shape their career on their own terms.
You'll get regular feedback and performance reviews to support your development, with fair and transparent salary reviews along the way. Many Mollies move into new roles or take on new projects to stretch themselves, and we actively hire from within to help you take the next step.
No matter if you're aiming for promotion, exploring a different career path or building new skills, you'll be supported with the tools, trust and opportunities to grow your way.
Unlock your full potential and join us to eliminate financial bureaucracy.
If you're excited by the idea of building a bank's Treasury function from scratch, for Mollie and for thousands of businesses across Europe, we'd love to hear from you. Apply with your CV (in English) using the form below.
Want a peek behind the scenes? Check out what life at Mollie is really like.
AI at Mollie
We believe in Always Be Shipping, and AI brings that philosophy to life across every role, every day.
AI is core to how we build. It helps us move faster, simplify work and make smarter decisions, creating real impact for the businesses we serve. We're looking for people who are excited to use AI to shape the future of finance and banking with us.

Mercor Safety Research Grants $5M
One of the biggest challenges the industry faces today is addressing whether frontier AI is safe enough to deploy. A model can pass safety checks and still act differently in production. This is why investing today in safety research, evals and verification is critical.
Mercor is committing $5 million to fund safety research. Award size and mix depend on the project. The grant supports:
- Researcher hours
- API costs
- Stipends for event and conference attendance
- The time of experts from Mercor's platform
This is separate from the Mercor Research Fellowship, which funds benchmark and economics work. You can apply to that HERE https://www.mercor.com/careers/?ashby_jid=e1f6792d-1aae-4c2e-8edb-e2b91343dbb5.
What we're looking for
We're open to proposals across the full range of safety interests. We're particularly interested in:
- Misalignment: deceptive alignment, goal misgeneralization, reward hacking, scheming, and situationally-aware failure modes
- Sandbox escape: containment failures, privilege escalation, tool misuse, and agents operating outside their intended scope
- Evaluation awareness: models detecting they are being tested and behaving differently under observation than in deployment
- Interpretability: understanding what models are actually doing internally, and whether that can be made legible to a human reviewer
- Oversight and control: scalable supervision, human-in-the-loop reliability, and what breaks when the system is more capable than its reviewer
- Red-teaming methodology: more robust systems for uncovering novel failures
If your work doesn't fit neatly into these, apply anyway. Strong proposals outside this list are welcome.
Why us
- Funding for researcher time, API costs, and event attendance
- Where useful to the work: access to Mercor's expert network for human grading, red-teaming, and annotation: lawyers, accountants, engineers, scientists, clinicians
- Access to Mercor's internal evaluation infrastructure, subject to review
- Introductions to Mercor's network of researchers across frontier labs and academia
Who should apply
- Researchers at universities and non-profit research organizations, as well as public benefit corporations and small startups that do not sell AI training data. Awards are made to the researcher’s institution.
- People with a specific, well-scoped question: the grant is built around your proposal, not a generic research rotation
- Applicants based in the United States or the United Kingdom
- Background in ML, CS, statistics, or an adjacent field (measurement, psychometrics, HCI, security, social science)
- Bonus: experience with agentic evaluation, RL environments, adversarial ML, or systems security
We expect grantees to publish. A paper, an open dataset, a public methodology, or a tool the field can use, released under an open license that permits commercial use.
Award terms
Selected grantees will sign Mercor’s research award agreement. Key terms include:
- Grantees keep ownership of their work and grant Mercor a non-exclusive license to use it, including commercially.
- Mercor may identify grantees and their institutions as award recipients, including by name and logo. Grantees may use Mercor’s logo with Mercor’s approval.
- For benchmark and evaluation projects, Mercor receives early access to the benchmark before public release and the exclusive right to build and host a private held-out test set, at Mercor’s cost.
- Grantees agree not to work with specified Mercor competitors on substantially similar benchmarks or evaluations during the award and for 12 months afterward.
- Grantees are free to publish their findings. Mercor reviews drafts in advance only to remove its confidential information.
- Awards are subject to tax documentation, sanctions screening, and periodic progress reports.

Submit an Expression of Interest. We expect to see a one- or two-page document. It should contain at least a section on your team, background, and research accomplishments; a section on your proposed research project; and a section on the outputs and impact of the project, with directionally correct timelines and resource requirements. Please do not include confidential or proprietary information in your Expression of Interest. Submitting an Expression of Interest does not obligate Mercor to make an award.

MERCOR AI RESEARCH FUND GRANTS: BENCHMARKS
One of the biggest challenges facing the industry today is determining whether frontier AI is capable enough to deliver value in real-world settings. A model can perform well on benchmarks and still struggle in production. That’s why investing in research, realistic evaluations, and robust verification is critical.
Mercor is seeking to fund AI research on benchmarking. This is separate from the Mercor Research Fellowship, which funds individual experts (apply HERE https://www.mercor.com/careers/a0a98be0-d856-4129-b500-c0a3e412ef01/), our $5m of safety funding awards (apply HERE https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/mercor/1d59ce50-4207-4d95-b7fd-5a01e90b0897), and our research funding on the economic impacts of AI.
The grant supports:
- The time of experts from Mercor's platform
- Researcher hours
- API costs
- Stipends for event and conference attendance
BUDGET CATEGORIES
Applications are grouped into three budget tiers. Please state your tier clearly in your application and ensure your overall budget ask falls within it:
- Tier 1: under $50,000: Suited to focused, well-scoped projects such as pilot studies, evaluations, replications, or extensions of existing work. These applications undergo a streamlined review.
- Tier 2: under $200,000: Suited to substantial projects requiring dedicated personnel time, meaningful compute, or data collection. Reviewed with proportionally greater attention to the budget breakdown and implementation plan.
- Tier 3: under $500,000: Reserved for ambitious, multi-component research programs. These applications receive the highest level of scrutiny: reviewers will expect a detailed justification of each spend category, a clear account of team capacity to execute at this scale, and milestones against which progress can be assessed.
The level of review scrutiny scales with the size of the ask, so applicants should request the smallest budget that credibly supports the proposed work.
RESEARCH AGENDA
We are interested in submissions in the following area:
- Real-world evaluations: measuring whether benchmark performance translates into reliable performance on realistic tasks and workflows
- Environments: building high-fidelity, interactive environments that capture the complexity of real-world work
- Long-horizon tasks: evaluating and improving models’ ability to plan, execute, and adapt across extended workflows
- Agentic capabilities: tool use, coordination, memory, and autonomous execution
- Reasoning and problem-solving: improving performance on complex, ambiguous, or underspecified tasks
- Post-training: developing better data, rewards, and training methods to improve model capabilities
- Evaluation methodology: creating more robust measures of capability, reliability, and real-world utility
ELIGIBILITY
- Researchers at universities and non-profit research organizations, as well as public benefit corporations and small startups (<20 people) that do not sell AI training data. Awards are made to the researcher’s institution.
- Applicants must be based in the United States or the United Kingdom
We expect grantees to publish a paper, an open dataset, a public methodology, or a tool the field can use, released under an open license that permits commercial use.
TIMELINE
- Application deadline: November 27, 2026, 11:59 PM PT (UTC−8)
- Notification to applicants: by December 18, 2026
Late or incomplete applications will not be reviewed. All applicants will be notified of the outcome whether or not they are shortlisted.
HOW TO APPLY
We invite interested researchers to submit a brief Expression of Interest (EOI) before preparing a full proposal. The EOI should be ~1–3 pages and include:
- Research question and background (max 250 words): What are you trying to do? State your objective in plain language, with minimal jargon. How is this problem addressed today, and what are the limits of current practice? Who cares: if you succeed, what difference will it make, and to whom?
- Project proposal (max 400 words): Concrete technical and implementation detail: your approach, methods, datasets, models, compute, and evaluation plan.
- Novelty (max 200 words): What is new in your approach relative to existing and ongoing work, and why do you believe it will succeed where current practice falls short?
- Risks (max 150 words): What are the main technical and execution risks, and how will you mitigate or detect them early?
- Team (max 100 words; if the team is large, up to 200): The researchers on the project and their relevant background and prior work.
- Proposed outcomes and timeline: Expected deliverables (papers, artifacts, datasets, tools) and key milestones, including how long the work will take. Include the mid-term and final “exams”: the checkpoints and success criteria by which we will know whether the project is on track and succeeds.
- Budget overview: How much will it cost? Provide a specific overall budget ask, your budget tier (see Budget Categories), and a breakdown by spend category (e.g., personnel, compute, data, travel/other).
- Other sources of funding for this project should be clearly identified in the proposal budget
GUIDANCE FOR APPLICANTS.
- Strong EOIs are specific rather than high-level: they name the methods, systems, and evaluation criteria they will use, and they engage directly with existing literature and ongoing efforts rather than describing the problem…

jobs.ashbyhq.com/orbitalindustries/0405b.description_excerpt:
Orbital Industries is an AI Industrial company, with frontier AI embedded at every step in the production of critical physical products - from creating advanced materials to engineering and manufacturing.
Every Orbital Industries product is developed using CurieOS, our AI operating system, uniting AI-automated hardware engineering with AI-designed material science to achieve breakthrough real-world performance. We also offer CurieOS to our customers and partners, extending the same platform and workflows that power Orbital Industries to their own teams and products.
We have an ambitious mission and need excellent people in all our teams - AI research, operations, advanced materials, mechanical engineering, chemical engineering and manufacturing.
Working at Orbital Industries means working in vertically integrated teams across the full stack, from molecules to manufacturing. We're looking for people who have a love of physical technology, curiosity in AI and a desire to learn.
As a Machine Learning Research Engineer at Orbital, you will architect cutting-edge AI systems for the multi-scale design of physical technologies. When we say multi-scale, we mean it: we build world-class foundation models for simulating both the microscopic motion of atoms and the macroscopic flow of liquids in 1GW data centers. We then co-design across these different scales using the ingenuity of our scientists and engineers, augmented with best-in-class domain agents.
In this role you will set exceptionally high technical standards and drive projects from prototype through to production deployment. First and foremost, we want to work with someone with a love of craftsmanship, continual learning, and building systems that scale. We also value low ego, and a genuine passion for using AI to solve major global industrial technology challenges.
Key Responsibilities
Set the technical bar and ensure engineering excellence
- Establish and maintain exceptionally high standards for code quality, system architecture and ML research and engineering practices through hands-on coding and technical review
- Design robust, well-engineered systems that others can build upon, balancing research velocity with production requirements
- Drive technical decisions on model selection, training approaches and deployment strategies
Deliver high-impact AI projects across diverse domains
- Develop and deploy AI solutions across the entire technology development pipeline- computational chemistry simulations, agentic workflows and beyond
- Rapidly upskill in new technical areas through close collaboration with domain experts (no prior chemistry or materials experience required)
- Demonstrate strong implementation skills through hands-on development, contributing significantly to the codebase
- Balance research rigour with pragmatic engineering to deliver production-ready systems at scale
Push the frontier of ML research
- Design and implement novel ML architectures for complex scientific domains, with work that meets publication standards at top-tier conferences
- Drive research projects from conception through to deployment, showing initiative and technical depth
- Engage continuously with the latest ML literature, staying current with developments in foundation models, generative AI and scientific machine learning
What We're Looking For
- Significant software engineering and ML experience, with depth in training, evaluating and deploying AI models - demonstrated through industry work
- Proven experience training, evaluating and productionising AI models at scale, with deep understanding of the full ML lifecycle from research to deployment
- Strong engineering fundamentals with the ability to write high-quality, maintainable code and architect robust systems
- A strong ability to reason about algorithms, system design, linear algebra, probabilistic concepts and ML engineering trade-offs
- An ability to debug complex machine learning systems through meticulous attention to detail, testing of edge cases and carefully selected ablations
- A genuine interest in building AI systems that enable breakthrough scientific and industrial applications
- Upon reading Hamming's You and Your Research, you resonate with quotes such as:
- "Yes, I would like to do first-class work"
- "You should do your job in such a fashion that others can build on top of it, so they will indeed say, 'Yes, I've stood on so and so's shoulders and I saw further.'"
- "Instead of attacking isolated problems, I made the resolution that I would never again solve an isolated problem except as characteristic of a class"
Bonus: Experience with physics-informed or chemistry-focused AI applications. Experience building or fine-tuning large language models. Experience with agent-based systems, tool use or agentic workflows. Contributions to open-source ML projects or published research.
Orbital is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Working at Orbital Industries means working in vertically integrated teams across the full stack, from molecules to manufacturing. We're looking for people who have a love of physical technology, curiosity in AI and a desire to learn.
THE ROLE
Physical engineering is one of the hardest domains for AI. Designs have to meet standards, calculations must be deterministic and checkable, and a wrong number can end up in a power system or a data centre. CurieOS is built to let agents do real engineering work and to show exactly how every output was produced.
The platform team builds the foundation that every workflow, agent and product on CurieOS depends on, and runs it in production for people who need to trust it. Your work sets the floor for how reliable our AI is, and the ceiling for what it can do.
This is a small team, and you'll shape what we build as well as how. You'll see the results of those decisions in production within days. If you want a narrow, well-defined slice of a large system, this isn't the role. If you want to own a platform while it scales, it is.
HOW WE WORK
We build with agents, not just for them. Everyone on the team works with the latest frontier models and coding agents every day, and token budgets won't hold you back. Part of what we build is CurieOS's ability to work on itself: triaging defects, proposing fixes and opening pull requests for engineers to review. So engineers here spend more of their time on design, review and judgement, and less on typing. If you already work this way, you'll feel at home. If you want to see how far it can go, this is the place to find out.
You'll also work alongside our AI researchers, turning cutting-edge research and evals into things that run in the platform and in production.
WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON FIRST
In your first six months you'll work across the parts of CurieOS that customers have to be able to trust. Like everyone on the team you'll touch most of them, and go deepest where your interests take you:
- Tenancy, isolation and identity. How CurieOS keeps each customer separate, from shared multi-tenant accounts to dedicated single-tenant deployments. That covers data isolation, SSO and access control. You'll also be an engineering voice in customer security reviews.
- Release and production. How changes get to production safely: release gates, staged rollouts and rollback, automated smoke tests, on-call and incident response. We ship often, and you'll build what lets us keep doing that without breaking what customers rely on.
- Agent quality in production. Measuring how well agents perform on real customer workflows, working with our researchers to bring the latest evals into the platform, and using those measurements to decide what is good enough to release. A model or prompt change should have to pass the same gate as a code change.
- Observability and cost. Knowing the platform is healthy and what it costs. That means SLOs, tracing and alerting, plus cost telemetry and usage metering for every workflow and every customer, so we can see where model and compute spend goes and make deliberate choices about it.
- Infrastructure and deployment. One standard for how CurieOS is deployed, configured and upgraded in each environment, across our own cloud accounts, GPU capacity and customer-dedicated deployments.
WHERE THE PLATFORM IS GOING
Once those foundations are solid, there's a lot to shape next:
- Traceable results. Provenance for every number an agent produces: which inputs, tools, models and versions went into it, so our users can check it and sign it off.
- Agent runtime and context. How agents plan, call tools, manage context across long-running work and hand off to people at the right moment.
- Durable workflows. Orchestration that survives failures, retries and runs lasting hours, mixing agent steps with deterministic calculations.
At Staff level, you'd set technical direction across these areas, not just within one. You'd own one of them end to end, run the design reviews that our research and forward deployed teams build on, make the architecture calls that are hard to reverse, and help shape how we hire and grow engineers.
OUR STACK
Python services on Kubernetes, running on AWS plus specialist GPU clouds for heavy compute. Strong engineers from Go, Kotlin, Java or a comparable stack will pick up the language quickly. What matters more is that you've run real systems in the cloud.
YOU'LL HAVE MOST OF THESE
- Designed and built backend services that other teams or customers relied on, and made the key decisions yourself.
- Owned a system in production after it shipped: the cloud infrastructure it ran on, on-call, incidents, how changes went out, and the monitoring that told you it was healthy.
- Built and run something where LLMs do real work for real users, and dealt with the cost, latency and quality trade-offs that come with it.
- Used coding agents heavily in your own work, with opinions on where they help and where they break.
- Led a project end to end, made trade-offs you can explain, and raised the bar for the engineers around you.
BONUS POINTS
- Shipped software to external enterprise customers: SSO, tenant isolation, per-customer deployments, security reviews.
- Run infrastructure as code at scale, or GPU workloads across more than one cloud provider.
- Helped a system or a company through a scaling phase, such as a platform going from internal use to many external customers.
- Worked closely with researchers, scientists, engineers or other domain experts and built what they actually needed.
- For Staff: a track record of setting technical direction beyond your own team, such as architecture other teams adopted, a migration you led across several teams, or engineers you've grown into senior roles.
You don't need a background in materials, chemistry or engineering. You'll pick up the domain from the people who have it.
WHY ORBITAL
Orbital Industries is an AI Industrial company. We put frontier AI into the making of critical physical products, from advanced materials to data-centre engineering. Our research team works at the cutting edge, from universal interatomic potentials to GPU-native simulation, and we turn that research into tools engineers…

- Generous, transparent compensation and equity - We hire the best talent and pay to reflect that. We also offer equity as a way to ensure everyone is invested in the success of the company.

- Home office - We will help provide equipment for a comfortable setup so you're as productive at home as you are in the office.

ABOUT THE ROLE
You’ll own security at Trigger.dev: our infrastructure, our app, the runtime that runs our users’ code, and the secrets they trust us with.
Some of our customers let their own users run code on Trigger.dev (think coding agents running whatever instructions they’re given). That code must never reach our systems or our customers’ systems. Keeping it contained is a feature we ship, so this is a product engineering role as much as a security one.
About half to three quarters of your time will be backend engineering. The rest is hunting for problems and fixing them. When you find something, you own the fix. You’ll set your own priorities and work with others when necessary.
We’re looking for an application security (AppSec) engineer who builds: a senior backend engineer who brings a security mindset to everything they ship.
WHAT YOU’LL DO
- Sandbox and runtime security. Design and harden the environments that isolate untrusted user code. This is the core of the role.
- Security features for customers. Build things like end-to-end encrypted secrets, log redaction, private networking, and runtime hardening.
- Automated offensive testing. Use AI tools to attack our own systems on a schedule, find weak spots, and fix them. Bring in outside pen testers when it’s worth it.
- Detection and response. Build monitoring and alerting for suspicious activity, improve our security observability, and lead the response when something needs a look.
- Vulnerability management. Run scanning and triage, own our vulnerability disclosure program, and handle incoming reports.
- Automated quality. Own our security PR reviews, automated scans, fixes, and triage.
- Write it down. Document how we do security so the rest of the team can answer customer questions with confidence.
- Security habits. Help the engineering team build secure habits with reviews, docs, and light guardrails.
Like everyone at Trigger.dev, you’ll also help in our Discord and GitHub community, write docs, and create content like blog posts, code examples, and videos.
WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR
- Senior backend engineer. You design and ship production backend systems yourself.
- AppSec experience. You’ve done hands-on application security work, such as secure code review, threat modelling, pen testing, CTFs or bug bounties. You don’t need a security job title or to have run a security team.
- Cloud operations. You’ve run production systems in the cloud.
- Multi-tenant systems. You’ve built or secured systems where many customers share the same infrastructure.
- TypeScript. You’re comfortable working in it. Our codebase also uses Go and Rust.
- AI-forward. You use AI tools to automate testing, detection, and defense.
- Startup pace. You’ve worked somewhere a step or two ahead of where we are, so you know what good looks like at our size.
- Owner’s mindset. You take work off the team’s plate and fix what you find.
- On call. Reliability and security response are shared across the team.
- In-person time. You’re open to team events a few times a year.
YOU’LL STAND OUT IF YOU HAVE
- Built or hardened sandboxes: containers, microVMs, gVisor, Firecracker, WASM, or similar.
- Secured platforms where customers have their own customers.
- A track record in bug bounties or CTFs.
- Contributed to open source.
- Worked at a developer tools, infrastructure, or open source company.
- Experience with Go or Rust.
BENEFITS
- Compensation and equity. Generous, transparent pay, plus equity so everyone shares in the company’s success.
- Async working. Need a heads-down day or a meeting-free day? No problem.
- Home office. We help with equipment so you’re as productive at home as in the office.
- Vacation. 25 days plus national holidays, sick leave, and generous parental leave.
- Training budget. An annual budget for books, courses, or an Audible subscription.
- Pension. Join our company scheme, or we’ll pay into your private pension.
OUR VALUES
- We’re proud to be open source. We believe in the open source community and in building a great free-to-use product.
- We ship uncomfortably fast. Moving fast is key for a startup. We’re pragmatic about what we build and when.

jobs.ashbyhq.com/siena/91e5e63a-7b02-417.description_excerpt:
MEET SIENA
Siena is the Agent of Record for CX, built for consumer brands like Spanx, FIGS, Brooklinen, and Grüns.
It runs as a connected multi-agent stack on top of a shared intelligence layer: agents that sell, support, listen, handle social and voice across the entire customer journey, turning every conversation into signal you can act on.
THE TEAM
We are a small, fully distributed, global team. We have built leverage into how we work, which is what lets a team this size move at the speed we do.
We hire athletes. Everyone here owns real outcomes, defaults to writing over meetings, communicates with directness, and acts the moment they see something worth acting on. Low ego, high standards, fast clock.
If you want to set the bar rather than follow one, keep reading.
THE ROLE
You'll own meaningful parts of the platform end to end, taking ambiguous problems and shipping reliable, high-performance systems that real brands depend on daily. You'll work closely with product to shape scope, make real architectural calls in your area, and do your best work without being managed task by task. This is for engineers who want ownership and can carry it.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
- Own features and systems across the full stack (frontend, backend, infrastructure) from problem definition through production.
- Partner with product to break down ambiguous scope and ship in iterative, high-impact releases.
- Make real architectural and design decisions in your area, and explain the reasoning so the team can build on it.
- Take cutting-edge language models into enterprise customer workflows, where reliability and safety actually matter.
- Solve hard engineering problems: API performance, microservices, scaling across channels and brands.
- Maintain and improve our AWS infrastructure with a DevOps mindset.
- Raise the bar around you. Share what you know, review thoughtfully, help teammates level up.
WHO YOU ARE
The Bar: if you're missing any of these, this isn't the role for you
- 5+ years shipping and owning systems that are live in production, not personal projects.
- Strong in our core stack: Node.js, React, TypeScript, Express.
- You've shipped LLM-powered features to real users. This is a must, not a bonus. You know what breaks when models meet production traffic.
Strong Signal: not dealbreakers, but what separates a good hire from a great one
- Solid with AWS (Fargate, Lambda, EC2, SQS), PostgreSQL, and Redis.
- Comfortable with CI/CD pipelines (CodePipeline, GitHub Actions, or similar).
- Experienced with microservices and scalable systems.
- Product-focused. You think past the code to customer outcomes and business impact.
- High-ownership and direct. You fix problems without waiting to be told.
Nice to Have: bonus, not required
- Next.js.
- Infrastructure as Code (CDK, Terraform).
- Python.
- Event-driven architecture.
- Background in customer support or CX software.
NOT A FIT IF
- You want tickets assigned to you and a clear spec before you start.
- You've only worked on internal tools, never shipped something real users depend on every day.
- You need a manager checking in regularly to stay motivated.
WHY SIENA?
Real ownership. You will own problems, not tasks, with the autonomy to solve them your way and the trust to do it without a manager in your inbox.
Work that ships and matters. What you build reaches real consumer brands fast.
A category we are creating. The Agent of Record is new ground, with unsolved problems and cutting-edge models, not a crowded field to compete in.
A team that respects your judgment. Globally distributed, async-first, low bureaucracy. We hire adults and treat you like one.
Great salary plus equity or stock grants. Own a piece of what you build.
Learning budget. If you are growing, so are we.
AI-fluency by default. Few places will push your work with production AI further or faster.
OUR VALUES
The people who thrive here are curious, customer-obsessed, and take ownership without being asked. They fix problems first and explain later. They're direct about feedback - both giving and receiving it - because they care more about getting things right than being polite.
They maintain high standards while moving at startup speed, and they build real relationships with teammates because they know that's how great work gets done. When things get tough, they adapt and keep pushing forward.
OUR APPROACH TO AI
The people who thrive here treat AI like a natural extension of themselves. They've built their own ecosystem of agents - some for research, others for debugging, writing, analysis, or writing code. They know which AI works best for what problem.
Everyone gets premium accounts (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity Pro, Cursor, Lovable) plus a quarterly budget for new tools. But the magic happens in how we share knowledge. Demo days where someone shows off a clever workflows. Slack threads about which model handles a specific use case better. Learning from each other's AI workflows.
At Siena, we're not just looking for people who can do a job. We're looking for people who want to break boundaries, create the future, and reshape industries. If that's you, we look forward to your application.
HOW WE HIRE
We use AI-assisted screening tools as part of our hiring process. All decisions are made by humans. You can request a human-only review at talent@siena.cx.
Siena provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Easyship is one of the world’s leading multi-carrier shipping software, built to make global eCommerce borderless. Job Title: Online Merchandiser  (International Returns)
Location: London (Travel to Corby Required Occasionally) 
Reporting to: Head of Programs
Key Relationships: Program Management, Operations & Hub Management, Compliance, eBay

Who We’re Looking For:

Easyship runs eBay’s International Returns programme, and every returned item is an opportunity to recover value. We’re looking for a eCommerce  Merchandiser to own the resale of that returned inventory. You’ll assess and triage returned items, set pricing and resale strategy, list them across resale channels, and keep stock moving so aging inventory stays low. We’re after someone commercially minded and detail-oriented, who enjoys turning returns into revenue and uses data to keep improving the approach.

What would you be responsible for:

  • Assessing, grading, and triaging returned items to decide the best route for each unit.
  • Setting pricing and resale strategy to maximise recovery value, balancing speed of sale against margin.
  • Listing and presenting items across resale channels, with accurate titles, photos, descriptions, and categorisation.
  • Managing stock flow: keeping aging inventory low, clearing slow movers, and prioritising high-value units.
  • Choosing between bulk and individual resale (liquidation lots or piece-by-piece) based on which returns the most value.
  • Tracking recovery rate, sell-through, inventory aging, and margin per unit, and refining strategy based on the results.
  • Working with Program Management, Operations, and Compliance to keep the programme running smoothly.

You Might Be a Good Fit If:

  • You have experience in eCommerce resale, online marketplace selling (eBay or similar), liquidation, or returns and reverse logistics.
  • You have strong commercial and pricing judgement, and you’re comfortable with margin and recovery calculations.
  • You have a sharp eye for detail when grading condition and writing listings.
  • You’re analytical and use data to refine pricing and resale decisions.
  • You’re highly organised and can prioritise high volumes of time-sensitive stock.
  • You thrive in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment and challenge the status quo to get better outcomes.
  • Bonus: liquidation or B2B bulk-lot selling; cross-border shipping and international returns; knowledge of restricted and prohibited goods; experience with inventory or warehouse management systems.

Why You’ll Love Working at Easyship?

  • Competitive compensation with equity options
  • Comprehensive health insurance
  • Gym & wellness reimbursement
  • Work from anywhere for up to 4 weeks per year
  • Generous vacation policy, duvet days, and mental health days

Headquartered in London with offices in New York, Hong Kong, Singapore, Melbourne, Toronto, and Taipei – our team is global and growing. We encourage you to apply if a challenge excites you. Come and join the Easyship team!

Type: Full-time in London (Waterloo, hybrid)

Reports to: Chief Operating Officer

 

What We Do

At Heat Geek, we are tackling one of the UK’s biggest carbon contributors: home heating. Nearly 20% of all UK carbon emissions stems from home heating  – and that contribution is even bigger on a global scale. 

At Heat Geek, we are changing that. By simplifying a traditionally complex industry and revolutionising the technology used by installers, we’re making low-carbon heating mainstream. We have already prevented 2,500,000+ kg of carbon from entering our atmosphere, and we won’t stop there!

 

Join Us!

People are at the core of who we are and what we do. From decreasing homeowners’ energy bills to help with the cost of living, to empowering talented heating engineers to perform outstanding installations, to ensuring a greener world for all of us, we believe in the power of what we can all do together. – And we need passionate, talented, hard working people to be a part of this journey.




Your Mission

Heat Geek is excited to bring a Head of Finance into our team. We want someone to own the finance function end to end: run it tightly, understand what the numbers are telling us, automate aggressively, and turn insight into decisions. You’ll be our number one in finance, working directly with the CEO and COO, and building the team that gets us through the next stage of growth.

If you’re reading this and it resonates with you, we know that you are talented and could do this work anywhere. But we want you to do it HERE, with us, because we need persevering teammates who care about making a real difference in the world.



What you'll own

A tightly run finance function. You’ll bring an auditor’s mindset to how we operate. That means proportionate but robust controls, a clean close, and a monthly set of numbers on Heat Geek’s performance that the leadership team trusts without caveats. P&L against budget and prior periods, balance sheet reviews, cash and debtor discipline, all delivered on time and to a standard you’d be happy to defend.

Analysis and comprehension of the numbers. Producing the numbers is the baseline. You’ll understand them. That means spotting the trend before it becomes a problem, noticing the margin that’s drifting or the cost line that doesn’t add up, and getting to the root cause rather than just reporting it. When something needs attention you’ll flag it clearly at the top of the business and own driving it to resolution. We want someone who reads the monthly pack and tells us what it means, not just what it says.

Data, automation and AI. You’ll make finance a reason Heat Geek excels, not a cost centre that keeps up. You’re technically minded and already use AI tools every day. You’ll own our finance systems and data architecture, integrate them cleanly with the wider platform, build self-serve reporting so budget holders stop waiting for month-end, and set sensible guardrails around accuracy, auditability and data protection. The aim is a function that scales on systems, not headcount.

Business partnering. You’ll bring the numbers to life.   • Establish documented pipelines, an access model for raw and transformed data, and a working intake process for cross-department data requests.
  • Act as a credible point of contact for CoreView's Databricks estate
  • Bring automation and AI-assisted tooling into the day-to-day work — for example automated monitoring and anomaly detection on metric movements — as the platform matures.
