The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-paced, data-driven environment and can quickly learn to navigate a high-tech SaaS product suite. You’ll play a critical role in connecting with prospects, diagnosing alignment between business challenges and our offerings, and helping accelerate the path from lead to opportunity.
 
Job Requirements
  • 1+ year experience in a Sales Development, Business Development, or  Inside Sales role, preferably in SaaS or technology environments.
  • Strong understanding of prospecting best practices and outbound cadencing.
  • Familiarity with prospecting tools (ZoomInfo, LinkedIn Sales Navigator), sequencing platforms (Salesloft, Outreach, Nooks), and CRM systems (Salesforce, HubSpot).
  • Exposure to or curiosity about AI-assisted prospecting tools and data-driven selling approaches.
  • Demonstrated ability to identify high-fit opportunities and manage multiple outreach streams simultaneously.
  • Excellent communication skills—both written and verbal—with the ability to personalize messaging by persona and intent.
  • Self-motivated, detail-oriented, and comfortable working toward measurable KPIs and process adherence.

Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience prospecting into IT, Security, or SaaS leadership personas.
  • Familiarity with Microsoft 365 or cloud-security markets.
  • Proven ability to interpret funnel data, assess lead quality, and make recommendations for campaign improvement.
Job Responsibilities
  • Execute hybrid outbound and inbound prospecting strategy, engaging accounts aligned with marketing campaigns and following up on Marketing Qualified Leads (MQLs) in territory.
  • Review top-of-funnel data and campaign engagement insights to prioritize accounts and prospects efficiently.
  • Research target organizations to identify key stakeholders and tailor outreach based on persona, use case, and buying triggers.
  • Conduct high-quality conversations that uncover prospect pain points, evaluate fit, and position relevant product offerings.
  • Partner closely with Account Executives, Marketing, and Product teams to ensure smooth lead handoffs and accurate pipeline tracking.
  • Maintain detailed activity tracking and follow-up consistency across CRM and sequencing tools.
  • Analyze performance metrics (conversion rate, meetings booked, pipeline influenced) and contribute insights on campaign and prospecting trends.
  • Participate in regular training, enablement, and process reviews to continuously refine skills and messaging.

Coreview Values

Ownership Mindset: Take ownership. Drive outcomes. 

One Team: One team, one goal, embracing diversity - to achieve more together. 

Velocity: Decide fast. Deliver fast. Repeat.

Continuous Improvement: Curiosity drives us. We challenge the status quo.

Customer First: Listen deeply. Solve boldly.  

Resilience: Steady under pressure.

job-boards.greenhouse.io/doitintl/jobs/8.description_excerpt:
Location

Our GTM Systems Engineer will be an integral part of our Enterprise Systems team. This role is based remotely as a full-time employee in the UK, Ireland, Estonia, the Netherlands, or Sweden. We are also open to contractors in Eastern Europe and Portugal.

The Opportunity
We're looking for an engineering-minded owner of the systems our Sales, Marketing and Revenue Operations teams run on: CRM, marketing automation, CPQ and the tools around them. This is not a ticket-queue role. Business teams will bring you solutions ("add a field", "build me a report"). Your job is to find the problem behind the request and see how a change affects every connected system. Then fix it once, ideally so the next person can do it themselves without filing a request. You'll have an internal engineering team to lean on, and you'll use AI tools daily to build faster.

Responsibilities

  • Own the GTM systems as one connected whole: know how CRM, CPQ, marketing automation and sales-engagement tools share data, and design every change with that in view.
  • Turn requests into problems: ask what the business is trying to solve, propose options, explain trade-offs, and say "no" or "not like that" when it's the right call.
  • Remove recurring manual work: measure the effort, then replace it with automation or self-service tools that business users run themselves.
  • Build automations, small tools and integrations, choosing the simplest approach that will hold up.
  • Keep the data model lean and trustworthy: retire unused fields and legacy workarounds, and enforce data quality where data enters rather than cleaning it up later.
  • Keep integrations reliable: use native connectors where they do the job; where something custom is needed, respect API limits, add error handling and monitoring, and keep sandbox and production consistent. Collaborate with our internal engineering team as necessary.
  • Use AI tools to build, investigate issues, and speed up routine work.
  • Provide EMEA-hours support for the GTM stack, and use what you see there to pick the next fix.
  • Document changes and follow change management from sandbox to production.
  • Current Sales/Marketing Tech Stack: Salesforce, Dealhub CPQ, Hubspot, ZoomInfo, Gong Professional, Gong Engage, Gong Forecasting, Lusha, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Dripify, Ringlead

Qualifications

  • 3+ years hands-on with Salesforce Sales Cloud (advanced Flow, data and security model), plus HubSpot and/or DealHub CPQ.
  • Working knowledge of Apex, SOQL and REST APIs, and able to write scripts in Python or JavaScript.
  • A track record of replacing manual processes with automation or self-service, with before-and-after examples.
  • Systems thinking: good judgment about where logic and data should live across connected systems.
  • Understanding of lead-to-quote-to-close and the marketing funnel (lead lifecycle, attribution).
  • Comfortable using AI coding and automation tools every day.
  • Clear communicator who can push back on requests with reasons, and works well with business users and engineers.
  • Fluent English, additional languages are a plus.
  • Ability to work in the country of residence (we do not provide visa sponsorship).

Nice to have:

  • Salesforce Platform App Builder or Platform Developer I certification;
  • Git/SFDX; depth in Gong, ZoomInfo or HubSpot; cloud platform experience;
  • experience with an integration platform or event-driven systems.

    Are you a Do’er?
    Be your truest self. Work on your terms. Make a difference.
    We are home to a global team of incredible talent who work remotely and have the flexibility to have a schedule that balances your work and home life. We embrace and support leveling up your skills professionally and personally. 
    What does being a Do’er mean? We’re all about being entrepreneurial, pursuing knowledge, and having fun! Click here to learn more about our core values. 

Sounds too good to be true? Check out our Glassdoor Page. We thought so too, but we’re here and happy we hit that ‘apply’ button. 

Full-time employee benefits include:

  • Unlimited Vacation
  • Flexible Working Options
  • Health Insurance
  • Parental Leave
  • Employee Stock Option Plan
  • Home Office Allowance
  • Professional Development Stipend 
  • Peer Recognition Program

Many Do’ers, One Team
DoiT unites as Many Do’ers, One Team, where diversity is more than a goal—it's our strength. We actively cultivate an inclusive, equitable workplace, recognizing that each unique perspective enhances our innovation. By celebrating differences, we create an environment where every individual feels valued, contributing to our collective success.

job-boards.greenhouse.io/insurtechinsigh.description_excerpt:
Are you commercially driven, excited by the idea of building a career in sales, and looking to join an ambitious, entrepreneurial team? Cool, this might be for you!

The role

You’ll be responsible for selling delegate passes to senior professionals attending our international conferences.

This is a high-performance, phone-based B2B sales role. You’ll proactively reach out to prospective delegates, including previous conference attendees and existing leads, build relationships, manage your own pipeline and take opportunities from first conversation through to close.

What we’re looking for

We’re looking for someone who genuinely wants to sell and is motivated by targets, performance and winning.

You should have:

  • At least 1 year of B2B sales experience, ideally in a phone-based sales, outbound sales or telesales environment.

  • Experience proactively contacting leads, building relationships and converting opportunities into sales.

  • A strong commercial mindset and motivation to hit and exceed revenue targets.

  • Confidence speaking with new people and the ability to build rapport quickly.

  • Resilience and persistence – you’re comfortable hearing “no” and continuing to push for results.

  • A high level of ownership over your pipeline, follow-ups and performance.

  • A desire to learn, improve and develop quickly.

This role might not be the right fit if...

  • You don't enjoy spending a significant part of your day on the phone, speaking with prospective customers.

  • You prefer a role focused on relationship management rather than actively driving sales.

  • You’re uncomfortable working towards clear sales and revenue targets.

  • You’re looking for a hybrid or remote position – our London team works together from the office five days a week.

What you’ll do

  • Generate new business by proactively reaching out to prospective delegates.

  • Sell delegate passes to senior professionals across Europe.

  • Manage your sales pipeline from initial contact through to close.

  • Work towards ambitious individual revenue targets.

  • Develop a strong understanding of our conferences, audiences and industries.

What we offer

  • Competitive base salary plus an uncapped commission structure.

  • Ongoing sales training, coaching and feedback.

  • Fast career progression with significant responsibility for high performers.

  • International exposure and opportunities to travel to our conferences.

  • 25 days’ holiday plus company pension contribution.

  • Regular team socials, lunches and events.

About us

Insurtech Insights is a global insurance technology community connecting executives, entrepreneurs, investors and innovators. Through our international conferences and media platforms, we bring together leaders shaping the future of insurance, creating opportunities to share insights, explore new technologies and build meaningful business relationships.

Insurtech Insights is part of United Media, a global B2B media and conferences group.

Start date: As soon as possible.

Monday–Friday, we work from our WeWork office in Victoria, London. Due to the collaborative nature of our work, we do not offer remote work.

You must have the right to work in the UK.

HELLO…We’re looking for an Account Director!

 

Who are we?

We’re Mediahub, the industry’s best kept secret. This year we got our first Campaign School Report, coming in at number one for building the most ethnically diverse team in the industry.  COMvergence rank us as the UK's fastest growing media agency for the second year running.

We bring a challenger mindset to everything we do. Brands choose to work with us to disrupt category norms.

We offer the best of both worlds.  A start-up culture backed by Mediabrands.

Just some of the brands we work with – New Balance, Pinterest, FarFetch.

You’ll be joining an agency that is for everyone.

We live by our values:

  • Anticipate tomorrow - we are challengers, we are proactive in thinking about what needs to happen today in order to make tomorrow better
  • Hustle from the heart - we move fast, take ownership, and look out for each other
  • Perform with pride - we take pride and care in what we do and we strive for excellence
  • Believe you can - believe in yourself to make a difference; believe in each other to do great things
  • Stay curious - we have fun on the journey of discovery

 

What will you do?

In this exciting role, you'll be responsible for the overall direction, development, and performance of our clients business in the DIY sector. You will be accountable for the client relationship as well as the performance and development of the team. This role covers full-service media planning and buying across Display, Paid social, TV, press, OOH & radio. 

You’ll be working with a wider team of media strategists, individual channel specialists and our data teams. We plan & buy activity across all channels working closely with specialist teams in IPG to support at key points. 

 

About You

Passionate about media & communications; you see how effective media campaigns make a real difference to a client’s business. You'll have a few years demonstrable experience in a media agency in an account handling role, being a cross channel planning/buying aficionado, with a head for numbers and a heart for creativity.

You are curious about the industry and excited about learning and continued development, bringing the same to your media plans. You'll have the ability to think strategically and look for creative solutions to briefs and commercial opportunities to grow clients. With a solid background in team leadership and management, you'll enjoy nurturing talent and helping them to achieve their goals.

 

Benefits

Hybrid working, flexible working hours, 25 days holiday plus your birthday off, healthcare, volunteer days, cycle to work scheme, gym discounts, Pilates and yoga classes and just about everything else you can think of! Dedicated to our people, we provide extensive benefits to help with that work life balance. We focus on great people, great work, effectiveness, creativity and passion. If that sounds like the place for you then we want to meet you!

 

Mediahub is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

We are looking for someone with demonstrable senior strategy experience who thrives on exploring changing consumer behavior, global trends, and competitive insights to discover new innovative solutions. About the Role

As a Customer Data Engineer, you will be a part of a strong energetic and fast-growing global team. You will be an integral part of clients' ongoing data requests and projects. You will be working closely with internal CSM teams as well as interacting directly with clients’ data teams across different business verticals. Your core responsibilities will involve playing an active role in collaborating with internal teams to construct tailored data transformations and manipulations while working with top-notch technology (Cloud tech etc.) The ideal candidate is an SQL whiz with a strong work ethic, robust analytical and technical capabilities, and highly effective time management skills. We are looking for a master multi-tasker who thrives in challenging, fast-paced environments, with agility and ease.

The Customer Data Engineer is a position that brings with it an excellent opportunity to learn and grow within a rapidly expanding company on the cutting edge of Martech.

Responsibilities: 

  • Develop and support a wide range of data transformations and migrations
  • Construct custom ETL processes: Design and implementation of data pipelines and data marts, access versatile data sources, and apply data quality measures
  • Investigate data mismatches and apply solutions
  • Work side by side and support the Customer Success teams in order to meet customer business needs.
  • Interact with clients to understand business needs and collaborate on project scopes, planning, and execution.

Requirements:

  • 1-3 years of experience in a similar technical client-facing position, OR graduate with a degree in STEM
  • Experience with databases and SQL - a Must
  • Outstanding technical and analytical skills
  • Highly motivated with an exceptional work ethic
  • High attention to detail with an ability to work on multiple projects simultaneously
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills
  • Quick, self-learning capabilities and creativity in problem-solving
  • This is a hybrid role, and you will be required in our Dundee office 2 days per week
  • Must be eligible to work in the UK – we are unable to provide sponsorship at this time 

Preferred:

  • Familiarity with Python
  • Familiarity with Airflow, ETL tools, Snowflake and MSSQL
  • Hands-on with VCS (Git)
  • Genuinely curious and already reaching for AI tools to work smarter (or itching to). This matters to us more than it might elsewhere

We’re committed to helping our people grow in an inclusive, supportive workplace recognised as one of the UK’s Best Workplaces in Tech and for Wellbeing.

We consider all qualified applicants fairly, without regard to race, ethnicity, gender, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. If you require any adjustments during the recruitment process, please let us know.

We're looking for an ML Data & Platform Engineer to own the infrastructure that powers our speech AI models: the pipelines that source and prepare training data, and the platform that trains, evaluates, and serves them in production. Speech AI has a data problem most ML teams don't, and you'll be at the centre of solving it, working as part of our ML team to remove friction across the entire lifecycle and get better models into production faster.

This is a broad, cross-functional role suited to someone who enjoys working across the full stack: data infrastructure, distributed systems, and production ML, and who takes ownership of problems end to end rather than waiting to be told what to fix.

What you'll do

  • Designing, building, and maintaining scalable data pipelines for ingesting, transforming, validating, and storing large datasets used to train our models
  • Developing and maintaining web scraping and data acquisition solutions to keep training datasets fresh, high-quality, and available at scale
  • Building and operating the infrastructure that lets the ML team deploy and evaluate new models quickly, and that serves models efficiently and reliably in production
  • Optimising infrastructure for both iteration speed and production reliability, including GPU utilisation, job scheduling, and training efficiency
  • Implementing observability (monitoring, logging, alerting) across data pipelines and ML systems to catch issues early and keep things running smoothly
  • Troubleshooting complex issues across distributed systems, spanning data infrastructure, training, and inference
  • Continuously improving our data and MLOps practices, and helping shape the roadmap for how our platform evolves as we scale

What you'll need

  • Strong proficiency in Python and SQL, with a solid backend or data engineering foundation
  • Hands-on experience with containerisation and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes), and working with a major cloud provider
  • Experience building data pipelines and ETL/ELT processes at scale, including web scraping or automated data collection
  • A solid understanding of the ML lifecycle, from data through to model training, evaluation, and serving
  • Experience with data quality practices (validation, cleaning, normalisation) and/or production-grade observability
  • Ability to design resilient, scalable architectures, and comfort operating and troubleshooting distributed systems
  • MLOps experience, for example model serving, experiment tracking, GPU/distributed training optimisation, or reproducible ML workflows
  • A self-starter mentality: comfortable identifying problems and driving fixes without needing detailed direction

*This position is fully remote/home based. Applications will be accepted from candidates based in the UK and the following US states: FL, IL, MA, MD, NY, PA, TX, VA.

 

Role Summary 

The Associate Director, Publishing provides strategic leadership for the PLOS journal portfolio, ensuring that portfolio priorities, publishing investments, and journal development strategies align with organizational goals and advance PLOS's mission. 

Reporting to the Director, Publishing & Publishing Operations, the Associate Director leads and develops a team of Publishers responsible for the performance and strategic development of journals portfolios. The Associate Director serves as the primary steward of portfolio-wide publishing performance, translating organizational strategy into clear priorities and ensuring effective coordination across the organization. 

The Associate Director uses publishing data, financial information, market intelligence, and research community insight to guide strategic decisions, establish priorities, identify opportunities for growth and innovation, and manage risks. Working in partnership with the Director, Publishing & Publishing Operations, the Associate Director ensures that journal-level strategies collectively support a sustainable PLOS portfolio with a strong value proposition. 

Supervisory Responsibilities 

  • Lead, develop, and support a team of senior publishing professionals responsible for journal and subject portfolio performance. 
  • Establish clear goals, priorities, and measures of accountability that align with organizational and portfolio strategy. 
  • Provide coaching, professional development, succession planning, and performance management for direct reports. 
  • Foster a culture of collaboration, inclusion, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement. 
  • Work with Publishers to ensure effective leadership and development of Journal Development Managers and other publishing staff. 

Responsibilities 

Portfolio Strategy and Performance 

  • Develop and implement a portfolio-wide publishing strategy aligned with PLOS's mission and organizational objectives. 
  • Ensure that journal and subject portfolio strategies collectively support a clear and differentiated value proposition for the PLOS portfolio. 
  • Lead regular portfolio reviews and develop recommendations regarding journal positioning, growth opportunities, performance, and future direction. 
  • Balance the needs of individual journals and research communities with broader portfolio and organizational objectives. 
  • Support Publishers in identifying and responding to changes in research communities, funding policies, scholarly communication, and the publishing market.
  • Develop consistent approaches and decision-making frameworks for evaluating proposals, opportunities, and performance across the portfolio. 
  • Guide the evaluation and development of new journals, products, services, publishing models in line with PLOS’s strategic direction.  

Strategic and Business Leadership 

  • Translate organizational strategy into clear portfolio priorities, objectives, and plans for the publishing team. 
  • Oversee publishing budgets and forecasts in partnership with the Director and Publishers, ensuring responsible decision-making and effective resource allocation. 
  • Act as a thought partner to, and deputize for, the Director, Publishing & Publishing Operations when appropriate. 
  • In close collaboration with colleagues in Editorial, Sales and Global Publishing Development, support publishers in developing impactful relationships with Editors-in-Chief, Editorial Board members, researchers, institutions, societies, and partner organizations.

Role Summary

The PLOS Publication Ethics team works to uphold the integrity and reliability of PLOS publications and supports PLOS journals in publication ethics-related issues and policy development. The team also engages with external parties and organizations in publication ethics-related discussions and initiatives.

As a Senior Editor, Publication Ethics, you investigate and resolve publication ethics cases for all PLOS journals, provide publication ethics support to PLOS journal teams, and contribute to team-level initiatives and projects that address ethics and integrity issues at PLOS.

This role is in the Publication Ethics team’s standard case group. This group’s primary case work responsibilities cover a broad array of integrity issues (e.g., image/data integrity, animal/human research ethics, authorship or data ownership disputes, etc.) that typically involve individual articles or research groups. Editors within this group may also be asked to contribute to work involving large-scale cases, as needed.

Responsibilities

  • Resolve publication ethics cases efficiently and in line with PLOS standards and COPE guidance; provide timely support for others’ publication ethics case work; address escalations and queries about publication ethics issues; prevent reputational damage to PLOS journals as feasible.
  • Contribute as requested to tasks, cases, documentation, and other processes needed to support the team’s casework and other objectives.
  • Contribute to team-level and/or cross-functional initiatives and projects that address ethics and integrity issues at PLOS. (e.g., development of workflows or policy updates; development, trials, and/or implementation of approaches to improve detection, prevention, and/or resolution of publication ethics cases)

  • Maintain an awareness of cross-industry issues and initiatives and attend COPE Forums that fall within your working hours.
  • Help with recruitment and onboarding for vacant team positions and help to train staff on other PLOS teams in publication ethics case management and standards. Provide training and feedback for other Publication Ethics team members as needed.

Qualifications

  • First-hand experience resolving publication ethics cases in STM publishing

Role Summary

PLOS is a nonprofit Open Access publisher with an ambitious mission: to help transform research communication so that science can be shared, understood and used more effectively. We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to join our Product team for a 12-month maternity cover contract. It's an interesting time to join us. 

Research publishing is changing rapidly. Researchers' expectations are changing. Technology is creating possibilities that didn't exist a few years ago. And at PLOS we're rethinking some of the services, systems and assumptions that have shaped scholarly publishing for decades. 

That means there are interesting product problems to solve - not just features to deliver. 

You'll take responsibility for a product area and work with designers, engineers and colleagues across PLOS to understand the problems that matter, work out where we can make the greatest difference and help the team learn its way towards good solutions. 

Although this is a fixed-term role, it isn't a caretaker role. You'll be joining active product teams working on significant problems and will have plenty of opportunity to shape what we do and how we do it. 

How we work 

We want our product teams to be curious, evidence-led and comfortable with uncertainty. 

We don't expect a Product Manager to arrive with all the answers. We do expect them to ask good questions. 

You'll use continuous discovery alongside delivery: spending time with users, looking at data, understanding the wider service, identifying assumptions and finding practical ways to test them. 

You'll help the team break large problems into smaller things we can learn from, rather than waiting until everything is known before we release something. 

And you'll make the team's thinking visible - explaining what we're trying to achieve, what we've learned, what we're uncertain about and why we're making the choices we are. 

Responsibilities

As a Senior Product Manager, you'll: 

  • Understand the problem. Build a deep understanding of our users, their needs and behaviours, as well as the organisational, operational and technical context surrounding them. 
  • Shape product direction. Work out where the greatest opportunities lie within your area and help translate PLOS's objectives into clear product outcomes and priorities. 
  • Practise continuous discovery. Work closely with design, engineering and others to explore problems, identify assumptions and regularly test ideas with users and through data. 
  • Turn uncertainty into learning. Frame hypotheses, design useful experiments and look for the smallest sensible way to learn whether we're heading in the right direction. 
  • Make good product decisions. Weigh evidence, impact, effort, risk and opportunity when deciding what to pursue - and what not to pursue. 
  • Measure whether things are getting better. Define useful measures of success and use qualitative and quantitative evidence to understand whether our work is having the intended effect.

You've been a strong data engineer or data lead for years, and you're comfortable in front of a client as well as in a pull request. Technical

Not theoretical, evidenced by things you've actually shipped, and deep enough to set the bar for a team and answer a sceptical client:

The role

Tavily, part of Nebius, is the web access layer for AI agents. Over two million developers use us, and our customers include Fortune 500 companies running agents in production.

We build and run our own index. That means we own the hard problems directly: crawl coverage at scale, freshness, cost per query, and the quality of what comes back. This role owns that infrastructure as a product.

When an agent asks a question, the answer has to be relevant, fresh, fast, and affordable. Those four things pull against each other, and someone has to decide which one gives. That is you. You will set what good means for each use case we serve and the bar a change has to clear before it ships, working closely with our evaluation team, who own how we measure it. You will also shape where our index goes next: what it needs to cover, how fresh it needs to be, and what it has to be good at.

The most open part of the job is what comes next. Search is being rebuilt for a consumer that is not a person. Agents do not want one result page, they want to break a problem apart, run many retrievals, and decide what to do next. That changes what search infrastructure should look like, and part of your job is to have a view on where ours should go.

The hard part is deciding what good enough means. Perfect coverage, perfect freshness, and low cost cannot all be true at once, and the person in this seat is the one who has to make that call for each use case and defend it.

In your first year, we expect you to set a clear quality bar for our search products that the team builds against, have a real influence on where our index goes next, and bring us a point of view on where search infrastructure is heading.

This is a hands-on senior IC role with real ownership, reporting to the Director of Product. You will work day to day with our search engineering and research teams, with the evaluation team, and with customer success, who bring us quality feedback from real accounts every week. Our search engineers are deeply experienced in large-scale retrieval, and the product team is small, so you will argue your case directly with the people building it. That only works if you have built at this scale yourself.

Your responsibilities will include:

This is a hands-on senior IC role with real ownership. You will work within a small PM team reporting to the Director of Product, alongside engineering, research, data, and go-to-market.

About Tavily 

We're building the infrastructure layer for agentic web interaction at scale. Our API is designed from the ground up to power Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and real-time reasoning in AI systems. By connecting LLMs to high-quality, trustworthy web content, we help developers build agents that are not only intelligent — but also informed. 

We work with some of the most innovative teams in AI — from small startups shaping the ecosystem to the largest enterprises deploying AI at scale. Whether it's powering sales assistants, research copilots, or internal knowledge tools, we're the missing link between LLMs and the real world. 

The Role

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to work on the web access infrastructure of a novel search engine tailored for agentic AI consumption.

In this role, you will focus on making our access to public web content reliable and efficient. You will investigate how modern websites and browsers communicate across the full request lifecycle, find the root cause when a request fails or returns something unexpected, and build the fixes into production systems operating at internet scale. Your work ensures that high-quality content is consistently available to the crawling, indexing and retrieval systems downstream.

In this position, your responsibility will be to

  • Diagnose failed or degraded requests at the right layer: network and IP, TLS and HTTP/2 behavior, headers and session state, client-side scripts, or browser characteristics
  • Analyze how websites verify and classify clients, including how client-side scripts and protocol-level behavior shape what a site serves to different clients
  • Build clients and tooling that behave consistently and compatibly with standard browsers across all of these layers, using a real browser where a lightweight client is not enough
  • Monitor access quality as websites change: detect regressions, find the cause, and measure success on real content rather than on status codes
  • Build the tooling to do this at scale: traffic capture and comparison against real browsers, per-site and per-method success tracking, and the cost of each successful fetch
  • Choose the fetch method for each host, from a lightweight HTTP client to a full browser, balancing quality against cost

You may be a good fit if you

Have 5+ years of experience building production systems, and are an expert in several of the following areas.

The request lifecycle

  • HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, TLS handshakes and TLS fingerprints (JA3/JA4), and header behavior
  • What a server can observe at each step of a request, and what a client controls at each step
  • A debugging method, not guesses: replaying captured browser traffic, comparing against a real browser on the same network path, and changing one variable at a time

Client-side analysis

  • Reading and analyzing complex or obfuscated JavaScript, and observing what a script measures by hooking browser APIs
  • How browser, device and network characteristics are measured (canvas, fonts, WebGL, screen and window metrics) and how consistent they are across layers
  • Browser instrumentation and the Chrome DevTools Protocol, used as tools for investigation

Running it for real

  • Have run this in production and can give numbers: requests per day, sites or hosts, and the success rate and how you measured it
  • Strong programming in at least one of Go, Python, Rust or C++

Strong candidates may also have experience with

  • Working at a web data provider, a browser or web-security company, or a company that collects data from complex sources
  • Contributions to browser networking or fingerprinting-related open-source tooling, or public write-ups of how client verification works
  • Building or maintaining a patched browser
  • Networks, proxies and IP reputation
  • Internet-scale distributed systems, Kubernetes and cloud infrastructure

The kind of problems you will work on

  • A site returns a different response to our client than to Chrome on the same network path. Find out why, and fix that cause.
  • A site changes how it verifies clients and success drops across a group of sites. Find what changed, adapt, and make the next change cheaper to catch.
  • Switching to a browser-like network profile makes results worse on some hosts. Work out what no longer matches.

We conduct coding interviews as part of the process.

About Tavily 

We're building the infrastructure layer for agentic web interaction at scale. Our API is designed from the ground up to power Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and real-time reasoning in AI systems. The Role

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to work on the rendering infrastructure of a novel search engine tailored for agentic AI consumption.

In this role, you will focus on loading modern web pages in a browser that we patch and build ourselves, so that content is rendered completely and reliably at a cost that works across billions of pages. You will work inside Chromium to remove what we do not need, make the rest faster and cheaper, and keep our build current as Chromium moves. Your work ensures that high-quality content is consistently available to the indexing and retrieval systems downstream.

In this position, your responsibility will be to

  • Change Chromium in its heavy core (Blink, the V8 integration, the compositor, the network service) to cut CPU, memory and startup cost per page
  • Strip Chromium down for agent workloads: skip what nobody needs, such as image and media decoding, web font downloads, and rasterization and GPU work where no one needs pixels, while keeping what page scripts depend on to run correctly (style, layout, animation frames, observers), and work out what breaks, or renders differently, when you do
  • Keep the browser compatible with the web: make sure that what we remove does not change how the sites we load behave or render
  • Profile and tune fleets of browsers: the process model, memory per renderer, startup, isolation and crash handling
  • Build the production system around it: how browsers are launched, pooled, recycled and monitored

You may be a good fit if you

Have 5+ years of experience building production systems, and are an expert in several of the following areas.

Inside the browser

  • Strong C++ in a large, performance-critical codebase, ideally Chromium, Blink or V8, or a comparable browser engine (Rust is a plus)
  • Chromium architecture: the process model, Mojo IPC, the rendering pipeline (DOM, style, layout, paint, compositing), and the network service
  • Building, debugging and shipping custom Chromium builds: the build system, tracing, crash analysis, and maintaining patches across releases

Performance and systems

  • Profiling CPU, memory and I/O for browser fleets, with tools such as perf, tracing and flame graphs
  • Linux process isolation and resource management, concurrency, and memory management
  • Have run browsers in production, or built the infrastructure that does, and can describe where the time and memory went

Strong candidates may also have experience with

  • Contributions to Chromium, Blink, V8, Firefox, WebKit or another browser engine
  • Building or maintaining a patched browser that you wrote the patches for
  • Browser instrumentation, including the Chrome DevTools Protocol
  • Working familiarity with how modern frontend frameworks render (SSR, CSR, streaming, hydration)
  • Distributed systems, Kubernetes, and Go or Python

The kind of problems you will work on

  • Cut the cost of loading a page in half. Where do CPU and memory go, and what would you change in the browser?
  • Turn off the GPU and image decoding for agent workloads. What breaks, and what changes in how pages load and render?
  • A page runs a script that never yields. How do we detect and stop it without help from the page?
  • Chromium ships a new version. How do we bring a large set of patches forward in days, not weeks?
  • Decide when a page is finished, for pages with analytics beacons, long polling and endless scrolling.

We conduct coding interviews as part of the process.

You will investigate difficult issues, communicate clearly with customers, collaborate with Product and Engineering, and help strengthen the team’s technical capability through knowledge sharing and mentoring.

The CORE team supports customers across areas including Single Sign-On, SMTP, APIs, Data Discovery, Certification Automation integrations, tenant-wide performance issues, integration workflows, and integration requests.

Your Mission

  • Own and resolve complex CORE support cases escalated from Support Analysts, taking responsibility from initial investigation through resolution or an effective engineering handoff.

  • Troubleshoot advanced issues across SSO, SAML, SMTP, APIs, integrations, workflows, Data Discovery, and related platform capabilities.

  • Reproduce customer issues in appropriate test or support environments and use available evidence to identify probable causes and practical resolutions.

  • Analyse logs, trace information, configuration details, API requests, integration behaviour, and other technical evidence to isolate issues.

  • Provide clear, structured customer communication, including acknowledgement, investigation updates, action plans, and resolution explanations.

  • Determine when an issue requires escalation to Product or Engineering and raise high-quality Jira tickets with the relevant troubleshooting, evidence, impact, and technical questions.

  • Work closely with Product, Engineering, Incident Management, and other Support teams to drive complex issues to resolution.

  • Identify recurring issues, documentation gaps, workflow improvements, and opportunities to reduce repeat contacts and escalations.

  • Mentor and support other analysts through case reviews, technical guidance, troubleshooting walkthroughs, and knowledge-sharing sessions.

  • Contribute to onboarding and enablement for new analysts joining the CORE team.

  • Maintain strong case ownership, accurate documentation, timely updates, and adherence to support processes and service-level expectations.

  • Continue building expertise through product releases, technical training, office hours, hands-on investigation, and relevant certifications.

You Are

  • 2+ years of experience in a technical customer support, technical account support, SaaS support, application support, or similar role.

  • Demonstrated experience handling complex technical issues and escalations in a customer-facing environment.

  • Hands-on experience troubleshooting at least one major cloud platform: AWS, GCP, or Azure. Experience with all three is not required, but strong practical depth in one is essential.

  • Strong troubleshooting skills and the ability to work methodically from symptoms and evidence to a clear diagnosis.

  • Experience supporting integrations involving identity providers, APIs, data connectors, or workflow automation.

  • Practical understanding of several of the following areas:

    • SSO, SAML, identity providers, certificates, and authentication flows

    • SMTP, email delivery, connection testing, and email-related troubleshooting

    • REST APIs, authentication, request/response analysis, and tools such as Postman

    • SaaS integrations, workflows, web technologies, and system dependencies

    • Logs, traces, monitoring tools, and root-cause analysis

  • Ability to explain technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Strong written and verbal English communication skills.

  • Experience working with ticketing and engineering collaboration tools, such as Salesforce and Jira.

Milltown Partners
Our clients operate at the frontiers of innovation - we advise technology companies driving change, global investors funding the future, the giants of sport and entertainment, and influential individuals on the communications and policy challenges that define their reputations. Our work spans corporate and financial communications, policy and public affairs to engage regulators and policymakers, policy communications and leadership communications. We underpin the full breadth of our capabilities with research-driven insights and campaigns. We're also pioneering AI-enhanced advisory work for both our clients and internal innovation, using technology to unlock insights from data at unprecedented scale and speed.
The role
Our Associate Directors are experienced communications leaders who combine real advisory authority with a genuine appetite to keep developing – working alongside senior leaders to deliver exceptional client work and grow their own leadership capabilities.
Your work could span AI companies defining responsible innovation, investors backing the next generation of technology, sports franchises building global audiences, and leaders whose decisions shape industries. The clients are category-defining. The challenges are complex. The standards are uncompromising.
You'll lead client relationships, shape strategic direction, and ensure the work your teams deliver consistently meets the highest standards. This is a hands-on role. You'll advise clients directly and play an active part in delivering work alongside your teams, not just directing from a distance. Beyond client delivery, you'll build your external network, contribute to new business opportunities, and support the development of colleagues at earlier stages of their careers.
What you'll do
Lead client work
You'll take strategic responsibility for our clients’ most important communications challenges, whether that's navigating policy debates, preparing for major announcements, or protecting reputation when stakes are highest. . You'll build the trust that lets you deliver genuinely impactful advice, drawing on the full resources of the firm to help clients build and defend their reputations.
Drive teams and develop colleagues
You'll structure work clearly, delegate effectively, and hold yourself and others to high standards. You'll coach colleagues on your teams, sharing your experience in ways that help them develop their own advisory instincts. You'll work alongside your peers to lead and inspire colleagues across our European team, fostering a culture where exceptional advice, continuous learning and collaboration are the norm.
Contribute to AI-enhanced advisory
You'll help drive how we're using AI to transform the quality and precision of our work. You'll guide colleagues in developing AI capabilities, document and share best practice across the firm, and push the boundaries of what's possible in advisory work through technology.
Support business development
You'll identify and contribute to converting new opportunities and extending existing client relationships. You'll cultivate an external network that's useful to clients and the firm, and you'll bring an entrepreneurial mindset to how you think about growth – whether that's identifying new ways to help existing clients or contributing to pitches and proposals.
Shape our culture
You'll give and receive regular feedback at all levels, demonstrate allyship to colleagues, actively seek input from others, and support the wellbeing of everyone on the team. You'll contribute to a culture where brilliance, restlessness, comradeship, inclusivity and integrity aren't just values - they're how we operate every day.
What we're looking for
Why join us

Cloud Solution Architect - Data & AI

Location: UK (Hybrid)
Practice: Data & AI

About HSO

HSO is a Business Transformation Partner with deep industry expertise and global reach. As one of Microsoft's leading partners, we help organisations unlock the full potential of Microsoft Dynamics 365, Azure, Data and AI technologies to deliver meaningful business outcomes.

With operations across Europe, North America and Asia, HSO combines industry knowledge, technical excellence and a people-first culture to help customers modernise their businesses, transform operations and embrace innovation with confidence.

As demand for Data & AI solutions continues to accelerate, we're expanding our Data & AI practice and looking for experienced Cloud Solution Architects to help shape the next generation of customer transformation programmes.

The Role

As a Cloud Solution Architect - Data & AI, you'll play a pivotal role in shaping and qualifying customer opportunities across the Microsoft cloud ecosystem.

This is a highly visible role that sits at the intersection of sales, enterprise architecture and delivery, combining technical leadership with commercial thinking. You'll work closely with customers, Microsoft and internal stakeholders to understand business challenges, identify opportunities, design compelling solutions and create clear pathways from initial discovery through to successful delivery.

You'll help organisations transform the way they use data, analytics and artificial intelligence, translating business ambition into practical, costed and deliverable solutions.

Success in this role requires more than technical expertise. You'll need strong consulting and stakeholder management skills, the confidence to challenge assumptions, and the commercial awareness to ensure opportunities are both valuable for clients and aligned with HSO's delivery capability.

What You'll Be Doing

Opportunity Qualification & Solution Shaping

  • Lead Data & AI opportunity qualification alongside Account Managers, Business Development teams and Enterprise Architects.
  • Facilitate customer discovery workshops, architecture assessments and strategic discussions.
  • Understand customer business drivers, challenges and desired outcomes.
  • Help customers define realistic transformation roadmaps aligned to business priorities.
  • Qualify opportunities using structured sales and consulting methodologies, including MEDDIC/MEDDICC approaches.

Solution Architecture & Advisory

  • Design end-to-end Data & AI solutions using Microsoft technologies and best practices.
  • Shape modern analytics, AI and data platform architectures that are commercially viable and technically deliverable.
  • Provide architectural leadership across data platform modernisation, analytics, AI and automation initiatives.
  • Ensure alignment with Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework and Azure Well-Architected principles.
  • Communicate architectural trade-offs and recommendations to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Commercial Leadership

  • Translate customer requirements into proposals, statements of work, delivery plans and business cases.
  • Produce solution estimates, cost models and phased implementation approaches.
  • Support customers in understanding ROI, value realisation and investment considerations.
  • Challenge unclear scope and identify delivery, cost and commercial risks early in the sales cycle.
  • Work closely with delivery teams to validate assumptions before commitments are made.

Growth & Go-to-Market

  • Contribute to the evolution of HSO's Data & AI propositions and repeatable offerings.
  • Develop demonstrations, accelerators, sales collateral and industry-specific solution narratives.
  • Support RFPs, bid responses, executive presentations and proof-of-concept engagements.
  • Collaborate with Microsoft stakeholders to drive pipeline growth and co-sell opportunities.
  • Keep up to date with emerging Microsoft technologies and industry trends across Data & AI.

What We're Looking For

The ideal candidate combines strong technical capability with exceptional commercial awareness.

You'll be equally comfortable discussing board-level business outcomes with executive stakeholders as you are diving into architecture decisions with technical teams.

Commercial & Consulting Experience

You'll have:

  • Proven experience in a Solution Architecture, Pre-Sales, Consulting or Technical Advisory role.
  • Experience working within a Microsoft partner, consultancy or enterprise technology environment.
  • Strong commercial acumen and experience creating proposals, business cases and Statements of Work.
  • The ability to qualify opportunities and challenge assumptions constructively.
  • Excellent workshop facilitation, discovery and stakeholder management skills.
  • Experience presenting to senior business and technical audiences.
  • The ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear business value.
  • Understanding of opportunity qualification methodologies such as MEDDIC or MEDDICC.

Experience across industries such as manufacturing, retail, financial services, healthcare, public sector, not-for-profit, utilities or professional services would be advantageous.

Technical Experience

We recognise that few candidates will have expertise across every area listed below. We're primarily looking for strong Data & AI architecture experience across the Microsoft ecosystem.

Essential

Data & Analytics

  • Microsoft Fabric
  • Lakehouse architecture patterns
  • Power BI and self-service analytics
  • Semantic modelling and reporting solutions
  • Data platform modernisation and analytics strategy

Azure Data Platform

  • Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS)
  • Azure Synapse Analytics
  • Azure Databricks
  • Azure SQL Database
  • Azure Cosmos DB
  • Azure Data Factory

AI & Automation

  • Azure AI Services
  • Azure OpenAI Service
  • Azure AI Foundry
  • Copilot Studio
  • Agentic AI patterns and intelligent automation solutions
  • Document intelligence and AI-driven business use cases

Data Engineering & Platform Delivery

  • SQL
  • Python and/or PySpark
  • Data pipelines and transformation frameworks
  • CI/CD concepts and deployment automation
  • Azure DevOps and/or GitHub
  • Infrastructure as Code…

Forward Deployed Engineer

About HSO

HSO is a global Business Transformation Partner with deep industry expertise and a long standing strategic relationship with Microsoft. We help organisations unlock the full potential of Microsoft Dynamics 365, Azure, Data and AI technologies to modernise operations, accelerate innovation and deliver meaningful business outcomes.

In 2026, HSO achieved Microsoft Frontier Partner status, recognising our advanced capabilities across Microsoft Cloud and AI and our ability to help customers move beyond AI experimentation into secure, governed, enterprise scale production.

With operations across Europe, North America and Asia, we combine industry knowledge, technical excellence and a practical, people first approach to transformation.

As we continue to expand our AI capabilities, we’re building a new generation of customer facing engineering talent to help organisations turn the potential of AI and agentic technologies into real, measurable value.

About the Role

HSO is building a new generation of customer facing engineers who will help our customers create the operating model of the future using the latest AI, data and cloud capabilities.

Forward Deployed Engineers combine consulting judgement, production software engineering, data platform expertise, AI delivery capability and business transformation skills.

You will embed with strategic customers, understand their most important business challenges and rapidly turn those challenges into working, production ready AI applications, agentic workflows, automation solutions and data driven platforms.

This is a hands on, outcome led role embedded within customer environments. You’ll move quickly from discovery to working software and take accountability for delivering measurable business outcomes.

You’ll work across business processes, data platforms, integrations, AI, cloud and security, designing solutions that make effective use of Microsoft technologies while integrating with the customer’s wider technology estate.

A strong understanding of modern enterprise data platforms is fundamental to the role. You will need to understand how data is structured, governed, integrated, transformed and made available to AI and application workloads, and how data platform decisions affect the quality, scalability and reliability of the solutions you build.

Forward Deployed Engineers work closely with Deployment Strategists. The Deployment Strategist focuses on identifying where AI can create the greatest customer value and defining the desired outcome. The FDE takes ownership of how that outcome is delivered technically.

From discovery through to go live, both roles work side by side. The FDE owns the technical solution and delivery, while the Deployment Strategist ensures the solution remains aligned to the business problem and measurable value.

The role does not end at first deployment. You’ll stay close to solutions through hardening, adoption and handover before moving on to the next value opportunity. You’ll also turn what you learn into reusable HSO assets, reference architectures and delivery patterns that help future engagements move faster.

What You’ll Do

Own Customer Outcomes

• Embed rapidly within customer teams and develop a strong understanding of their priorities, operating processes, systems, data and constraints.

• Translate ambiguous business problems and defined customer outcomes into clear technical delivery plans.

• Act as the technical lead throughout an engagement, guiding customer sponsors, business users, technical teams and HSO colleagues towards successful delivery.

• Build trusted relationships with senior operational and technical stakeholders, including CTO and CIO level leaders.

• Take ownership for delivering solutions that create measurable customer value rather than simply completing technical tasks.

Lead Discovery and Solution Design

• Lead technical discovery workshops to understand customer challenges and identify high value AI, data and automation opportunities.

• Assess business processes, data readiness, data architecture, integration points, security requirements, technical risks and operational constraints.

• Understand the customer’s existing data platform landscape and identify how data needs to be accessed, transformed, governed or modernised to support the required solution.

• Apply a problem first approach to identify the smallest valuable solution that can be built and proven quickly.

• Design end to end solution architectures that balance speed, scalability, maintainability, security and responsible AI.

• Turn discovery into a pragmatic roadmap from prototype through to production.

Build and Ship Production Solutions

• Design, build, integrate, test and deploy enterprise grade solutions using modern cloud, data and AI technologies.

• Develop AI powered applications, copilots, agents, automations, integrations and workflow solutions.

• Build solutions that make effective use of modern enterprise data platforms and ensure AI applications are supported by reliable, governed and accessible data.

• Integrate solutions with platforms such as Microsoft Fabric, Azure Data Services, Dynamics 365, Power Platform, Salesforce, SAP, ServiceNow and customer owned systems, APIs and data platforms.

• Apply modern engineering practices including source control, CI/CD, automated testing, infrastructure as code, observability and secure development.

• Work iteratively. Deliver value quickly, learn from real world usage and progressively harden solutions for enterprise production.

Engineer AI and Agentic Solutions

• Design and implement robust agentic workflows, human in the loop processes and, where appropriate, multi agent architectures.

• Apply modern techniques across retrieval, grounding, orchestration, tool integration, context engineering and evaluation.

• Build evaluation frameworks and guardrails to test AI behaviour, reliability and quality before and after deployment.

• Implement appropriate responsible AI, security, monitoring and governance controls.

• Ensure data quality, lineage, governance and availability are considered as fundamental components of AI solution design.

• Use operational data and user feedback to continuously improve solution quality and performance.

Create Reusable HSO Capability

• Reuse existing HSO assets, accelerators and delivery patterns wherever they improve speed and quality.

• Turn lessons from customer engagements into reusable assets, reference architectures, engineering patterns and playbooks.

• Contribute actively to HSO’s AI, Data, Frontier and Horizon…

About HSO 

HSO is a Microsoft focused, business transformation partner, with deep industry expertise and global reach. We leverage the full power of the Microsoft Cloud to transform the way in which people work and engage customers, accelerating the impact of cloud transformation and improving overall business performance. By leveraging the power of Dynamics 365, Generative AI, Data, AI, Copilot capabilities and the Microsoft Cloud, HSO helps companies innovate faster, by modernizing business operations, adopting data-driven intelligent automation, delivering real-time insights and connecting the enterprise.  

Founded in 1987, HSO has more than 2,500 professionals throughout EMEA, the Americas and Asia and is one of the world’s top business solution and implementation partners. We are a member of Microsoft’s elite Inner Circle, representing the Top 1% of partners worldwide. HSO UK has grown to more than 300 people and we expect over 100% organic growth in the next 5 years. 

HSO specializes in industry sectors such as Retail, Manufacturing, Professional Services, Financial Services and Public Sector. HSO has been recognized as the global winner of the 2023 Partner of the Year Award for D365 Finance and as a Finalist for D365 Sales and Marketing. In addition, we have been awarded ‘Best Tech Company 2021 to Work For’ and the ‘6th Best Large Company to Work For’ in 2022.   

At HSO we take pride in being large enough to serve, but small enough to care. Both for our customers and colleagues. We are uniquely positioned to empower you to transform your career, without compromising your life goals and we take pride in investing as much in our people as we do in our clients. Our culture and values support entrepreneurial mindsets and attitudes, where your voice will always be heard. 

 

Why Work for HSO? 

Joining the HSO team means being an integral part of a dynamic organization that values innovation, collaboration and professional growth. Here are some of the reasons why HSO is a great place to work and build your career: 

  • Customer Value: Work for market-leading clients across multiple industries, delivering value-adding solutions and a meaningful difference. 
  • Supportive Culture: Enjoy an environment where everyone is encouraged to be heard in a positive and inclusive environment.

MOO's engineering teams span the physical and digital worlds. Every order we take is manufactured after it is paid for, so the journey from "buy" to "delivered" runs through a factory as well as a database. That is true of the storefront, our design and customisation tools, cart, checkout and payments, business accounts, and equally true of order orchestration, manufacturing, fulfilment, shipping and the tooling our Customer Service and Operations teams use. The problems worth solving here run the length of that journey, and the hardest ones are usually the ones that cross it.
As we scale, we're bringing together two ecommerce platforms while also experimenting with our customers' browsing experiences to support growth. On the other side of the order, we're consolidating tooling for Customer Service and Operations, improving data visibility across the order journey, integrating new carriers, and increasing manufacturing capacity while protecting customer experience and margin. We're also changing how we build, with AI-assisted development now part of everyday engineering practice here.
You'll partner closely with engineering teams across our entire ecosystem, product leadership, and our Platform group, to deliver a coherent, scalable architecture and unblock cross-team delivery.
Bring deep technical leadership across MOO's ecommerce ecosystem, from storefront and checkout through to delivered. You'll support in setting the architectural direction for that journey and enable multiple teams to move quickly and efficiently.
Balance essential scaling of today's systems with an iterative migration away from legacy components. Define contracts, events and guardrails that make our ecosystem observable, resilient and cost-efficient. Set the standard for how we use AI-assisted development, so we get the speed without lowering the quality bar. Translate operational requirements from Operations and Customer Service, and commercial requirements from Product and Trading, into pragmatic platform improvements.
You'll work with our engineering team, who are largely based in the UK, and with stakeholders at our manufacturing facilities in East Providence, Rhode Island and Dagenham, London.

The Role
As an Account Executive, you’ll join our Sales team and run full-cycle sales across your territory in EMEA. You’ll become an expert in compensation, identify market trends, and share insights that help shape our product and marketing strategy—including how we bring an agentic layer to our compensation data and insights.
We believe in value-based selling, so this role will suit someone consultative who can manage multiple opportunities in a high-velocity small- and mid-market environment.
This is your chance to help build a category-defining company at an exciting point in its evolution. You’ll develop new relationships with HR and Reward leaders and establish Ravio as the go-to compensation insights platform in your territory. As we add an agentic layer to our data and insights, you’ll help customers understand what this new generation of compensation technology can unlock.
Compensation hasn’t been reinvented in decades—HR buyers often tell us their current benchmarking providers “still look like Windows 96”—so you’ll help define what modern looks like and solve meaningful challenges for customers.
We also invest in mentoring and genuine career progression, whether you want to deepen your expertise as an individual contributor, move into leadership, or explore other parts of the business as Ravio scales.
What we’re looking for
- Research, identify, and approach prospective customers in your territory.
- Own the entire sales lifecycle, from outreach and demos through legal review, negotiation, and close.
- Manage a high volume of opportunities in parallel while building strong customer relationships.
- Collaborate closely with Customer Success to ensure a smooth handover for newly onboarded customers and support their ongoing success with Ravio.
- Develop a deep understanding of the compensation challenges facing tech companies and how Ravio can help solve them.
- Build fluency in Ravio’s evolving compensation insights and AI and agentic capabilities, clearly communicate their value to customers, and bring market feedback into how the proposition develops.
- Share market insights and work closely with our Commercial and Product teams to refine our product suite and commercial strategy.
You’ll be a good fit for this role if you have:
- 3+ years of experience in a full-cycle B2B SaaS sales role, working alongside wider commercial functions and independently driving success in your region. Experience selling to HR or Reward buyers is a plus.
- Exceptional emotional intelligence and communication skills, with the ability to engage stakeholders at every level and build trust and excitement with prospects.
- An entrepreneurial mindset and bias for action. You thrive in a fast-paced environment and embrace constant change.
- Familiarity with the Account Executive tech stack, such as HubSpot, Claude, Cognism, and LinkedIn Sales Navigator, is a plus.
- Curiosity about AI and agentic technology, with the openness and learning agility to understand emerging capabilities and translate them into clear customer value. Prior AI sales experience is welcome but not required.
- Fluency in Spanish or Swedish is ideal, but not essential.
If you don’t meet every requirement, we’d still love to hear from you if you believe you have what it takes and can demonstrate it through your previous work.
Sales at Ravio in 2026
This is an opportunity to play an important part in Ravio’s next phase of growth. We’ve already established strong product-market fit, and you’ll build on that success by growing a designated geographic territory across revenue, dataset growth—that is, compensation insights—and brand awareness.
One of our core values is “nothing’s someone else’s problem.”
You’ll work directly with the Sales Manager, Marketing, and Customer Success to shape and expand your territory. At the same time, you’ll have a high level of autonomy and ownership. We’ll look to you to bring your own innovative perspective and share insights into what will make your territory successful.
If you want to make an outsized impact at a company poised for further growth, work alongside a smart team, and embrace change, this could be the role for you.
Compensation & Benefits
- Base £52,530 - £71,070 OTE £75,000–£101,520 - 70/30 split.
- Company ownership—everyone receives a meaningful equity stake in Ravio.
- 37 days of paid time off: 25 days of holiday, 4 wellness days, and 8 public holidays.
- Up to 6% pension matching.
- £60 monthly wellness allowance to invest in your physical wellbeing.
- £500 annual learning and development budget.
- Private healthcare cover with AXA.
- Personal travel insurance.
- 6 weeks work from anywhere per year
- Income protection insurance if you’re unable to work because of sickness or disability.
- 16 weeks of fully paid birthing-parent leave, followed by 4 weeks at 50% pay, and 8 weeks of leave for non-birthing parents.

CUSTOMER SUCCESS MANAGER, SMB
We help companies get compensation right.
What we get paid at work has a massive impact on our lives, and it’s one of the biggest factors in hiring and retaining talent - and yet so many companies struggle to get it right. They simply have no choice but to rely on poor data and unsophisticated tools for their pay decisions. That’s why we created Ravio.
We help many of the world’s most innovative and ambitious companies build stronger teams and reach their goals through better compensation. Our real-time data platform brings compensation into the modern age with clarity and transparency. We’re passionate about ensuring everyone is paid what they deserve, no matter their background or circumstances. We believe that when compensation is done right, everyone wins.
Ravio is growing fast, which means you can too. We’ve established ourselves as the European leader in our space serving more than 1,200 clients, and now have our sights set on becoming the global go to place for compensation data and tools for managing compensation.
Joining a startup and scaling it into a global product is one of the most challenging and rewarding experiences a career can offer. If that sounds exciting to you, you’re in the right place.
The Role
You’ll be joining a team of Customer Success Managers, supporting Ravio’s customers across their full lifecycle. This is a role which encompasses implementation, value delivery, ongoing relationship building, as well as renewals and upselling.
You’ll own a scale portfolio of 300+ SMB accounts, responsible for improving and maintaining account health and retaining and growing revenue across your book, using a hybrid of tech-touch and high-touch engagement.
You’ll work closely with other teams across the business to share feedback from customers, and to influence the product roadmap based on what customers are telling us they need.
What we’re looking for:
- Managing a scale portfolio. You’ll be responsible for a large and growing portfolio of SMB customers, using tech-touch tools (automation, segmentation, one-to-many outreach) alongside a hands-on approach for the accounts that need it, so you can prioritise your time where it has the most impact.
- Customer relationship building / empathy. You can build rapport fast, and gain customer’s trust, while understanding and empathising with their challenges.

Our real-time data platform brings compensation into the modern age, tracking the market across all compensation types from salary to equity and benefits. Ravio is growing fast, which means you can too. We’ve established ourselves as the European leader in our space serving more than 1,200 clients, and now have our sights set on becoming the global go to place for compensation data and tools for managing compensation.

jobs.ashbyhq.com/slingshotai/994b40ca-31.description_excerpt:
Slingshot AI
Slingshot AI is the team behind Ash, the first AI designed for mental health. Our mission is to make support more accessible and help people change their lives in the ways they want.
We’re building a world-class team by empowering individuals with the autonomy, flexibility, and support they need to do their best work. We dream big, iterate fast, and care deeply. If that sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you.
Our team spans machine learning, product, engineering, conversational design, clinical, growth, and operations, with offices in both New York City and London.
We're a well-funded Series A company, having raised $93M from Andreessen Horowitz, Radical Ventures, Forerunner Ventures, plus top-tier tech investors involved in ElevenLabs, Captions, Shopify, Plaid, Notion, Canva, Twitch, Airtable, and many others.
The role
We are seeking a Creative Strategy Lead to join the Slingshot AI marketing team. Reporting to our head of growth, your job is to identify, create, test, and scale our D2C creative motion. Millions of people already use general purpose AI as a therapist, and millions more are on a waitlist or priced out of care. Demand is not our problem. Getting Ash in front of the people who need it is. Creative is the biggest lever we have on that, and this role owns it.
This is a hands-on role by design. You own the loop, coming up with creative copy, producing visuals and tag-lines, and iterating quickly to dial in on what works. You are building the engine that gets Ash in front of people. You create and test fast, trust your instincts, and want to develop the playbook that puts proper mental healthcare at the world's fingertips.
Key responsibilities:
- Own the weekly experiment loop: hypothesis, A/B test, read the result, identify winners, iterate. This is the spine of the role and where taste shows up.
- Build the system that makes it repeatable. Testing cadence, angle library, naming and tagging, and a bank of real user language pulled from communities, reviews, and our own conversations.
- Create winning concepts and then raise the hit rate of winning concepts so paid has more to scale behind. The bar is quality, not volume, and you manage what we spend proving things out.
- Write the hooks, headlines, overlays, and scripts, in the voice of the person scrolling.
- Brief at volume: one brief that many creators each interpret their own way, built for what each network rewards rather than resizing one idea for all of them.
- Coach creators with sharp feedback, one to many. You brief and evaluate and if required can do creator ops, supporting in producing the content yourself.
- Work with media buying on a weekly cadence. You read media buy KPIs and go into the buying tools yourself to check how tests performed, and you know buying well enough to challenge the buyer on their own ground.
- Develop the product and audience understanding that decides what works. When AI makes output cheap, this becomes the deciding factor in paid.
- Set the visual and verbal point of view for Ash in market. We do not look like the rest of this category, and we do not intend to start.
About you:
- You produce assets yourself on the AI stack, Figma, CapCut and the rest. Not in front of the camera, but you make the creative for testing, not just brief it.
- You come from the paid side moving into creative, or creative moving toward paid. Both work. What matters is turning product and audience understanding into creative that wins.
- Experienced in writing performance copy; have taste and can quickly iterate
- Consumer only, ideally subscription. If your background is SaaS, this is not the role.
- You can set up a clean test, say in advance what would prove you wrong, read the result honestly, and defend your taste with an argument rather than a mood board.
- You want to work on mental health for a reason you can say out loud.
Nice to have:
- You can challenge our media buyer on their own ground, because you have done the buying yourself.
- You have built or reshaped web funnels and landing pages to match the creative that drove the click.
- You have built or run a creator or UGC pipeline, including sourcing, briefing, and quality control.

jobs.ashbyhq.com/slingshotai/657d1a1d-4b.description_excerpt:
Slingshot AI
Slingshot AI is the team behind Ash, the first AI designed for mental health. Our mission is to make support more accessible and help people change their lives in the ways they want.
We’re building a world-class team by empowering individuals with the autonomy, flexibility, and support they need to do their best work. We dream big, iterate fast, and care deeply. If that sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you.
